sourceDefinition: see 2, in nine places. [The first of the meanings there assigned to this verb is, in my opinion, more than doubtful. In all its senses, it seems to be properly trans.: when it is used as an intrans. verb, an objective complement is app. understood. Thus,] A^asolama is syn. with A^asolafa [as meaning He paid in advance, or beforehand ]; (S, M, Mgh, Msb;) Alv~amana [ the price ] being suppressed, though sometimes it is expressed; (Mgh;) as also ↓ sl~m ; (M;) and ↓ tsl~m , as occurring in a trad., where it is said, mano tasal~ama fiY $aYo'K falaA yaSorifuhu A_ilaY gayorihi [ Whoso pays in advance for a thing, he shall not turn it over, or transfer it, to another than him ]; but Kt says that he had not heard this verb thus used except in this instance. (TA.) So the first of these verbs signifies in the saying, Aslm fiY AlT~aEaAmi (S) or fY Albur~i (Mgh) [ He paid in advance for the wheat ], and fY Al$~aYo'i [ for the thing ], as also ↓ sl~m . (M.) And hence the saying, A_i*aA A^asolama SuwfFA fiY libodK A^awo $aEarFA fiY misoHK lamo yajuzo [ If he give in advance wool for felt, or goats' hair for a garment, or piece, of haircloth, it will not be allowable ]. (Mgh.) And so in the phrase, A^asolamotu A_ilayohi [ I paid in advance to him ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- Also [ He resigned, or submitted, himself; nafosahu being understood: or] he was, or became, resigned, or submissive; (M, K;) and so ↓ Astslm : (S, M, Msb, K:) you say, Aslm lil~`hi [ He resigned, or submitted, himself, or he was, or became, resigned, or submissive, to God: see also an ex. (before referred to) in the last sentence of the second paragraph: or he was, or became, sincere in his religion, or without hypocrisy, towards God: see musolimN ]: (Msb:) [or] Aslm signifies he entered into Als~ilom , (S, Msb,) which here means AlAisotisolaAm [i. e. the state of resignation, or submission ]. (S.) ― -b3- And He became a Muslim; as also ↓ tsl~m ; (M, * K;) as in the saying, kaAna kaAfirFA vum~a tasal~ama , i. e. A^asolama [ He was an unbeliever, or a denier of the unity of God, &c.; then he became a Muslim ]: (M:) or he entered [ the pale, or communion, of ] the religion of AlA_isolaAm . (S, * Msb.) AlA_isolaAmu as a principle of the law of God is The manifesting of humility or submission, and outward conforming with the law of God, and the taking upon oneself to do or to say as the Prophet has done or said: for this, the blood is to be spared, and one may demand the repelling of evil: (T, * M:) and if there is therewith firm belief with the heart, it is A_iymaAnN : (T:) this is the doctrine of Esh-Sháfi'ee; but the doctrine of Aboo-Haneefeh makes no difference between these two terms: (KT:) [agreeably with the former doctrine,] Th well and briefly says, AlAslAm is with the tongue, and AlAymAn is with the heart: and he says, in explaining verse 48 of ch. v. of the Kur, that every prophet has been sent with AlAslAm , though the ordinances differ. (M.) ― -b4- One says also, A^asolamotu Eanohu , meaning I left it [app. an affair, as in an explanation in the TK,] after I had been [ engaged ] in it. (Ibn-Buzurj, K.) And Aslm occurs intransitively in the saying, kaAna raAEiYa ganamK vum~a A^asolama , meaning [ He was a pastor of sheep, or goats; then ] he left them. (M.) ― -b5- [Freytag assigns to Aslm another signification “ Adscendere fecit (vid. a sul~am ), ” as from the Ham, p. 39: but this is app. a mistake, into which he has been led by a saying, there cited, of Zuheyr, which I read thus: hawiY~a Ald~alowi A^asolamahaA Alr~i$aA='u (meaning, The descent, or as the descent, of the bucket that the well-rope has let go ): and by its being there said that “ you should not prefer any reading of hwY to that with damm, though it has been said otherwise: ” whereas the correct reading is, in my opinion, hawiY~ , agreeably with what here follows:] Er-Riyáshee says, on the authority of AZ, that AlhawiY~u , with fet-h, is downwards; and with damm, upwards; and he cites the saying above as an ex. of the word as meaning downwards. (TA in art. hwY .)

I saw the Apostle of God ( may God bless and save him ) circuiting around the Kaabeh, upon his camel, touching the Black Stone with his hooked staff, and kissing the hooked staff ]. (TA.) The primary signification of AlAisotilaAmu is [said to be] The wiping, or stroking, the salimap , i. e. the stone: afterwards it was used in relation to other things, and one said Aisotalamotu yadahaA , meaning I stroked, or kissed, her hand. (Har pp. 30 and 31.) ― -b2- Astlm Alxuf~u qadamayohi means The boot rendered his feet soft [after he had been accustomed to walking barefoot]. (TA.)

definition: Peace, or reconciliation;
sourceDefinition: Peace, or reconciliation; as also ↓ salomN ; (S, M, Msb, K;) masc. and fem.; (S, Msb, K; *) and ↓ salamN and ↓ salaAmN are like silomN [in signification]: (M: [the context there shows that the signification mentioned above is what is meant in this instance:]) or silomN signifies the making peace, or becoming at peace or reconciled, with another or others; (Ham p. 80;) as also ↓ salomN ; and both are sometimes fem. as being syn. with muSaAlaHapN . (L voce janaHa , q. v.) In the saying of El-Aashà, A^a*aAqatohumu AlHarobu A^anofaAsahaA ↓ waqado tukorahu AlHarobu baEoda Als~ilimo [ War made them, or has made them, to taste its draughts, and verily war is disliked after peace ], he has transferred the vowel of the m to the l , in pausing; or it may be that he has inserted a kesreh in imitation of the preceding kesreh: it is not an instance like A_ibil , in the opinion of Sb; for in his opinion the latter is the only instance of its kind. (M.) It is said in a trad., respecting El-Hodeybiyeh, A^axa*a vamaAniyna mino A^aholi mak~apa silomFA , or ↓ salomFA , or ↓ salamFA , accord. to different relations, meaning [ He took forty of the people of Mekkeh ] peaceably: thus expl. by El-Homeydee, in his “ Ghareeb. ” (TA. [See also salamN below.]) ― -b2- Also i. q. ↓ salaAmN , (S, K, TA,) as signifying Selfresignation, or submission; (TA; [and thus the latter is expl. in one place in the S;]) which is also a signification of ↓ salamN : (S, M, K, TA:) and this is meant in the Kur [iv. 96], where it is said, lasota muw^ominFA ↓ walaA taquwluwA limano A^aloqaY A_ilayokumu A@ls~alaAma , (Bd, TA,) or ↓ Als~alama , as some read, (Bd,) [i. e. And say not ye to him who offers to you submission, Thou art not a believer: ] or ↓ Als~alaAma here means the salutation of AlA_isolaAm [ by saying salaAmN Ealayokumo ]: (Bd, TA: *) or salutation, and submission by uttering the profession of AlA_isolaAm ; and so ↓ Als~alama : (Jel:) [or the latter here means, simply, salutation; and this is app. what is meant by its being said that] Als~alamu is the subst. from Alt~asoliymu ; (K;) [but accord. to SM,] this means the unreserved approval of what is decreed; and this is said to be meant by the reading Als~alama mentioned above. (TA.) ― -b3- And [hence] Als~ilomu signifies also AlA_isolaAmu [as meaning The religion of the Muslims; because it is a religion of self-resignation, or submission]: (S, K:) this is meant in the Kur [ii. 204], where it is said, AudoxuluwA fiY Als~ilomi kaAf~apF [ Enter ye into the religion of El-Islám wholly ]; (S, Bd, Jel;) and so ↓ Als~alomi , as some there read; (Bd, Jel;) or both there mean submission and obedience to God: (Bd:) [and] ↓ Als~alamu [also] has the former meaning. (M.) -A2- Also, (S, M, K,) and ↓ salomN , (M,) A man, (S, K, TA,) [and] a woman, (M,) who makes peace, or is at peace, with another; (S, M, K;) and in like manner, a company of men ( qawomN ). (M.) This is said to be meant in the Kur [xxxix. 30], where it is said, warajolFA silomFA lirajulK , as some read, i. e. And a man who is at peace with respect to a man: (TA:) or silomFA and ↓ salomFA and ↓ salamFA , three different readings, in the place of [the more common reading] saAlimFA , are all inf. ns. of salima , used as epithets [syn. with saAlimFA ], or *aA is suppressed before them. (Bd.) You say, A^anaA silomN limano saAlamaniY [ I am one who is at peace with respect to him who is at peace with me ]. (S, TA.) And a poet says, [using this word in two different senses, the latter of which has been mentioned above,] liA^aholiki faA@qobaliY silomiY A^anaAy^ilu A_in~aniY silomN [ O Náïleh, ( naAy^ilu being for naAy^ilapN , a woman's name, apocopated,) verily I am one who is at peace with respect to thy family, therefore accept thou my submission ]. (TA. [It seems to be there indicated by the context that slmY here means my peace, or reconciliation; which is less appropriate than the meaning that I have assigned to it.])

definition: ― -b2- Also, in buying or selling, (Msb,) the subst.
sourceDefinition: : see salaAmN : and see also silomN , in seven places. ― -b2- Also, in buying or selling, (Msb,) the subst. from A^asolama fiY Al$~aYo'i and sal~ama signifying A^asolafa , (M,) i. q. salafN ; (S, Msb, K;) i. e. Any money, or property, paid in advance, or beforehand, as the price of a commodity for which the seller has become responsible and which one has bought on description: (T and TA in art. slf :) or payment for a commodity to be delivered at a certain [ future ] period with something additional to [ the equivalent of ] the current price at the time of such payment; this [transaction] being a cause of profit to him who makes such payment: (TA in that art.:) or a sort of sale in which the price is paid in advance, and the commodity is withheld, on the condition of description, to a certain [ future ] period: (S and O in that art., in explanation of salafN :) but it is said in a trad. that the term salamN as meaning salafN was disliked; app. because the former is applied to obedience, and self-resignation, or submission, to God. (TA.) -A2- And The making [one] captive. (K. [See 1, in the latter part of the paragraph.]) -A3- And A captive; (K;) because he submits himself. (TA.) One says, A^axa*ahu salamFA , (M, TA, [in the TK biAls~alami ,]) He took him [ a captive ], (TA,) or made him captive, (M,) without war: (M, TA:) or he brought him in a state of submission, not resisting; and so, if wounded: (IAar, M, TA:) and thus El-Khattábee has expl. the phrase in the trad. respecting El-Hodeybiyeh cited above, voce silomN . (TA.) -A4- Also A sort of tree, (S, M, Msb, K,) [the mimosa flava of Forskål, who writes its Arabic name in Italic characters syllæm, and in Arabic characters slym , (Flora Aegypt. Arab., p. cxxiii.,)] a species (M) of the [ kind of thorny trees called ] EiDaAh , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, TA, [not gaDaAp , as in the Lexicons of Golius and Freytag,]) the leaves whereof are the qaraZ , with which skin is tanned: (TA:) AHn says, its branches are long, like rods; and it has no wood such as is used in carpentry, even if it grows large: it has slender, long thorns, grievous when they wound the foot of a man; and a yellow [ fruit such as is termed ] baramap [n. un. of baramN , see this word, and see also HubolapN ,] which is the sweetest of the baram in odour; and they tan with its leaves: and it is said, on the authority of the Arabs of the desert, that it has a yellow flower, containing a green grain ( Hab~ap xaDoraA=' [or this may mean a grain of a dark, or an ashy, dustcolour ]), of sweet odour, in which is somewhat of bitterness, and of which the gazelles are very fond: (M:) the n. un. is with p : (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K:) and pl. A^asolaAmN , (M,) and silaAmN is said by IB to be pl. of the n. un., like as A_ikaAmN is of A^akamapN . (TA.) [Hence,] *aAtu A^asolaAmK A land ( A^aroD ) that gives growth to the [ trees called ] salam . (K.) See also slamaAn .

sourceDefinition: , (S, K, TA,) in its primary acceptation, (TA,) is syn. with ↓ salaAmapN , (S, K, TA,) as is also ↓ salamN , (S, [so in one of my copies, but omitted in the other copy,]) and signifies Safety, security, immunity, or freedom, from faults, defects, imperfections, blemishes, or vices, (S, * [mentioned in one only of my two copies, and there as relating peculiarly to the third word,] K, [in which it ostensibly relates peculiarly to the first word, but in the CK, by the omission of a w before it, it is made to relate only to the second word,] and TA, [accord. to which it relates to the first and second words, as it is well known to do,]) and from evils of any kind: (TA:) or [simply] safety, security, immunity, or freedom; as also ↓ salaAmapN : (Sb, M:) IKt says that these two words may be dial. vars. [syn. each with the other]; or the former may be pl. of the latter [or rather a coll. gen. n. of which the latter is the n. un.]: (M, TA:) and Suh says, in the R, that most of the lexicologists hold them to have one [and the same] meaning: but that if they considered the language of the Arabs, and the distinction, or limitation, denoted by the p , they would see that between them is a great difference [inasmuch as the former has a large range of meaning which the latter has not, as will be seen from what follows]. (TA.) salaAmN Ealayokumo is an announcement of the continuance of salaAmap [or safety, &c.]: (Bd in xiii. 24:) [it may therefore be rendered Safety, &c., be, or light and abide, on you; or, generally, peace be, or light and abide, on you; for] it means nothing disliked, or evil, shall befall you henceforth: (Bd in xvi. 34:) and salaAmN Ealayoka [may be rendered in like manner; for it virtually] means I will not do to thee anything that is disliked, or evil; (Bd and Jel in xix. 48;) nor say to thee henceforward what would annoy thee, or be disagreeable, or evil, to thee. (Bd ibid.) It may also be [rendered May safety, &c., or peace, be, or light and abide, on you; as] a prayer for salaAmap , to those to whom it is addressed, from the state in which they are at the time. (Bd in xxviii. 55.) [It is generally held that this salutation may not be used by, nor to, any but a Muslim.] In the beginning of an epistle, the approved practice is to write salaAmN Ealayoka , without the article Al ; and in repeating it, at the end, to write it with that article. (Durrat el-Ghowwás, in De Sacy's Anthol. Gramm. Arabe, p. 72 of the Arabic text. [In the latter case, the general practice in the present day is to write simply waAls~alaAm , suppressing Ealayoka .]) In saluting the dead, one puts Ealayoka first, saying, Ealayoka salaAmu A@ll~`hi . (Ham p. 367.) You also say, maA kaAna ka*aA waka*aA ↓ laA bisalaAmatika [ No, by thy safety, such and such things were not ]. (S.) Als~ulaAmu is also a name of God, (S, M, Msb, K,) [applied to Him in the Kur lix. 23, accord. to some for *uw Als~alaAmi , i. e. *uw Als~alaAmapi ,] because of his safety, or freedom, from defect, and imperfection, and cessation of existence; (IKt, M, TA;) or from variations, and as being the everlasting, who brings the creation to nought and will not come to nought; or, accord. to Suh in the R, He is so named [as being the Author of Safety, Security, &c.; i. e.] because He has rendered all his creatures safe, or free, from defectiveness, or unsoundness, and mankind and the jinn, or genii, from the betiding of injustice, or wrong, to them, from Him; and the expositors who assert that He is thus named because of his safety, or freedom, from imperfections, and evils of any kind, utter an unseemly saying, making salaAmN to be syn. with ↓ saAlimN , which latter applies only to him who is liable to evil of any kind, and who expects it, and then becomes safe, or free, from it. (TA.) daAru Als~alaAmi is an appellation of Paradise, (M, K,) [applied thereto in the Kur vi. 127 and x. 26,] as being the abode of everlasting safety, or security; (Zj, M, TA;) the abode of safety, or security, from evils of any kind, from death and decrepitude and diseases [ &c. ]: (TA:) or as being the abode of God. (M, TA.) ― -b2- See also silomN , in four places. ― -b3- [As is there stated,] it signifies also Salutation, or greeting; (M, TA;) particularly the salutation of AlA_isolaAm [ by saying salaAmN Ealayoka or salaAmN Ealayokumo , expl. above]; (Bd in iv. 96;) a subst. (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) from sal~ama Ealayohi , (Msb,) [i. e.] from Alt~usoliymu , (S, Mgh, TA,) like kalaAmN from Alt~akoliymu . (Mgh. [See 2, third sentence.]) ― -b4- In the saying in the Kur [xxv. 64], waA_i*aA xaATabahumu A@lojaAhiluwna qaAluwA salaAmFA [ And when the ignorant speak to them, they say, salaAmFA ], this last word signifies tasal~umFA , (Sb, M,) or tasal~umFA minokumo [for natasal~amu minokumo tasal~umFA We declare ourselves to be clear, or quit, of you ], and mutaArakahF lalumo [for nutaArikukumo mutaArakapF we relinquish you ], (Bd,) [and means] there shall be neither good nor evil between us (Sb, M, Bd) and you: it is not the slAm that is used in salutation; for the verse was revealed at Mekkeh, and the Muslims had not then been commanded to salute the believers in a plurality of gods: (Sb, M:) [in iv. 88 of the Kur, which was promulgated afterwards, at ElMedeeneh, is a general command to return a salutation with a better or with the same; but the Sunneh prescribes that the salutation of salaAmN Ealayoka or salaAmN Ealayokumo when addressed to a Muslim by one not a Muslim is to be returned only by saying waEalayoka or waEalayokumo :] or the meaning in xxv. 64 is, they say a right saying, in which they are secure from harming and sinning. (Bd.) Sb asserts that Aboo-Rabee'ah used to say, A_i*aA laqiyta fulaAnFA faqulo salaAmFA , meaning tasal~umFA [for A^atasal~amu minoka tasal~umFA , i. e. When thou meetest such a one, say, I declare myself to be clear, or quit, of thee ]: and he says that some of them said salaAmN , meaning The case of me and thee is the [ case of ] being clear, or quit, each of the other; and the [ case of ] mutual relinquishing. (M.) [It is usual, in the present day, to say, AifoEalo ka*aA waAls~alaAm , meaning Do thou such a thing, and there will be an end of altercation between us.] -A2- See also saliymN . -A3- Also A kind of trees; (S, M, Msb, K;) they assert that they are evergreen; nothing eats them; but the gazelles keep to them, and protect themselves by their shade, but do not hide among them; and they are not great trees, nor of the kind called EiDaAh : (AHn, M:) they are also called ↓ silaAmN ; (K;) or this is pl. of salamapN [n. un. of salamN ], which is of another kind; like as A_ikaAmN is pl. of A^akamapN : (IB, TA:) n. un. with p . (S, M.) Als~alaAmu Ealayoka was said to an Arab of the desert; and he replied, AljavojaAvu Ealayoka : and being asked, “ What is this reply? ” he answered, “ They are two bitter trees: thou hast put upon me one, so I have put upon thee the other. ” (K.) -A4- See also salimN , in two places.

It may also be [rendered May safety, &c., or peace, be, or light and abide, on you; as] a prayer for salaAmap , to those to whom it is addressed, from the state in which they are at the time. (Bd in xxviii. 55.) [It is generally held that this salutation may not be used by, nor to, any but a Muslim.] In the beginning of an epistle, the approved practice is to write salaAmN Ealayoka , without the article Al ; and in repeating it, at the end, to write it with that article. (Durrat el-Ghowwás, in De Sacy's Anthol. Gramm. Arabe, p. 72 of the Arabic text. [In the latter case, the general practice in the present day is to write simply waAls~alaAm , suppressing Ealayoka .]) In saluting the dead, one puts Ealayoka first, saying, Ealayoka salaAmu A@ll~`hi . (Ham p. 367.) You also say, maA kaAna ka*aA waka*aA ↓ laA bisalaAmatika [ No, by thy safety, such and such things were not ]. (S.) Als~ulaAmu is also a name of God, (S, M, Msb, K,) [applied to Him in the Kur lix. 23, accord. to some for *uw Als~alaAmi , i. e. *uw Als~alaAmapi ,] because of his safety, or freedom, from defect, and imperfection, and cessation of existence; (IKt, M, TA;) or from variations, and as being the everlasting, who brings the creation to nought and will not come to nought; or, accord. to Suh in the R, He is so named [as being the Author of Safety, Security, &c.; i. e.] because He has rendered all his creatures safe, or free, from defectiveness, or unsoundness, and mankind and the jinn, or genii, from the betiding of injustice, or wrong, to them, from Him; and the expositors who assert that He is thus named because of his safety, or freedom, from imperfections, and evils of any kind, utter an unseemly saying, making salaAmN to be syn. with ↓ saAlimN , which latter applies only to him who is liable to evil of any kind, and who expects it, and then becomes safe, or free, from it. (TA.) daAru Als~alaAmi is an appellation of Paradise, (M, K,) [applied thereto in the Kur vi. 127 and x. 26,] as being the abode of everlasting safety, or security; (Zj, M, TA;) the abode of safety, or security, from evils of any kind, from death and decrepitude and diseases [ &c. ]: (TA:) or as being the abode of God. (M, TA.) ― -b2- See also silomN , in four places. ― -b3- [As is there stated,] it signifies also Salutation, or greeting; (M, TA;) particularly the salutation of AlA_isolaAm [ by saying salaAmN Ealayoka or salaAmN Ealayokumo , expl. above]; (Bd in iv. 96;) a subst. (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) from sal~ama Ealayohi , (Msb,) [i. e.] from Alt~usoliymu , (S, Mgh, TA,) like kalaAmN from Alt~akoliymu . (Mgh. [See 2, third sentence.]) ― -b4- In the saying in the Kur [xxv. 64], waA_i*aA xaATabahumu A@lojaAhiluwna qaAluwA salaAmFA [ And when the ignorant speak to them, they say, salaAmFA ], this last word signifies tasal~umFA , (Sb, M,) or tasal~umFA minokumo [for natasal~amu minokumo tasal~umFA We declare ourselves to be clear, or quit, of you ], and mutaArakahF lalumo [for nutaArikukumo mutaArakapF we relinquish you ], (Bd,) [and means] there shall be neither good nor evil between us (Sb, M, Bd) and you: it is not the slAm that is used in salutation; for the verse was revealed at Mekkeh, and the Muslims had not then been commanded to salute the believers in a plurality of gods: (Sb, M:) [in iv. 88 of the Kur, which was promulgated afterwards, at ElMedeeneh, is a general command to return a salutation with a better or with the same; but the Sunneh prescribes that the salutation of salaAmN Ealayoka or salaAmN Ealayokumo when addressed to a Muslim by one not a Muslim is to be returned only by saying waEalayoka or waEalayokumo :] or the meaning in xxv. 64 is, they say a right saying, in which they are secure from harming and sinning. (Bd.) Sb asserts that Aboo-Rabee'ah used to say, A_i*aA laqiyta fulaAnFA faqulo salaAmFA , meaning tasal~umFA [for A^atasal~amu minoka tasal~umFA , i. e. When thou meetest such a one, say, I declare myself to be clear, or quit, of thee ]: and he says that some of them said salaAmN , meaning The case of me and thee is the [ case of ] being clear, or quit, each of the other; and the [ case of ] mutual relinquishing. (M.) [It is usual, in the present day, to say, AifoEalo ka*aA waAls~alaAm , meaning Do thou such a thing, and there will be an end of altercation between us.] -A2- See also saliymN . -A3- Also A kind of trees; (S, M, Msb, K;) they assert that they are evergreen; nothing eats them; but the gazelles keep to them, and protect themselves by their shade, but do not hide among them; and they are not great trees, nor of the kind called EiDaAh : (AHn, M:) they are also called ↓ silaAmN ; (K;) or this is pl. of salamapN [n. un. of salamN ], which is of another kind; like as A_ikaAmN is pl. of A^akamapN : (IB, TA:) n. un. with p . (S, M.) Als~alaAmu Ealayoka was said to an Arab of the desert; and he replied, AljavojaAvu Ealayoka : and being asked, “ What is this reply? ” he answered, “ They are two bitter trees: thou hast put upon me one, so I have put upon thee the other. ” (K.) -A4- See also salimN , in two places.

sourceDefinition: i. q. ↓ saAlimN , (S, M, K,) which means Safe, secure, or free, (Msb,) from evils of any kind; (K, Msb, TA;) applied to a man: (M:) pl. sulamaA='u ; (M, K, TA;) in some copies of the K salomaY , like jaroHaY pl. of jariyHN ; (TA;) [but this is probably its pl. only when it is used in the sense of jariyHN or the like, as seems to be the case from what follows.] Also, (M,) applied to a heart: (S, M:) biqalobK saliymK , in the Kur xxvi. 89, means With a heart free from unbelief: (M, TA:) or, divested of corruptness, or unsoundness: (Er-Rághib, TA:) in the Kur xxxvii. 82, some say that it means with a grieving, or sorrowful, heart; from saliymN in the sense here next following. (Bd.) ― -b2- Also i. q. ladiygN [meaning Bitten by a serpent ]; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ salaAmN (S, K) and ↓ masoluwmN : (K:) app., (S,) as implying a good omen, of safety; (S, M;) or because the person is left ( musolamN ) to that [bane] which is in him: (IAar, S, * M:) and sometimes it is metaphorically used as meaning (tropical:) wounded: (M:) or it means wounded, at the point of death, (M, K,) as some say: (M:) pl. salomaY . (M, and Ham p. 214.) -A2- Also, (M, K,) of a horse, (M,) The part, of the hoof, that is between the A^a$oEar [or hair, or extremity of the skin, next the hoof ], (M, TA,) or that is between the A^amoEar [q. v.], (K,) but the former is the right, (TA,) and the interior of the hoof. (M, K, TA.)

definition: , a noun of the fem.
sourceDefinition: , a noun of the fem. gender, (Msb,) A certain bone that is in the firosin [q. v., here meaning foot ] of the camel: (S, K:) this is said by A'Obeyd to be the primary signification: (S:) or the sulaAmaY of the camel are the bones of the furosin [or foot ]: (M:) [for] sulaAmaY is used alike as sing. and pl., and sometimes it has also a pl., (S,) which is sulaAmayaAtN : (S, M, K:) or it is a pl. [or rather a coll. gen. n.], of which the sing. [or n. un.] is sulaAmayapN , signifying the A^anomalap [q. v.] of [ any of ] the fingers: (IAth, TA:) [but this is a strange explanation:] it is said that the last parts in which mux~ [here meaning marrow or pulp and the like] remains in a camel when he has become emaciated are the sulaAmaY and eye; and when it has gone from these, he has none remaining: (S:) the pl. sulaAmayaAtN , (S, TA,) or sulaAmaY , (M, Msb,) also signifies the bones of the A^aSaAbiE , (S, M,) so says Kh, and Zj adds that they are also called the qaSab , (Msb,) of the hand and of the foot; (M;) [i. e., of the fingers and of the toes; and this seems to be the most common meaning, in relation to a human being; namely, the phalanges of the fingers and of the toes; ] that are between every two joints [ and what are beyond the extreme joints ] of the A^aSaAbiE : accord. to Lth, the slAmY are the bones of the A^aSaAbiE [or fingers and toes ] and the A^a$aAjiE and the A^akaAriE , and are hard and compact bones like kiEaAb [pl. of kaEobN ]: (TA: [see the words that I have here left untranslated, for the senses in which they are here used are doubtful:]) accord. to IAar, (M,) certain small bones, of the length of the A_iSobaE [or finger ], (M, K,) or nearly so, (M,) or less, (K,) of which there are four, or three, (M,) [or app., five, for the meaning here seems to be the metacarpal and metatarsal bones, to which the terms sulaAmaY and sulaAmayaAtN are sometimes applied, (see A^a$ojaEu and mu$oZN ,)] in the hand and in the foot, (K,) [i. e.] in each hand and foot: (M:) Ktr says that the slAmyAt are the Euruwq [app. a mistake for EiZaAm i. e. bones ] of the outer side of the hand and foot: (Msb:) slAmY is also said to signify any small hollow bone: and any bone of a human being: and ISh says that in every horse are six slAmyAt [app. in the fore legs and the same in the hind legs; for he seems to mean that the term slAmY is applied to each of the pasternbones and to the coffin-bone; these three corresponding to the phalanges of a human being: see faS~N ]: (TA:) it is not allowable to write slAmY otherwise than with what is termed the short alif. (MF, TA.) -A2- sulaAmaY , (M, K,) like suk~aAraY , (K, TA, [in the CK like sakor`Y , which is shown to be wrong by a verse cited in the M and TA,]) signifies also The [ south, or southerly, wind called ] januwb . (M, K.)

AlA^ :) n. un. with p . (M.)

definition: A ladder, or a series of stairs or steps, syn.
sourceDefinition: A ladder, or a series of stairs or steps, syn. miroqaApN , (M, K,) and darajapN , (M,) or miEoraAjN , (Msb,) upon which one ascends; (S, Mgh;) either of wood or of clay [ &c. ]: (Mgh:) said by Zj to be so called because it delivers thee ( yusal~imuka ) to the place to which thou desirest to go, (Mgh, TA,) i. e., to some high place, and thou hopest for safety ( Als~alaAmap ) by means of it: (Er-Rághib, TA:) masc. and fem.; (Lth, M, Mgh;) [app., accord. to Lth and F, generally fem.; for] accord. to Lth, one says, hiYa Als~ul~amu and huwa Als~ul~amu ; (Mgh;) [and F says,] it is sometimes made masc.: (K:) pl. salaAliymu (S, Mgh, K) and salaAlimu , (K,) [which latter is the original, for] the Y in salaAliymu is added by poetic license. (M, TA.) [Hence,] Als~ul~amu (assumed tropical:) Certain stars, below [ those called ] AlEaAnapu , on the right of them; (K;) as being likened to the sul~am [above-mentioned]. (TA.) ― -b2- And The garoz [or stirrup of the camel's saddle ] (S, K) is sometimes thus called [as being a means of mounting]. (S.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) A means to a thing; (K, TA;) because it leads to another thing like as does the sul~am upon which one ascends. (TA.) ― -b4- And Als~ul~amu is the name of The horse of Zebbán (in the CK Zeiyán ) Ibn-Seiyár. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, &c.,) inf. n. tasowiyapN , (K,) He made it equal, equable, uniform, even, level, flat, plane or plain; (S, * M, MA, Msb, K;) or equal in respect of elevation or of depression; (Er-Rághib, TA;) [and straight, right, direct, or rightly directed; (see its quasi-pass. 8;)] and ↓ AswAhu signifies the same; (M, K;) namely, a place, (Msb, K,) or a thing, (S, M, Er-Rághib, TA,) or an uneven, or a crooked, thing. (Mgh.) It is said in a trad., faA^amara biAlxirabi fasuw~iyato [ And he gave orders respecting the ruins, and they were levelled ]. (TA in art. xrb .) And in another trad., saw~ayonaA EalaY ruqay~apa , meaning We buried Ru- keiyeh, and made the earth of the grave even, or level, over her. (Mgh.) [Hence also,] suw~iyto Ealayohi AlA^aroDu : see 8. And hence the saying in the Kur [iv. 45], luwo tusaw~aY bihimu A@loA^aroDu , (TA,) i. e. That they were buried, and that the ground were made level over them; (S, * Bd;) bi being here syn. with EalaY : (TA in art. b :) or the meaning is, that they became like the dust of the earth; (M, Jel;) thus expl. by Th; (M;) or that they had not been created, and that they and the earth were alike. (Bd.) definition: , (S, * M, * Msb,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, * M, * Msb,) inf. n. musaAwaApN (M, Er-Rághib, Msb, TA) and siwA='N , (M,) It was, or became, equal to it, (S, Er-Rághib, Msb, TA,) and like it, in measure, extent, size, bulk, quantity, or amount, and in value, (Msb, TA,) or in linear measure, and in weight, and in the measure of capacity, [ as well as in value: ] one says h`*aA li*`lika Alv~awobi ↓ Alv~awobu musaAwK [ This garment, or piece of cloth, is equal in length and breadth to that garment, or piece of cloth ]; and h`*aA Alv~awobu li*`lika Ald~irohami ↓ musaAwK [ This garment, or piece of cloth, is equivalent to that dirhem ]: and sometimes it means in mode, or manner of being: one says, li*`lika Als~awaAdi ↓ h`*aA Als~awaAdu [ This blackness is equal in quality to this blackness ]. Er-Rághib, TA.) It is said in a trad., saAwaY AlZ~il~u Alt~ilaAla The shade, or shadow, was like, in its extent, to the mounds, in their height. (TA.) [And sAwY Al$~aYo'u raA^osahu means The thing equalled in height his head: see an ex. of the verb tropically used in this sense voce siY~N .] One says also, h`*aA yusaAwiY dirohamFA This is worth, or equal in its value to, a dirhem: and in a rare dial., one says, dirohamFA ↓ sawiYa , aor. yasowaAhu ; (Msb, TA;) which AZ disallows, saying, one says sAwAh , but not yasowaAhu . (Msb.) And h`*aA Al$~aYo'u laA yusaAwiY ka*aA This thing is not equivalent to [or is not worth ] such a thing: (Fr, S:) or laAyusaAwiY $ayoy^FA [ It (a garment, or some other thing, M) is not worth anything ]: (M, K:) ↓ lA yasowaY is of a rare dial., (K,) unknown to Fr, (S,) disallowed by A'Obeyd, but mentioned by others: (M:) Az says that it is not of the language of the Arabs [of pure speech], (Msb, TA,) but is post-classical; and in like manner ↓ lA yusowiY is not correct Arabic: this last is with damm to the [first] Y : MF says that the generality of authorities disallow it, and the Fs expressly disallows it, but the expositors thereof say that it is correct and chaste, of the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz, though an instance of a verb of which the aor. only is used. (TA.) One says likewise, sAwY Alr~ajulu qironahu The man equalled his opponent, or competitor, in knowledge, or in courage. (TA.) ― -b2- See also 6. -A2- And see 2, in four places, in the former half of the paragraph.

definition: They two were, or became, equal, like each other, or alike;
sourceDefinition: They two were, or became, equal, like each other, or alike; as also ↓ AisotawayaA . (M, K.) ↓ AstwY has two and more agents assigned to it: one says, AstwY zayodN wuEamoruw waxaAlidN fiY h`*aA [ Zeyd and 'Amr and Khálid were equal, or alike, in this ]; i. e. tasaAwawoA : whence the saying in the Kur [ix. 19], Einoda A@ll~`hi ↓ laA yasotawuwna [ They will not be equal, or alike, in the sight of God ]. (TA.) And one says, tasaAwawoA fiY AlmaAli They were, or became, equal in respect of the property, none of them exceeding another; as also fiyhi ↓ AisotawawoA . (Msb.) It is said in a trad., as some relate it, ↓ mano saAwaY yawomaAhu fahuwa magobuwnN , in which the meaning is said to be tasaAwaY [i. e. He whose two days are alike, neither being distinguished above the other by any good done by him, is weak-minded ]. (TA.) And in another it is said, laA yazaAlu Aln~aAsu bixayorK maA tafaADaluwA faA_i*aA tasaAwawoA halakuwA , (S, * TA,) i. e. [ Men will not cease to be in a good state while they vie in excellence, ] but when they cease from vying in excellent qualities and are content with defect [ and thus become alike, they perish ]: or when they become equal in ignorance: or when they form themselves into parties and divisions, and every one is alone in his opinion, and they do not agree to acknowledge one exemplar or chief or leader [ so that they are all alike ]: or, accord. to Az, when they are alike in evil, there being none among them possessed of good. (TA.)

AiEotadala (S, M, Msb, K, TA, and Ksh and Bd in ii. 27) fiY *aAtihi , (TA,) said of a place, (Msb,) and AisotaqaAma , said of a stick, or piece of wood, &c. (Ksh ubi suprà.) (TA.) One says, Aisotawato bihi AlA^aroDu [lit. The earth, or ground, became equable, uniform, even, &c., with him, he having been buried in it], meaning he perished in the earth; as also ↓ tasaw~ato , and Ealayohi ↓ suw~iyato . (M, K.) And Astwt A^aroDuhumo Their land became [ even in its surface, being ] affected with drought, or barrenness. (M, * TA.) And AstwY AlmaA='u waAlxa$abapa , meaning maEa Alxa$abapi [i. e. The water became even, or level, with the piece of wood ]. (TA.) See also 6, in four places. One says also, AstwY AlmuEaw~aju [or AlmuEowj~u (as in the MA) i. e. The crooked, or uneven, became straight, or even ]: (Mgh:) and AstwY mini A@EuwijaAjK [ It became even from a state of unevenness ]. (S.) faA@sotawaY EalaY suwqihi , in the Kur xlviii. last verse, means And has stood straight, or erect, (Bd,) or become strong, and stood straight, or erect, (Jel,) upon its stems. (Bd, Jel. [Golius erroneously assigns a similar meaning to AstswY , a verb which I do not anywhere find.]) And faA@sotawaY in the same, liii. 6, And he stood straight, or erect, in his proper form in which God created him: or was endowed by his strength with power over the affair appointed to him: (Bd:) or became firm, or steady. (Jel.) AstwY said of a stick &c. means It stood up or erect: and was, or became, even, or straight: hence one says, AstwY A_ilayohi kaAls~ahomi Almurosali He, or it, went towards him, or it, with an undeviating, a direct, or a straight, course, like the arrow hot forth: and hence, vum~a A@sotawaY A_ilaY Als~amaA='i is metaphorically said of God, in the Kur ii. 27 [and xli. 10]; (Ksh;) meaning (tropical:) Then He directed himself by his will to the [ heaven, or] elevated regions, (Ksh, Bd,) or upwards, (Ksh,) or to the heavenly bodies; (Bd;) syn. Eamada , (Zj, M, K,) and qaSada (Zj, S, M, K, and Ksh and Bd) biA_iraAdatipi ; (Ksh, Bd;) for when AlAisotiwaA='u is trans. by means of A_ilaY it imports the meaning of the directing of oneself, or, as in this case, of one's design: (TA;) you say of any one who has finished a work and has directed himself to another, qadi A@sotawaY lahu and A_ilayohi : (Har p. 631:) or the meaning here is SaEida , (Zj, M, K,) or SaEida A^amoruhu [i. e. his command ascended ]; (M;) and this is what is intended here by SaEida : (TA:) or A^aqobala EalayohaA [i. e. He advanced to it, namely, the heaven]; (Fr, Th, M, K;) like as one says, kaAna fulaAnN muqobilFA EalaY fulaAnK vum~a A@sotawaY EalaY~a yu$aAtimuniY and A_ilaY~D also, meaning A^aqobala [i. e. Such a one was advancing against such a one, then he advanced against me, and to me, reviling me, or contending with me in reviling ]: (TA:) or it means AisotawolaY , (M, K,) as some say: (M:) J says, [in the S,] but not explaining thereby the verse above cited, that it signifies also AisotawolaY and Zahara [as meaning He had, or gained, the mastery, or victory ]: and hence the saying of El-Akhtal, cited by him [in the S,] qadi A@sotawaY bi$orN EalaY AlEiraAqi mino gayori sayofK wadamK muhoraAqi [ Bishr has gained the mastery over El-'Irák without sword and without shed blood ]: Er-Rághib says that when this verb is trans. by means of EalaY , it imports the meaning of AlAisotiylaA=' ; as in the saying in the Kur [xx. 4], Aalr~aHom`nu EalaY A@loEaro$i A@sotawaY [which may be rendered, The Compassionate hath ascendancy over the empyrean so as to have everything in the universe equally within his grasp; agreeably with what here follows]: he then adds, it is said to mean that everything is alike in relation to Him in such manner that no one thing is nearer to Him than another thing, since He is not like the bodies that abide in one place exclusively of another place. (TA.) The saying lam~aA A@sotawato bihi raAHilatuhu EalaY AlbayodaA='i means [ When his riding-camel ] ascended with him upon the desert: or stood up with him straight upon its legs. (Mgh.) (Msb.) [ AstwY as quasi-pass. of saw~aAhu also signifies It was made, or became, symmetrical; congruous, or consistent in its several parts: was made, formed, or fashioned, in a suitable manner: was made, or became, adapted to the exigencies, or requirements, of its case, or of wisdom: was made, or became, complete: was made, or became, right, or good; became rectified, adjusted, or put into a right or good state. (K.) And AstwY AlT~aEaAmu The food became thoroughly cooked. (Msb.) [ xaT~u AlAisotiwaA='i means The equinoctial line. ]

sourceDefinition: , originally siwoYN ; and its dual: see sawaA='N , in ten places, all except one in the latter half of the paragraph. ― -b2- [Hence,] of him who is, or has become, in a state of wealth, or welfare, [or rather, of abundant wealth or welfare,] one says, huwa fiY siY~i raA^osihi and raA^osihi ↓ sawaA='i , (Fr, S,) or waqaEa fiY siY~i raA^osihi [in the CK (erroneously) saY~i ] and rA^sh ↓ sawaA='i (M, K) and rA^sh ↓ siwaA='i , (K,) or waqaEa rA^sh ↓ mina Aln~iEomapi fiY siwaA='i , (Ks, M,) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He is in, or has lighted upon, or come upon, ] what is in the predicament of his head ( Hukomi raA^osihi ) [ in point of eminence, of wealth, or welfare ]: or what covers his head [ thereof ]: (M, K:) or what equals his head [ in eminence ] ( yusaAwiY raA^osahu ), of wealth, or welfare: (T, TA:) or what has equalled his head [ in eminence ], of wealth, or welfare; i. e. what has accumulated upon him, and filled [or satisfied ] him: (M:) or [ what equals ] the number of the hairs of his head, of wealth, or good; (A'Obeyd, S, K;) as some explain it. (A'Obeyd, S.) See also sin~N , last sentence but one. ― -b3- [Hence likewise,] laA siy~amaA , (S, M, Msb, K,) also pronounced lA siyamaA , without teshdeed, (Msb, Mughnee, K,) and ↓ lA say~amaA is a dial. var. thereof, (Msb,) a compound of siY~ and maA , denoting exception: (S:) one says, laA siy~amaA zayodK , i. e. laA mivola zayodK [lit. There is not the like of Zeyd; virtually, and generally, meaning above all Zeyd, or especially Zeyd ]; maA being redundant: and lA sy~mA zayodN also; like as one says, daEo maA zayodN : (M, K:) [J says,] with respect to the case of the noun following mA , there are two ways: you may make maA to be in the place of Al~a*iY , and mean that an inchoative is to be understood, [namely, hw or the like,] and put the noun that you mention in the nom. case as the enunciative; thus you may say, jaA='aniY Alqawomu laA siy~amaA A^axuwka , meaning laA siY~a Al~a*iY huwa A^axuwka [i. e. The people, or party, came to me, and there was not the like of him who is thy brother; or above all, or especially, he who is thy brother ]: (S, TA: [thus in a copy of the S: in other copies of the same, and in the TA, for siY~a , siy~amaA :]) but this rendering is invalidated in such a phrase as walaA siy~amaA zayodN by the supression of the correlative of the noun in the nom. case where there is no lengthiness, and by the applying mA to denote a rational being: (Mughnee:) or you may put the noun after it in the gen. case, making mA redundant, and making siY~ to govern the noun in that case because the meaning of siY~ is mivol : [and this is the preferable way:] (Mughnee:) in both of these ways is recited the saying of Imra-el-Keys, A^alaA rub~a yuwomK laka minohun~a SaAliHK walaA siy~amaA yawomNK bidaArapi julojuli [ Verily many a good day was there to thee by reason of them; but there was not the like of a day, or above all a day, or especially a day, at Dárat Juljul, a certain pool, where Imra-el-Keys surprised his beloved, 'Oneyzeh, with others, her companions, bathing: see EM pp. 9 and 10]: you say also, A^aDoribu Alqawoma walaA siy~amaA A^axiyka , meaning walaA mivola Darobi A^axiyka [i. e. I will beat the people, or party, but there shall not be the like of the beating of thy brother ]: and if you say, walaA siy~amaA A^axuwka , the meaning is, walaA mivola Al~a*iY huwa A^axuwka [ and there shall not be the like of him who is thy brother ]: in the saying A_in~a fulaAnFA kariymN walaA siy~amaA A_ino A^atayotahu qaAEidFA , accord. to Akh, mA is a substitute for the affixed pronoun hu , which is suppressed; the meaning being, walaA mivolahu A_ino A^atayotahu qaAEidFA [i. e. Verily such a one is generous, and there is not the like of him if thou come to him sitting ]: (S, TA:) it is said in the Msb, [after explaining that mA in sy~mA may be redundant, and the noun after it governed in the gen. case as the complement of a prefixed noun; and that mA may be used in the sense of Al~*Y , and the noun following put in the nom. case as the enunciative of the inchoative hw which is suppressed;] that, accord. to some, the noun following may be in the accus. case, as being preceded by an exceptive; [or, as a specificative; (Mughnee;) in which case we must regard mA as a substitute for the affixed pronoun hu ;] but that this is not a good way; [and in this case, accord. to the generality of the authorities, it must be an indeterminate noun, not, like zayodN , determinate: (Mughnee:)] also that sy~mA should not be used without lA preceding it: and that it denotes the predominance of what follows it over what precedes it: but it is added that lA is sometimes suppressed [as is said in the Mughnee] because known to be meant, though this is rare. (TA.) One says also, laAsiY~a limaA fulaAnN (Lh, M, K) i. e. There is not the like of such a one: (TA:) and laA siy~aka maA fulaAnN (Lh, M, K) i. e. Such a one is not the like of thee. (TA.) [In both of these instances, mA is obviously redundant. Other (similar) usages of siY~ are mentioned voce sawaA='N , to which reference has been made above.] ― -b4- siY~N also signifies A [ desert such as is termed ] mufaAzap ; (S, M, K) because of the evenness of its routes, and its uniformity. (TA.) [Hence Als~iY~u is the name of a particular tract, said in the M to be a certain smooth place in the baAdiyap .] ― -b5- See also art. syw .

The people, or party, came to me, and there was not the like of him who is thy brother; or above all, or especially, he who is thy brother ]: (S, TA: [thus in a copy of the S: in other copies of the same, and in the TA, for siY~a , siy~amaA :]) but this rendering is invalidated in such a phrase as walaA siy~amaA zayodN by the supression of the correlative of the noun in the nom. case where there is no lengthiness, and by the applying mA to denote a rational being: (Mughnee:) or you may put the noun after it in the gen. case, making mA redundant, and making siY~ to govern the noun in that case because the meaning of siY~ is mivol : [and this is the preferable way:] (Mughnee:) in both of these ways is recited the saying of Imra-el-Keys, A^alaA rub~a yuwomK laka minohun~a SaAliHK walaA siy~amaA yawomNK bidaArapi julojuli [ Verily many a good day was there to thee by reason of them; but there was not the like of a day, or above all a day, or especially a day, at Dárat Juljul, a certain pool, where Imra-el-Keys surprised his beloved, 'Oneyzeh, with others, her companions, bathing: see EM pp. 9 and 10]: you say also, A^aDoribu Alqawoma walaA siy~amaA A^axiyka , meaning walaA mivola Darobi A^axiyka [i. e. I will beat the people, or party, but there shall not be the like of the beating of thy brother ]: and if you say, walaA siy~amaA A^axuwka , the meaning is, walaA mivola Al~a*iY huwa A^axuwka [ and there shall not be the like of him who is thy brother ]: in the saying A_in~a fulaAnFA kariymN walaA siy~amaA A_ino A^atayotahu qaAEidFA , accord. to Akh, mA is a substitute for the affixed pronoun hu , which is suppressed; the meaning being, walaA mivolahu A_ino A^atayotahu qaAEidFA [i. e. Verily such a one is generous, and there is not the like of him if thou come to him sitting ]: (S, TA:) it is said in the Msb, [after explaining that mA in sy~mA may be redundant, and the noun after it governed in the gen. case as the complement of a prefixed noun; and that mA may be used in the sense of Al~*Y , and the noun following put in the nom. case as the enunciative of the inchoative hw which is suppressed;] that, accord. to some, the noun following may be in the accus. case, as being preceded by an exceptive; [or, as a specificative; (Mughnee;) in which case we must regard mA as a substitute for the affixed pronoun hu ;] but that this is not a good way; [and in this case, accord. to the generality of the authorities, it must be an indeterminate noun, not, like zayodN , determinate: (Mughnee:)] also that sy~mA should not be used without lA preceding it: and that it denotes the predominance of what follows it over what precedes it: but it is added that lA is sometimes suppressed [as is said in the Mughnee] because known to be meant, though this is rare. (TA.) One says also, laAsiY~a limaA fulaAnN (Lh, M, K) i. e. There is not the like of such a one: (TA:) and laA siy~aka maA fulaAnN (Lh, M, K) i. e. Such a one is not the like of thee. (TA.) [In both of these instances, mA is obviously redundant. Other (similar) usages of siY~ are mentioned voce sawaA='N , to which reference has been made above.] ― -b4- siY~N also signifies A [ desert such as is termed ] mufaAzap ; (S, M, K) because of the evenness of its routes, and its uniformity. (TA.) [Hence Als~iY~u is the name of a particular tract, said in the M to be a certain smooth place in the baAdiyap .] ― -b5- See also art. syw .

sourceDefinition: : see sawaA'N , in seven places. ― -b2- Also, and likewise ↓ suwFY , (Akh, S, Msb, Mughnee, K,) and ↓ sawaA='N , (Akh, S, M, Mughnee, K,) and ↓ siwaA='N , (Mughnee,) i. q. makaAnN , (Mughnee,) or gayorN , (Akh, S, M, Msb, Mughnee, K,) accord. to different authorities: each used as an epithet, and as denoting exception, like gayor ; accord. to Ez-Zejjájee and Ibn-Málik, used in the same sense and manner as gayor : but accord. to Sb and the generality of authorities, an adv. n. of place, always in the accus. case, except in instances of necessity: (Mughnee:) one says, EinodiY rajulN siwaY zayodK , meaning badala zayodK and makaAna zayodK [i. e. I have with me a man instead of Zeyd and in the place of Zeyd ]: (Ham p. 570, and TA: *) [but] one says [also] mararotu birajulK siwaAka and ↓ suwaAka and ↓ sawaAy^ika , meaning gayorika [i. e. I passed by a man other than thee ]: (S:) and ↓ jaA='aniY sawaAw^uka [and siwaAk &c. Other than thou came to me ], using it as an agent; and ↓ raA^ayotu sawaA='aka [and siwaAka &c. I saw other than thee ], using it as an objective complement: and ↓ maA jaA='aniY A^aHadN sawaA='aka [and siwaAka &c. None except thou came to me ]: and maA jaA='aniY A^aHadN ↓ sawaAw^uka [and siwaAka &c. None other than thou came to me ]: (Mughnee:) and qaSadotu Alqawoma siwaY zayodK , meaning gayora zayodK [i. e. I betook myself to, or towards, the people, or party, others than Zeyd, which is virtually the same as except Zeyd ]: (Msb:) and lay^ino faEalota *aAka waA^anaA siwaAka layaA^otiyan~aka min~iY maA takorahu , meaning [ If thou do that ] when I am in a land other than thy land, [ what thou dislikest, or hatest, shall assuredly come to thee from me. ] (Ibn-Buzurj, TA.) ― -b3- The Arabs also said, Eaqoluka siwaAka , meaning Thine intellect has departed from thee. (IAar, M.) -A2- The strangest of the meanings of siwaY , in this sense with the short alif and with kesr, is qaSodN . (Mughnee.) siwaY Al$~aYo'i means qaSoduhu [i. e. The tendency, or direction, of the thing ]. (M.) And one says, qaSadotu siwaY fulaAnK , meaning qaSadotu qaSodahu [i. e. I tended, or betook myself, in the direction of, or towards, such a one ]. (S, K. * [In the CK, and in my MS. copy of the K, sawaAhu is erroneously put for siwaAhu .]) And hence, (Mughnee,) a poet says, (namely, Keys Ibn-El-Khateem, TA,) walaA^aSorifan~a siwaY Hu*ayofapa midoHatiY [ And I will surely turn towards Hodheyfeh my eulogy ]. (S, Mughnee.)

sourceDefinition: [in some copies of the K erroneously written without ' ] in its primary acceptation is an inf. n., [but without a proper verb, used as a simple subst.,] meaning Equality, equability, uniformity, or evenness; syn. AisotiwaA='N ; (Mughnee;) as also ↓ sawiy~apN : (M, K:) or [rather] it is a subst., (S, and Ksh and Bd in ii. 5,) meaning AisotiwaA='N , (Ksh and Bd ibid.,) from AisotawaY in the sense of AiEotadala ; (S;) and signifies [as above: and] equity, justice, or rectitude; syn. EadolN ; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ sawiy~apF ; (M;) and ↓ siwFY and ↓ suwFY , as well as sawaA='N , accord. to Fr, are syn. with naSafN ; and accord. to him, (TA,) and to Akh, (S, TA,) syn. with EadolN ; (S, K, TA;) [but app., only syn. with EadolN and naSafN not as a subst. but as an epithet, like wasaTN thus used, as will be shown by what follows, although] each said by Er-Rághib to be originally an inf. n. (TA.) One says, humaA mino h`*aA AlA^amori ↓ EalaY sawiy~apF , meaning sawaA='K [i. e. They two are on an equality, or on a par, in respect of this affair, or case ]: (S, TA:) and ↓ humo EalaY sawiy~apK , meaning [likewise] AisotiwaA='N [i. e. They are on an equality, or on a par ], (M, K,) fiY h`*aA AlA^amori [ in this affair, or case ]. (M.) And ↓ qasamotu Al$~aYo'a bayonahumaA biAls~awiy~api , (S,) meaning biAlEadoli [i. e. I divided the thing between them two with equity, justice, or rectitude ]. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur [viii. 60], faA@nobi*o A_ilayohimo EalaY sawaA='K , meaning EadolK [as expl. in art. nb* , q. v.]. (S, * TA.) [Hence,] layolapu Als~awaA='i The night of the thirteenth [ of the lunar month; the first being that on which the new moon is first seen]; (As, S, K, TA;) in which the moon becomes equable or uniform ( yasotawiY ) [ in illumination ]: (TA:) or the night of the fourteenth. (M, K.) ― -b2- And i. q. wasaTN [as meaning The middle, or midst, of a thing]; (S, M, Mughnee, K;) as also ↓ suwFY and ↓ siwFY . (Lh, M, K.) Hence, sawaA='u Al$~aYo'i The middle, or midst, of the thing; (S, M;) as also ↓ suwaAhu and ↓ siwaAhu . (Lh, M.) It is said in the Kur [xxxvii. 53,] faraA=hu fiY sawaA='i A@lojaHiymi [ And he shall see him ] in the middle or midst [ of the fire of Hell ]. (S, * Mughnee, TA.) In like manner also one says sawaA='u Als~abiyli [ The middle of the road ]: or, accord. to Fr, it means the right direction of the road or way. (TA.) And one says, AinoqaTaEa sawaAy^iY , meaning My waist [ broke ], or my middle. (TA.) And sawaA='u Aln~ahaAri means The middle of the day. (M, K. [In some copies of the K, mut~asaEuhu is erroneously put for munotaSafuhu .]) ― -b3- [Hence, perhaps, as being generally the middle or nearly so,] The summit of a mountain. (M, K.) And An [ eminence, or a hill, or the like, such as is termed ] A^akamap : or a [ stony tract such as is termed ] Har~ap : or the head of a Har~ap . (M.) -A2- It is also used as an epithet; (Mughnee;) and signifies Equal, equable, uniform, or even; syn. ↓ musotawK ; (M, Mughnee, K;) applied in this sense to a place; (Mughnee;) as also, thus applied, ↓ sawiY~N , and ↓ siY~N ; (M, K;) or these two signify, thus applied, [like sawaA='N as expl. hereafter,] equidistant in respect of its two extremities. (TA.) And as syn. with ↓ musotawK , it is applied [to a fem. noun as well as to a sing., and] to one and more than one, because it is originally an inf. n.; whence the phrase layosuwA sawaA='F [ They are not equal; in the Kur iii. 109]. (Mughnee.) Using it in this sense, one says A^aroDN sawaA='N [ An even land ]: and daArN sawaA='N A house uniform (↓ musotawiyapN ) in respect of the [ appertenances termed ] maraAfiq : and vawobN sawaA='N A garment, or piece of cloth, equal, or uniform, (↓ musotawK ,) in its breadth and its length and its two lateral edges: but one does not say jamalN sawaA='N , nor HamaArN sawaA='N , nor rajulN sawaA='N : (M, TA:) though one says rajulN sawaA='u AlbaToni A man whose belly is even with the breast: and sawaA='u Alqadami having no hollow to the sole of his foot. (TA.) One says also Alxaloqi ↓ rajulN sawiY~N , (S, M,) meaning ↓ musotawK [i. e. A man uniform in make, or symmetrical; or full-grown, of full vigour, or mature in body, or in body and intellect: see 8]: (S:) and rajulN ↓ sawiY~N A man equally free from excess and deficiency in his dispositions and his make: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or sound in limbs: (TA voce mir~apN , q. v.:) and ↓ gulaAmN sawiY~N A boy, or young man, uniform in make, or symmetrical, ( Alxaloqi ↓ musotawiY ,) without disease, and without fault, or defect: (Mgh:) and the fem. is sawiy~apN . (M.) Accord. to Er-Rághib, ↓ Als~awiY~u signifies That which is preserved from excess and deficiency: and hence ↓ AlS~iraATi Als~awiY~i [in Kur xx. last verse, as though meaning The road, or way that neither exceeds, nor falls short of, that which is right ]; (Er-Rághib, TA;) the right, or direct, road: (Bd, Jel:) and some read Als~awaA='i , meaning the middle, good, road: and Als~awo'i (Ksh, Bd) i. e. the evil, or bad, road: (Bd:) and Als~uwo'aY [i. e. most evil, or worst; fem. of A^asowaA^u ; for AlS~iraATu is fem. as well as masc.]: (Ksh, Bd:) [and] ↓ Als~uwaYa , of the measure fuEolaY from Als~awaA='u , [with which it is syn.,] or originally Als~uwo'aY [mentioned above]: (K:) and ↓ Als~uwaY~i , (Ksh, Bd,) which is dim. of Als~awaA=' , (Lth, TA,) [or] as dim. of Als~awo' [in which case it is for Als~uwaYo'i ]. (Ksh, Bd.) ― -b2- [Hence,] it signifies also Complete: (Mughnee:) you say, h`*aA dirohamN sawaA='N (M, Mughnee) This is a complete dirhem; (Mughnee;) using the last word as an epithet: and sawaA='F also, using it as an inf. n., as though you said AisotiwaA='F : and in like manner in the Kur xli. 9, some road sawaA='F ; and others, sawaA='K . (M.) ― -b3- And Equitable, just, or right; syn. EadolN : used in this sense in the saying in the Kur [iii. 57], taEaAlawoA A_ilaY kalimapK sawaA='K bayonanaA wabayonakumo [ Come ye to an equitable, or a just, or right, sentence, or proposition, between us and you ]. (Az, TA.) ― -b4- And Equidistant, or midway, ( EadolN , and wasaTN , S, or naSafN , Mughnee,) between two parties, (S,) or between two places; (Mughnee;) applied as an epithet to a place; as also ↓ siwFY and ↓ suwFY ; (S, Mughnee;) of which three words the second ( siwFY ) is the most chaste; (Mughnee;) or the last two signify equal ( musotawK ) in respect of its two extremities; and are used as epithets and as adv. ns.; originally, inf. ns. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ↓ makaAnFA siwFY and ↓ suwFY , (M, K,) in the Kur xx. 60, accord. to different readings, means A place equidistant, or midway, (Ksh, Bd, Jel,) between us and thee, (Ksh, Bd,) or to the comer from each of the two extremities: (Jel:) or makaAnN siwFY and suwFY means muEolamN [i. e. a place marked ], (so in a copy of the M and in one of the K,) or maEolamN , (so in other copies of the K and in the TA,) which is for *uw maEolamK , meaning having a mark, or sign, by which one is guided, or directed, thereto. (MF, TA.) ― -b5- [Also Equal, or alike, in any respect.] One says, mararotu birajulK sawaA='K waAlEadamu , (M, Mughnee, K,) and waAlEadamu ↓ siwaA='K , (K,) and waAlEadamu ↓ siwFY , and waAlEadamu ↓ suwFY , (M, K,) meaning wujuwduhu waEadamuhu sawaA='N [i. e. I passed by a man whose existence and whose non-existence are equal, or alike, to me, or in my opinion]: (M, K: *) and Sb mentions the phrase, sawaA='N huwa waAlEadamu [as meaning His existence and his nonexistence are equal, or alike, to me]. (M.) And sawaA='N EalaY~a qumota A^awo qaEadota [ It is equal, or alike, to me, that thou stand or that thou sit, or whether thou stand or sit; or that thou stand or that thou sit is equal, or alike, to me: see Kur ii. 5, and the expositions thereof]. (S.) [And ↓ siwFY is used as an adv. n., or as an inf. n. adverbially, meaning Alike: see an ex. in a verse cited voce sabotN .] ― -b6- Also A like; a similar person or thing; (S, M, K;) and so ↓ siY~N : [each used as masc. and fem.; and the former as sing. and dual and pl., though having proper dual and pl. forms:] the pl. of the former is A^asowaA='N , (S, M, K,) and also, (S, * K,) but anomalous, (S,) or [rather] quasi-pl. ns., all anomalous, (M,) ↓ sawaAsiyapN (S, M, K) and ↓ sawaAsK and ↓ sawaAsiwapN : (M, K:) and A^asowaA='N is also pl. of ↓ siY~N : (TA:) as to ↓ sawaAsiyapN , Akh says, sawaA='N is of the measure faEaAlN , and siyapN may be of the measure fiEapN or filapN , the former of which is the more agreeable with analogy, the w being changed into Y in siyapN because of the kesreh before it, for it is originally siwoyapN ; and it is from A^asowayotu Al$~aYo'a meaning “ I neglected the thing: ” [see 4:] (S:) accord. to Aboo-'Alee, the Y in sawaAsiyapN is changed from the w in sawaAsiwapN , in which latter some preserve it to show that it is the final radical: (M:) accord. to Fr, sawaAsiyapN has no sing., and relates only to equality in evil: (T, TA:) so in the saying, sawaAsiyapN kaA^asonaAni AlHimaAri [ Equals like the teeth of the ass ]. (TA.) It requires two [or more nouns for its subjects]: you say, sawaA='N zayodN waEamorNw , meaning *awaA sawaA='K [i. e., lit., Two possessors of equality, or likeness, are Zeyd and 'Amr ], (M, K,) because it is [originally] an inf. n.: (M:) and humaA fiY h`*aA AlA^amori sawaA='N [ They two are in this affair, or case, likes ]: (S:) and humaA sawaAA=ni (S, M, K) and ↓ siy~aAni i. e. They two are likes: (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K:) and humo sawaA='N and A^asowaA='N and ↓ sawaAsiyapN i. e. They are likes; (S; [the first and last of these three are mentioned in the Mgh as identical in meaning;]) or, accord. to Fr, the last means they are equals in evil, not in good: (T, TA:) and ↓ maAhuwa laka bisiY~K He is not a person like to thee: and maAhumo laka biA^asowaA='K [ They are not persons like to thee ]: (Lh, M:) and ↓ maAhiYa laka bisiY~K (Lh, M, K *) i. e. She is not a person like to thee: (TA:) and maAhun~a laka biA^asowaA='K [ They (females) are not persons like to thee ]: and limano faEala *aAka ↓ laA siY~a [ There is not a like to him who did that ]: and A_i*aA faEalota *aAka ↓ laA siy~aka [ There is not the like of thee when thou doest that ]: (Lh, M, K:) and fulaAnK ↓ laA siy~apa (K) [ There is not the like of such a one: in the CK, fulaAnN : perhaps the right reading is fulaAnN ↓ laA siy~aka Such a one is not the like of thee ]. sawaA='N and ↓ siy~aAni should not be used with A^awo in the place of wa except by poetic license: one of the exceptions to this rule is the saying of Aboo-Dhu-eyb, wakaAna siy~aAni A^al~aA yasoraHuwA naEamFA A^awo yasoraHuwhu bihaA waA@gobar~ati Als~uwHu [ And they were two like cases that they should not send forth cattle to pasture or send him forth with them when the tracts were very dusty by reason of drought]. (M.) For two other exs. of sawaA=' , [as well as of its syn. siY~ , and for laA siy~amaA also,] see siY~N . ― -b7- See also siwFY in six places.

EadolN : used in this sense in the saying in the Kur [iii. 57], taEaAlawoA A_ilaY kalimapK sawaA='K bayonanaA wabayonakumo [ Come ye to an equitable, or a just, or right, sentence, or proposition, between us and you ]. (Az, TA.) ― -b4- And Equidistant, or midway, ( EadolN , and wasaTN , S, or naSafN , Mughnee,) between two parties, (S,) or between two places; (Mughnee;) applied as an epithet to a place; as also ↓ siwFY and ↓ suwFY ; (S, Mughnee;) of which three words the second ( siwFY ) is the most chaste; (Mughnee;) or the last two signify equal ( musotawK ) in respect of its two extremities; and are used as epithets and as adv. ns.; originally, inf. ns. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ↓ makaAnFA siwFY and ↓ suwFY , (M, K,) in the Kur xx. 60, accord. to different readings, means A place equidistant, or midway, (Ksh, Bd, Jel,) between us and thee, (Ksh, Bd,) or to the comer from each of the two extremities: (Jel:) or makaAnN siwFY and suwFY means muEolamN [i. e. a place marked ], (so in a copy of the M and in one of the K,) or maEolamN , (so in other copies of the K and in the TA,) which is for *uw maEolamK , meaning having a mark, or sign, by which one is guided, or directed, thereto. (MF, TA.) ― -b5- [Also Equal, or alike, in any respect.] One says, mararotu birajulK sawaA='K waAlEadamu , (M, Mughnee, K,) and waAlEadamu ↓ siwaA='K , (K,) and waAlEadamu ↓ siwFY , and waAlEadamu ↓ suwFY , (M, K,) meaning wujuwduhu waEadamuhu sawaA='N [i. e. I passed by a man whose existence and whose non-existence are equal, or alike, to me, or in my opinion]: (M, K: *) and Sb mentions the phrase, sawaA='N huwa waAlEadamu [as meaning His existence and his nonexistence are equal, or alike, to me]. (M.) And sawaA='N EalaY~a qumota A^awo qaEadota [ It is equal, or alike, to me, that thou stand or that thou sit, or whether thou stand or sit; or that thou stand or that thou sit is equal, or alike, to me: see Kur ii. 5, and the expositions thereof]. (S.) [And ↓ siwFY is used as an adv. n., or as an inf. n. adverbially, meaning Alike: see an ex. in a verse cited voce sabotN .] ― -b6- Also A like; a similar person or thing; (S, M, K;) and so ↓ siY~N : [each used as masc. and fem.; and the former as sing. and dual and pl., though having proper dual and pl. forms:] the pl. of the former is A^asowaA='N , (S, M, K,) and also, (S, * K,) but anomalous, (S,) or [rather] quasi-pl. ns., all anomalous, (M,) ↓ sawaAsiyapN (S, M, K) and ↓ sawaAsK and ↓ sawaAsiwapN : (M, K:) and A^asowaA='N is also pl. of ↓ siY~N : (TA:) as to ↓ sawaAsiyapN , Akh says, sawaA='N is of the measure faEaAlN , and siyapN may be of the measure fiEapN or filapN , the former of which is the more agreeable with analogy, the w being changed into Y in siyapN because of the kesreh before it, for it is originally siwoyapN ; and it is from A^asowayotu Al$~aYo'a meaning “ I neglected the thing: ” [see 4:] (S:) accord. to Aboo-'Alee, the Y in sawaAsiyapN is changed from the w in sawaAsiwapN , in which latter some preserve it to show that it is the final radical: (M:) accord. to Fr, sawaAsiyapN has no sing., and relates only to equality in evil: (T, TA:) so in the saying, sawaAsiyapN kaA^asonaAni AlHimaAri [ Equals like the teeth of the ass ]. (TA.) It requires two [or more nouns for its subjects]: you say, sawaA='N zayodN waEamorNw , meaning *awaA sawaA='K [i. e., lit., Two possessors of equality, or likeness, are Zeyd and 'Amr ], (M, K,) because it is [originally] an inf. n.: (M:) and humaA fiY h`*aA AlA^amori sawaA='N [ They two are in this affair, or case, likes ]: (S:) and humaA sawaAA=ni (S, M, K) and ↓ siy~aAni i. e. They two are likes: (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K:) and humo sawaA='N and A^asowaA='N and ↓ sawaAsiyapN i. e. They are likes; (S; [the first and last of these three are mentioned in the Mgh as identical in meaning;]) or, accord. to Fr, the last means they are equals in evil, not in good: (T, TA:) and ↓ maAhuwa laka bisiY~K He is not a person like to thee: and maAhumo laka biA^asowaA='K [ They are not persons like to thee ]: (Lh, M:) and ↓ maAhiYa laka bisiY~K (Lh, M, K *) i. e. She is not a person like to thee: (TA:) and maAhun~a laka biA^asowaA='K [ They (females) are not persons like to thee ]: and limano faEala *aAka ↓ laA siY~a [ There is not a like to him who did that ]: and A_i*aA faEalota *aAka ↓ laA siy~aka [ There is not the like of thee when thou doest that ]: (Lh, M, K:) and fulaAnK ↓ laA siy~apa (K) [ There is not the like of such a one: in the CK, fulaAnN : perhaps the right reading is fulaAnN ↓ laA siy~aka Such a one is not the like of thee ]. sawaA='N and ↓ siy~aAni should not be used with A^awo in the place of wa except by poetic license: one of the exceptions to this rule is the saying of Aboo-Dhu-eyb, wakaAna siy~aAni A^al~aA yasoraHuwA naEamFA A^awo yasoraHuwhu bihaA waA@gobar~ati Als~uwHu [ And they were two like cases that they should not send forth cattle to pasture or send him forth with them when the tracts were very dusty by reason of drought]. (M.) For two other exs. of sawaA=' , [as well as of its syn. siY~ , and for laA siy~amaA also,] see siY~N . ― -b7- See also siwFY in six places.

sourceDefinition: , aor. and , inf. n. $aHiyjN (S, O, K) and $uHaAjN (As, S, O, K) and $aHajaAnN (O, K) and ta$oHaAjN ; (O, L;) and ↓ t$H~j ; and ↓ Ast$Hj ; (L, TA;) He uttered his voice or cry; [ brayed; croaked; ] said of a mule, (S, O, K, &c.,) and of an ass, (ISd, O,) and of a raven, or crow; (S, O, K, &c.;) and sometimes, (tropical:) of a man: (L:) or $aHiyjN is used in relation to a mule; and $aHajaAnN , in relation to a raven, or crow: (T, TA:) or the former of these two signifies the reiterating of the voice or cry of the raven, or crow; and when it stretches forth its head [and croaks], you say naEaba : and accord. to the L, the first and second inf. ns., used in relation to an ass, signify the uttering certain of his voices or cries: Th is thought by ISd to have mentioned also $aHija ; but the latter doubts its correctness: and $uHaAjN is also expl. as signifying the raising of the voice; but as used more especially in relation to the mule and the ass. sourceDefinition: , aor. , (K,) inf. n. $aroHN , (S, O,) He uncovered, laid open, displayed, exposed to view, discovered, revealed, or disclosed. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, $araHa A^amorahu (tropical:) He showed, discovered, disclosed, or made apparent, his affair, or case. (A, TA.) And $araHa masoA^alapF (A, TA) (tropical:) He explained a question; (TA;) he explained, or made manifest, the answer to a question. (A.) And $araHa AlgaAmiDa (assumed tropical:) He expounded, explained, or interpreted, what was obscure, recondite, or abstruse. (S, O.) And $araHa AlHadiyva , inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) He expounded, explained, or interpreted, the tradition; showed, or made apparent, its meaning. (Msb.) ― -b3- And $araHa , aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n., (O, TA,) He opened (O, K, TA) a thing of any kind, of any substance or material. (TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) He defloured a virgin: (O, K, TA:) or (tropical:) he compressed a woman, (A, L,) or a virgin, (K,) lying on her back; (A, L, K;) or he threw, or laid, upon her back, and then compressed, his female slave, or young woman. (O, L.) ― -b5- He widened, or dilated, a thing. (K.) ― -b6- Hence, (TA,) $araHa A@ll~`hu Sadorahu , (S, A, Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (Msb, TA,) (assumed tropical:) God dilated his bosom, (Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) liqabuwli Alxayori [ for the acceptance, or favourable acceptance, of what was good ], (O, TA,) and liloA_isolaAmi (Mgh, Msb, TA) for the acceptance, or favourable acceptance, [ of El-Islám, or] of the truth, (Msb, TA,) as in the Kur [xxxix. 23]. (TA. [Said in the TA to be tropical; but not so in the A, being mentioned in the latter as proper.]) [And hence, an objective complement being app. understood,] fulaAnN ya$oraHu A_ilaY Ald~unoyaA (tropical:) Such a one manifests desire for the things of the present world: (A:) or such a one becomes dilated in the bosom at the prospect of the things of the present world, and desirous of acquiring them, with large desire. (O, * L.) And maA liY A^araAka ta$oraHu A_ilaY kul~i riybapK (tropical:) What aileth me that I see thee manifesting desire for everything occasioning doubt, or suspicion, or evil opinion? (A, TA.) ― -b7- Also He cut; and so ↓ $r~H . (K.) You say, $araHa All~aHoma , (A, O, Msb, TA,) inf. n. as above; (O;) and ↓ $r~Hhu , (A, O, Msb, TA,) inf. n. ta$oriyHN ; (S, O, TA;) the former meaning He cut the flesh-meat lengthwise [or into an oblong slice or into such slices ]: and the latter, he so cut it much or into many [ such ] pieces [or slices ]: (Msb:) or the former, he cut the flesh-meat from the joint or limb: or both signify he cut the flesh-meat upon the bone: (L, TA:) or $aroHu All~aHomi signifies taSofiyfuhu ; and so ↓ ta$oriyHuhu : (O:) or Alt~aSofiyfu is a kind of ↓ ta$oriyH ; i. e. the cutting a piece of flesh-meat thin, so that it is translucent by reason of its thinness, and then throwing it upon the live coals. (TA.) ― -b8- Also, (K,) inf. n. as above, (O,) He understood (O, K) speech, or language. (TK.) ― -b9- And $aroHN also signifies The act of keeping, preserving, or guarding. (TA.) [And particularly The guarding of seed-produce from the birds; (see $aAriHN ;) as also $iraAHapN ; (see 1 in art. xfr , fourth sentence;) each an inf. n., of which the verb is $araHa .]

sourceDefinition: , aor. (S, M, Msb, K) and , (M, K,) inf. n. $anoqN , (S, M, Msb,) He curbed the camel by means of his zimaAm [or nose-rein ], (S, K,) or pulled the xiTaAm [or halter, or leadingrope, ] of the camel, (M,) while riding him, (S, M,) in the direction of his [ own ] head, (M,) so as to make the prominences behind his [ the camel's ] ears cleave to the upright piece of wood rising from the fore part of the saddle: (M, K:) or he raised the camel's head (M, Msb, K) by pulling his zimaAm , (M, Msb,) while riding him, (Msb, K,) like as the rider of the horse does with his horse: (Msb:) and ↓ A$nqhu signifies the same: (S, M, Msb, K:) or ↓ A$nq is intrans.; you say, $anaqa AlbaEiyra and huwa ↓ A$nq , the reverse of the usual rule; (IJ, M;) or the latter is intrans. also; (S, Msb, K;) signifying he (the camel) raised his head. (S, M, Msb, K. *) ― -b2- Hence, $anaqotuhaA , occurring in a trad., referring to a female hare, inf. n. as above, means, as implying restraint, I cast, or shot, at her, or I struck her, so as to render her incapable of motion. (O.) ― -b3- And $anaqa AlbaEiyra , or Aln~aAqapa , (M, K,) inf. n. as above, (M,) He bound the he-camel, or the she-camel, with the $inaAq [q. v.]. (M, K.) ― -b4- And $anaqa raA^osa Ald~aAb~api , (M,) or raA^osa Alfarasi , (K,) (tropical:) He bound (M, K) the head of the beast, (M,) or the head of the horse, (K,) to the upper part of a tree, (M,) or to the head of a tree, or to a tree, (accord. to different copies of the K,) or to a peg, (M,) or to an elevated peg, (K,) so that his neck became extended and erect. (M, TA.) ― -b5- And $anaqa Alqirobapa , (IDrd, O, K,) aor. , (IDrd, O,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He bound the mouth of the water-skin with the bond called wikaA=' , and then bound the extremity of its wikaA=' to its fore legs: (IDrd, O, K, TA: [in the CK, A^awokaA^ahA is erroneously put for A^awokaAhaA , or, as in some copies of the K, wakaAhaA :]) or he suspended it: and [in like manner] Alqirobapa ↓ A$nq , inf. n. as above, he suspended the water-skin to a peg: (TA:) or the latter signifies he put a $inaAq to the water-skin: (M:) or he bound the water-skin with a $inaAq , (S, K, TA,) i. e. a cord with which its mouth is bound. (S.) ― -b6- [Hence $anaqahu , as used in the present day, and in post-classical works, meaning (assumed tropical:) He hanged him by the neck, till he died: (see the pass. part. n., below:) whence ↓ mi$onaqapN , meaning A gallows; pl. ma$aAniqu .] ― -b7- $anaqa Alxaliy~apa , (M, K,) aor. , inf. n. $anoqN ; (M;) and ↓ $n~qhA , (M, K,) inf. n. ta$oniyqN ; (TA;) He put a piece of wood, which is called ↓ $aniyqN , (M, K,) pared for the purpose, (M,) into the hive, and with it raised a portion of the honey-comb in the width of the hive, (M, K, *) having fixed the $ynq beneath it; and sometimes two portions of the honey-comb, and three: (M: [accord. to which one says also, $anaqa fiY Alxaliy~api AlquroSayoni waAlv~alaAvapa :]) this is done only when the bees are rearing their young ones. (M, K. *) ― -b8- Accord. to Aboo-Sa'eed, Al$~aYo'a ↓ A^a$onaqotu and $anaqotuhu signify the same: (TA: [in which the meaning is not expl.; but it is immediately added, app. to indicate the meaning here intended;]) El-Mutanakhkhil El-Hudhalee says, describing a bow and arrows, $anaqotu bihaA maEaAbila murohafaAtK i. e. I put its string into [ the notches of ] arrows [ broad and long in the heads, made sharp or pointed ]. (O, * TA.) -A2- $aniqa , (M, K,) aor. ; (K;) and $anaqa , (M, K,) aor. ; (K;) He loved a thing, and became attached to it; (M, K, TA;) said of a man: (TA:) and $aniqa , inf. n. $anaqN , is said of a man's heart, (O, TA,) meaning as above: (O:) or $anaqN signifies the heart's yearning towards, or longing for, or desiring, a thing. (Msb.) -A3- $anaqN also signifies The being long: (M:) or the being long in the head, (JK, S, TA,) as though it were stretched upwards: (TA:) one says of a horse, $aniqa inf. n. $anaqN , meaning He was long in the head. (JK.) ― -b2- $anaqu AlmaroA^api , signifies AisotinaAnuhaA mina Al$~aHomi [app. meaning The woman's becoming sleek, like masaAn~ (or whetstones ) by reason of fat: see Aisotan~ati AlfiSaAlu , in art. sn ]: and the epithet applied to her is ↓ $aniqapN , pl. $aniqaAtN . (JK, Ibn-' Abbád, O, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. mu$aAnaqapN and $inaAqN , He mixed his cattle with his [i. e. another's] cattle: (K, TA:) this is when [contributions to the poor-rate such as are termed] A^a$onaAq [pl. of $anaqN ] are incumbent on a man, or two men, or three, when their cattle are separate, and one says to another, $aAniqoniY , i. e. Mix thou my cattle and thy cattle; for if they are separate, a $anaq will be obligatory, or incumbent, on each of us; and if they are mixed, the case will be light to us: so the $inaAq signifies the sharing in the $anaq or in the $anaqaAni . (L, TA.) [See also what follows in this paragraph: and see $anaqN .] One says also ↓ laA ta$aAnaquwA [for laA tata$aAnaquwA ] Ye shall not put together what are separate [of cattle]; Alt~a$aAnuqu being syn. with Almu$aAnaqapu . (TA.) ― -b2- $inaAqN signifies also The taking somewhat from the $anaq : and hence the trad., laA $inaAqa : (K, TA:) this means There shall not be taken from the $anaq [any contribution to the poorrate] unless it is complete [in number]: (A' Obeyd, S, TA:) the $anaq being, of camels, such as exceed five, up to ten; and what exceed ten, up to fifteen: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) Aboo-Sa'eed Ed-Dareer says, up to nine; and up to fourteen: but this is pronounced in the L to be wrong: (TA:) [Mtr also says,] it means there shall not be taken aught of what exceed five, up to nine, for example: or, accord. to Aboo-Sa'eed Ed-Dareer, it is like the mixing; but this requires consideration: (Mgh:) Aboo-Sa'eed says that laA $inaAqa means a man shall not adjoin (↓ laA yu$oniqu [thus written here and thus expl. in the TA]) his sheep or goats, and his camels, to the sheep or goats [and the camels ] of another person, in order to annul what is obligatory, or incumbent, on him, of the poor-rate: this is [for instance] in the case in which each of them has forty sheep or goats; so that it is incumbent on them to give two sheep or goats; but when one of them adjoins ( A^aHaduhumaA ↓ faA_i*aA $an~aqa [thus in this instance in the TA, perhaps a mistranscription for A^a$onaqa ,]) his sheep or goats to those of another, and the collector of the poorrate finds them in his [the latter's] possession, he takes from them one sheep or goat. (TA.)
