sourceDefinition: What is between one fariyDap and the next fariyDap , (A'Obeyd, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, TA,) [meaning a number that is between two other numbers whereof each imposes the obligation of giving a due termed fariyDap ,] of camels, and of sheep or goats, (M, TA,) in relation to the poorrate: (S, Mgh, K, TA:) so called because nothing is taken therefrom; so that it is adjoined ( A^u$oniqa i. e. A^aDiyfa ) to that [number] which is next to it [of the numbers below it]: (JK:) accord. to some, it is syn. with waqaSN ; (Mgh, Msb;) but some say that it relates peculiarly to camels; (M, Mgh, Msb;) and waqaSN , to bulls and cows: (Mgh, Msb:) used in relation to sheep or goats, it is what is between forty and a hundred and twenty; and in like manner as to other numbers [that impose the obligation of giving a fryDp ]: K, TA:) Ahmad Ibn-Hambal is related to have said that the $anaq is what is above the fryDp , absolutely; as, for instance, what is above forty sheep or goats: (TA: [I here render the word duwna “ above, ” though it also means “ below, ” because nothing is due from sheep or goats fewer than forty:]) as A'Obeyd says, it is, of camels, such as exceed five, up to ten; and what exceed ten, up to fifteen: (O, * TA: [see also 3:]) Ks states, on the authority of some one or more of the Arabs, that it is up to twenty-five; and says that it is what does pot impose the obligation of the fryDp ; meaning what is between five and twenty-five: (Fr, TA:) [but it is also expl. as applied to the due itself that is to be contributed to the poorrates for certain numbers of camels: thus] Aboo- 'Amr Esh-Sheybánee says, the $anaq for five camels is a sheep or goat; for ten, two sheep or goats; for fifteen three sheep or goats; and for twenty, four sheep or goats; the term $anaqN being applied alike to the sheep or goat, and to the two sheep or goats, and to the three sheep or goats, and to the four sheep or goats; what exceeds this last being termed fariyDapN : (TA:) or, in the case of the poor-rate, the lowest $anaq ( Al$~anaqu AlA^asofalu ) is a sheep or goat for five camels; and the highest $anaq ( Al$~anaqu AlA^aEolaY ) is a binot maxaAD for five and twenty: (O, K:) the pl. of $anaqN is A^a$onaAqN (M, Msb, TA) and $inaAqN . (M.) ― -b2- Also What is above the bloodwit ( maA duwna Ald~iyapi ): (As, S, O, Msb, K:) the term A^a$onaAq , (S, M, Msb,) pl. of $anaqN , (M,) being applied to the fines, for wounds, that are sent with the complete bloodwit (S, M, * O, Msb) by him upon whom rests the obligation to send such; (S, O, Msb;) as though they were attached to the main, or greatest, fine: (S, M, * O:) and an addition, in the bloodwit, (M, Msb,) of five, (M,) or of six, (M, Msb,) or of seven, (Msb,) to the hundred camels [ which constitute the complete bloodwit ], (M, Msb, *) in order that it may be described as ample: (Msb:) [for,] as IAar and As and El-Athram say, the man of rank or quality, when he gave [the bloodwit], used to add to it five [or more] camels, to show thereby his excellence and his generosity: (TA:) a redundancy [ in the case of the bloodwit ]; (O, K;) one of the explanations of the term given by As: (O:) or in the case of bloodwits ( diyaAt ), the lowest $anaq ( Al$~anaqu AlA^asofalu ) is twenty camels whereof every one is a binot maxaAD ; and the highest $anaq ( Al$~anaqu AlA^aEolaY ) is twenty camels whereof every one is a ja*aEap : (O, K:) and some say that A^a$onaAqu Ald~iyaAti means the sorts of bloodwits; the bloodwit for purely-unintentional homicide being a hundred camels, which those who are responsible for it undertake to give in fifths, consisting of twenty whereof every one is an Aibonap maxaAD , and twenty whereof every one is an Aibonap labuwn , and twenty whereof every one is an Aibon labuwn , and twenty whereof every one is a Hiq~ap , and twenty whereof every one is a ja*aEap ; these also being termed A^a$onaAq . (TA.) ― -b3- It signifies also A fine, or mulct, for a wound or the like; (O, Msb, K;) as, for instance, for a burn, (O, TA,) or such as a wound on the head that lays bare the bone, (Msb, TA,) and other wounds, (Msb,) and for a tooth [ knocked out ], and for an eye blinded, and for an arm or a hand vitiated, or rendered unsound and motionless, or stiff; and for anything short of what requires the complete bloowit: (TA:) or, as some say, a fine for that which does not render obnoxious to retaliation; as a scratch, or laceration of the skin, and the like: (M:) pl. A^a$onaAqN . (M, Msb.) -A2- Also A burden borne on one side of a beast, equiponderant to another borne on the other side; syn. EidolN : (K, TA: [in the CK and my MS. copy of the K, AlEadolu is erroneously put for AlEidol :]) Al$~anaqaAni signifies AlEidolaAn . (JK, Ibn-' Abbád, O, TA. *) ― -b2- And A rope, or cord. (Ibn-' Abbád, O, K.) ― -b3- And A bow-string; (O, TA;) as also ↓ $inaAqN ; (O, K, * TA;) so called because it is bound to the head of the bow: (O, TA:) or, accord. to Sh, a good bow-string, i. e. strong and long. (TA.) [See what follows.] -A3- Al$~anaqu also signifies AlEamalu [ The making a thing]: (K:) thus accord. to some in the saying of Ru-beh, describing a sportsman [and his bow], saw~aY lahaA kabodaA='a tanozuw fiY Al$~anaqo [as though meaning He prepared for it, or them, a bow such that the part whereby it was held filled the hand, springing in the making by reason of its elasticity and strength: but the word which I have written tanozuw , and which is thus in one place in the TA, and in another place in the same, where the verse is repeated, tanozuwA , is illegible in the copy of the O, and may be a mistranscription]: accord. to others, however, the last word, Al$~anaqo , here means the bow-string. (O, TA.)

sourceDefinition: A mountain: (IAar, S:) or the highest part of a mountain: (Skr, O, K:) or a part that is even, (Lth, O, K,) and small in breadth, in the face of a mountain, resembling a wall, ( fiY lihobi jabalK ,) (Lth, O,) that cannot be ascended: (Lth, O, K: *) or the most difficult place in a mountain. (S, O, K.) A poet says, cited as using it in the last sense, $agowaA='u tawTinu bayona Al$~iyqi waAln~iyqi [ An eagle dwelling between the most difficult place in a mountain and the highest part thereof ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And accord. to some, it signifies in that verse (TA) A narrow cleft in a mountain: or in the head thereof: or a cleft between two rocks. (K, TA.) ― -b4- A side; syn. jaAnibN . (Skr, O, K.) One says, AimotalA^a mina Al$~iyqi A_ilaY Al$~iyqi It became filled from side to side. (TA.) -A2- The head [or glans ] of the penis. (IAar, O, K.) -A3- The hair of a horse's tail: n. un. with p . (IAar, O, K.) -A4- A species of fish. (IAar, O, K.) ― -b2- The aquatic bird [or rather birds ] called burak [pl. of burokapN , q. v.]: (K:) n. un. with p . (TA. (O.) -A6- See also art. $wq .

definition: It (water, S, M, and the like, M) poured out or forth, or became poured out or forth;
sourceDefinition: It (water, S, M, and the like, M) poured out or forth, or became poured out or forth; (S, M, A, K;) as also ↓ Sab~a , (M, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. SabiybN ; (Msb;) and ↓ tSb~b , (M, K,) which is of a form rarely occurring as that of a quasi-pass. of an unaugmented triliteral verb, being generally that of the quasi-pass. of a verb of the form faE~ala ; (MF, TA;) [but this app. denotes its doing so repeatedly; and abundantly, like tadaf~aqa , q. v.;] and ↓ ASTb~ . (K.) One says, AlmaA='u yanoSab~u mina Aljabali , (TA,) and mn Aljbl ↓ yataSab~abu , (S, TA,) The water descends, little by little, from the mountain. (S, TA.) And AlEaraqu ↓ tSb~b [ The sweat flowed ], and Ald~amu [ the blood ]. (A.) And EaraqFA ↓ taSab~abotu [which may be rendered I flowed with sweat ] is a phrase of the Arabs, meaning tSb~b EaraqiY [ my sweat flowed ]: thus the act is literally ascribed to the speaker, and what is essentially the agent becomes a specificative: it is not allowable to say EaraqFA taSab~abotu ; for, as it is not allowable to put the agent before the verb, so it is not allowable to put the specificative, when it is virtually the agent, before the verb. (IJ, M.) ― -b2- One says also, AnSb~ Alkuwzu [ The mug had its contents poured out or forth ]. (TA in art. dfq .) ― -b3- See also 1, in three places. ― -b4- AnSb Aln~aAsu EalaY AlmaA='i [generally implies descent, but] means (assumed tropical:) The people collected together, or assembled, at the water. (Msb.) ― -b5- [And AnSb~ is often said of a place, or the ground, &c., meaning (assumed tropical:) It sloped downwards. ― -b6- Har (p. 125) uses the phrase tanoSab~u A_ilaY All~ahowi , meaning (as there expl.) (assumed tropical:) Thou inclinest to diversion, or sport. .]

definition: A quantity of wheat or food, &c.
sourceDefinition: A quantity of wheat or food, &c., that is poured out or forth (M, K) together, or collectedly; (M;) also (M, K) sometimes (M) termed ↓ Sub~N . (M, K.) See also 1, near the beginning. ― -b2- And A suforap [or piece of skin in which the traveller puts his food; or the thing upon which one eats ]; (M, K;) so called because the food is poured into it, or upon it: (M:) or a thing like the suforap : (M, K:) and Sun~apN , with n , signifies the same. (M.) ― -b3- See also SubaAbapN , with which it is syn. ― -b4- Also A company of men: (M, Msb, K:) [app. tropical; but it is said that] this is the primary meaning, and it is used in relation to camels, and sheep or goats, and the like, tropically. (TA.) ― -b5- (tropical:) A detached number of horses, (S, M, A, Msb, K,) and of camels, (A, K,) and of sheep or goats, (A, Msb, K,) and of dirhems, or pieces of money: (A:) or from ten to forty: (A, K:) or from twenty to thirty and forty of camels and of sheep or goats: or less than a hundred (M, A, K) of camels: (M, K:) or of camels i. q. SiromapN : (S:) and from ten to forty of goats: (AZ, S:) or a flock of sheep or a herd of goats, as being likened to a company of men: (TA:) or from twenty to forty of sheep and of goats; or peculiarly of goats: or about fifty: or from sixty to seventy: and of camels about five or six: (IAth, TA:) and a collection of dirhems, or pieces of money, and of wheat, or food, &c.: and a piece of a thing: (Msb:) [or] a small quantity or portion of wealth or property. (M, K.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) A part, or portion, of the night: so in the saying, maDato Sub~apN mina All~ayoli (assumed tropical:) [A part, or portion, of the night passed ]. (S.)

definition: signifies The turning, or sending, or putting, a thing away, or back, from its way, or course;
sourceDefinition: signifies The turning, or sending, or putting, a thing away, or back, from its way, or course; the causing it to turn away, or back; therefrom; the averting it, or repelling it therefrom: (M:) or the shifting a thing from one state, or condition, to another; (Bd in vi. 105;) and so ↓ Alt~aSoriyfu . (TA.) You say, Sarafahu , (M, K,) or Sarafahu Eano wajohihi , (Msb, TA,) i. e. Eano sananihi , (TA in art. wjh ,) aor. , (M, Msb, K,) inf. n. SarofN , (M, Msb,) He turned, sent, or put, him, or it, away, or back, &c., (M, K,) from his, or its, way, or course. (M.) And nafosahu Eani ↓ SArf Al$~aYo'i , meaning SarafahaA Eanohu [ He turned himself away, or back, from the thing ]. (M.) And Sarafotu Alr~ajula Ean~iY [ I turned the man away, or back, or I averted him, or repelled him, from me ]. (S.) And Sarafa AlS~iboyaAna He dismissed the boys, or sent them away, syn. qalabahumo , (S, K,) from the school: (K:) or Sarafotu AlS~abiY~a I let the boy go his way; and in like manner, AlA^ajiyra the hired man. (Msb.) And Sarafa A@ll~`hu Eanoka AlA^a*aY [ May God avert from thee harm ]. (S.) And ↓ ASTrf wajohahu (K in art. sfw and sfY ) [meaning Sarafahu i. e.] He turned away his face. (TK in that art.) Sarafa A@ll~`hu quluwbahumo , in the Kur [ix. 128], means God hath made them to err in requital of that which they have done: (M, TA:) or God hath turned them away, or may God turn them away, from belief. (Bd.) And saA^aSorifu Eano A=yaAtiY , in the Kur [vii. 143], means [in like manner] I will requite by causing to err from the direction of my signs. (O, TA.) sourceDefinition: [in its primary acceptation is like AlS~arofu in the primary acceptation of the latter, but generally relates to several objects, or is used in an intensive sense]: see 1, first sentence: it signifies The turning of the winds (Lth, O, K, TA) from one state or condition, to another; (O, TA;) or from one direction, or course, or way, to another; (Lth, O, K, TA;) and so of the torrents, and of the horse, and of affairs, and of the verses of the Kur-án; (Lth, TA;) the making of the winds to very, or differ; and so of the clouds; (M;) the changing of the winds to south and north [&c.] and hot and cold [&c.]; (Jel in ii. 159, and xlv. 4;) or the making of the winds to be south and north, and east and west, and to be of various sorts in their kinds: (TA:) or taSoriyfu AlA=yaAti signifies [ the varying, or diversifying, of the verses of the Kur-án, by repeating them in different forms; or] the making of the verses of the Kur-án distinct [ in their meanings by repeating and varying them, as expl. by many of the expositors in the instances occurring in vi. 46 and 65 and 105, and xlvi. 26]. (O, K.) ― -b2- It signifies also The deriving one word from another [ by modification of the form for the purpose of modifying the meaning; including what we term the declining of nouns (like AlS~arofu ) and the conjugating of verbs]. (O, K.) [The science of Alt~aSoriyf in language is commonly termed Eilomu ↓ AlS~arofi .] ― -b3- In relation to property, or money, see 1, near the middle of the paragraph. ― -b4- And in relation to speech, see 1, near the middle of the paragraph. ― -b5- One says also, Sr~f Al$~aYo'a , (M,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) meaning He employed the thing in other [i. e. more ] than one way; as though he turned it from one way to another way. (M, TA.) ― -b6- And [hence,] Sar~afotuhu fiY AlA^amori , (K,) or fiY A^amoriY , speaking of a man, (S, O,) i. q. qal~abotuhu [meaning I employed him to act in whatsoever way he pleased, according to his own judgment or discretion or free will, or I made him a free agent, in the disposal, or management, of the affair, or my affair: or (assumed tropical:) I made him, or employed him, to practise versatility, or to use art or artifice or cunning, in the affair, or in my affair; for the quasi-pass., tSr~f , is said to be from AlS~arofu as signifying AlHiylapu , and is expl. as syn. with AiHotaAla : but the former meaning is the more common: and it is also used as meaning simply I employed him in the managing of the affair, or my affair ]. (K.) ― -b7- [Hence also, Sr~f Alfarasa He exercised the horse. ] -A2- Sr~f Al$~araAba : and Sr~f Alxamora : see 1, latter half.

sourceDefinition: [as an inf. n.: see 1]. ― -b2- Used as a subst., The evil accidents, mishaps, or calamities, of time, or fortune; [thus expl. as having a pl. signification;] Sarofu Ald~ahori meaning HadavaAnuhu , (S, M, O, K,) and nawaAy^ibuhu , (S, O, K,) or HawaAdivuhu ; (Msb;) because it [i. e. time, or fortune,] turns things from their way, or course: (M:) [but it seems to be more properly rendered the shifting of fortune, or its shifting about; and to be an inf. n. sometimes used as a simple subst., and therefore having a pl., for] its pl. is SuruwfN . (M, Msb.) In the phrase qado $aHaTato Sarofu nawaAhaA , in a verse of Sakhr-el-Ghei, [ISd says,] he has made it fem. because of its dependance upon Aln~awaY [which is fem.; as though the meaning were The afflictions that are the consequence of the course taken by her in her journey have exceeded the bounds of moderation ]: (M:) [or it is here made fem. because having the signification of a broken pl., which is fem.:] or the meaning is, qado baEudato taSar~ufu wajohihaA Al~a*iY A^axa*ato fiyhi [i. e. the shiftingabout of her course that she has taken has become far-extending; Sarof being thus used as an inf. n.; for the Arabs sometimes make the inf. n. fem., saying A^awojaEatoniY Darobuka as well as A^awojaEaniY Darobuka ; (see EM p. 157;) and this I think the most preferable explanation]. (Skr in his Expos. of the Poems of the Hudhalees, p. 14 of the vol. edited by Kosegarten.) ― -b3- Also Repentance. (S, M, O, Msb, K.) [See a phrase below, in which this and other meanings are assigned to it.] ― -b4- And (tropical:) Art, artifice, or cunning. (Yoo, S, M, O, K, TA.) Hence, in the Kur [xxv. 20], famaA= yasotaTiyEuwna SarofFA walaA naSorFA (tropical:) [ And they are not able to put in practice art or artifice or cunning, nor aid ]: (S, TA:) or this means and they are not able to avert, or repel, from themselves punishment, (O, K, TA,) nor to aid themselves. (O, TA.) ― -b5- And Excellence, or superiority, of a dirhem, (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) and of a deenár, (M,) over another, (S, M, &c.,) in goodness, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or in value; (M, Mgh, O, K;) as in the saying, bayona Ald~irohamayoni SarofN [ Between the two dirhems is a difference of excellence ], because of the [superior] goodness of the silver of one of them: (S:) and in like manner, of speech; (O, K;) as in the saying fulaAnN laA yaEorifu Sarofa AlkalaAmi Such a one knows not the excellence of speech over other speech: (O:) and [in like manner] one says, lih`*aA EalaY h`*aA SarofN There is, or pertains, to this, an excess, and an excellence, over this; for when one is judged to excel, it, or he, is turned aside from its, or his, likes, or fellows. (O, K. *) ― -b6- And The night; and the day: (K:) [because of their interchanging:] AlS~arofaAni signifies the night and the day; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ AlS~irofaAni ; (K;) the latter accord. to Ibn-'Abbád; (O;) like AlS~iroEaAni , with kesr also [as well as with fet-h]. (TA.) ― -b7- In the saying (S, M, O, Msb) of the Arabs, (M,) or of the Prophet, (O, Msb,) in a certain trad., (K,) laA yuqobalu minohu SarofN walaA EadolN [ Neither Sarof nor Eadol shall be accepted from him ], (S, M, * O, Msb, *) by Sarof is meant repentance; (S, M, O, Msb, K;) and by Eadol , ransom: (M, Msb, K:) or by the former, art, or artifice, or cunning; (Yoo, S, M, O, K;) and by the latter, ransom: (M:) or by the former, acquisition of gain; and by the latter, ransom: (K:) or by the former, a supererogatory act; (A'Obeyd, M, O, K;) and by the latter, an obligatory act: (A'Obeyd, M, K:) or vice versâ: (K:) or by the former, weight; and by the latter, measure: (M, O, K:) or by the former, deviation; and by the latter, a right, or direct, course: (IAar, M:) or by the former, maA yutaSar~afu fiyhi [app. meaning an evasive artifice ]; and by the latter, a like: (Th, M:) or by the former, value, or price; and by the latter, a like; the saying originally relating to the bloodwit ( Ald~iyap ): one says, lamo yaqobaluwA minohumo SarofFA walaA EadolFA , i. e. They did not accept from them a bloodwit, nor did they slay one man for him, of their people, who had been slain; but they required from them more than that; for the Arabs used [often] to slay two men, and three, for one man; when they slew a man for a man, that was AlEadol with them; and when they took a bloodwit, having turned from the blood to another thing, that was Sarof , i. e. the value, or price, was Sarof : then the saying was applied in relation to anything, so as to be proverbially used in the case of him who was to render more than was incumbent on him: it has also been said that by Sarof is meant [in the saying cited above] something additional, or in excess; but this is nought. (M.)

definition: One of the Mansions of the Moon;
sourceDefinition: One of the Mansions of the Moon; [ the Twelfth Mansion; ] a single very bright star, [ β of Leo, ] (S, O, K, and Kzw in his Descr. of the Mansions of the Moon,) by which are some small evanescent stars; (Kzw;) over against, ( bitiloqaA=' , so in my copies of the S,) or following, (O, K and Kzw ubi suprà,) Alz~uborap ; (S, O, K, Kzw;) [i. e.] it is a single star behind the xaraAtaAni of the Lion; (M;) it is on the hinder part of the tail ( *anab ) of the Lion; [wherefore it is called by our astronomers Deneb; ] and is also called the qunob , which means the sheath of the penis, of the Lion: (Kzw in his Descr. of Leo: [in the S and O, erroneously, “ the qalob of the Lion: ”]) [ it rose aurorally, in Central Arabia, about the commencement of the era of the Flight, on the 8th of Sept., O. S.; and set aurorally on the 9th of March: ] Ibn-Kunáseh says, (M,) it is called AlS~arofapu because of the turning away of the cold (S, M, O, K) from the heat, (M,) and the coming of the heat, (S, O,) accord. to the [O and] K at its rising, but [as] IB says, correctly because of the turning away of the heat [at its rising], and the coming of the cold: (TA:) [i. e., correctly,] it is thus called because of the turning away of the cold at its setting in the early mornings, and the turning away of the heat at its rising from beneath the rays of the sun in the early mornings: (Kzw in his Descr. of Leo:) when it rises before the dawn, that is the beginning of autumn; and when it sets with the rising of the dawn, that is the beginning of spring. (M.) [Hence,] AlS~arofapu is [called] naAbu Ald~ahori Al~a*iY yufotar~u , (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K,) or naAbu Ald~ahori Al~a*iY yafotar~u Eanohu [ The dog-tooth of time, or fortune, which it shows smiling ]: for when AlSrfp rises, [a mistake for “ sets, aurorally, ”] the blossoms come forth and the herbage attains its full height: (M and K in art. fr :) in the T it is said that AlS~arofap is called by the Arabs naAbu Ald~ahori [ the dog-tooth of time, or fortune, ] liA^an~ahu yafotar~u Eani Albarodi waEani AlHar~i fiY AlHaAlatayoni [i. e. because it smiles revealing (the advent of) the cold and (that of) the heat, in its two states (of auroral rising and setting)]. (TA.) -A2- SarofapN also signifies A certain kind of bead ( xarazapN ); (Lh, S, M, O, K;) mentioned among those by means of which men are captivated, or fascinated, or restrained by women from other women; (S, O, K; *) or by means of which men are conciliated, so as to be turned thereby from their ways of acting or conduct or the like. (Lh, M.) -A3- And A bow having upon it a black mark or spot ( $aAmapN sawodaA='u ), the arrows of which, when they are shot, will not hit the object of aim. (O, K.) -A4- And one says, Halabotu Aln~aAqapa SarofapF , meaning I milked the she-camel in the early morning, between dawn and sunrise, and then left her until the like time of the morrow. (O, K. *)

S.; and set aurorally on the 9th of March: ] Ibn-Kunáseh says, (M,) it is called AlS~arofapu because of the turning away of the cold (S, M, O, K) from the heat, (M,) and the coming of the heat, (S, O,) accord. to the [O and] K at its rising, but [as] IB says, correctly because of the turning away of the heat [at its rising], and the coming of the cold: (TA:) [i. e., correctly,] it is thus called because of the turning away of the cold at its setting in the early mornings, and the turning away of the heat at its rising from beneath the rays of the sun in the early mornings: (Kzw in his Descr. of Leo:) when it rises before the dawn, that is the beginning of autumn; and when it sets with the rising of the dawn, that is the beginning of spring. sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) and Samima , which is extr., (M, K,) [first pers. of each Samimotu ,] aor. yaSam~u , (M, Msb, K,) inf. n. SamamN (S, * M, Msb, K) and Sam~N ; (M, K;) and ↓ A^aSam~a ; (S, M, Msb, K;) He was, or became, deaf; (M, * Msb, K; *) [or] he had a stoppage of the ear, and a heaviness of hearing. (M, K.) And Sam~ati AlA^u*unu , aor. as above, inf. n. SamamN , The ear was, or became, deaf. (Msb.) ― -b2- [And He was, or became, as though he heard not. ] One says, Sam~a Eanohu (assumed tropical:) [ He was as though he heard not him, or it; he was deaf to him, or it ]; (M;) and Eanohu ↓ A^aSam~a [meaning the same]. (S, M.) ― -b3- [Hence Sam~a signifies also (assumed tropical:) He or it, uttered, or made, no sound or noise; like him who, not hearing, returns no reply to a call or question; (assumed tropical:) was dumb, or mute. ] One says, Sam~ato HaSaApN bidamK (tropical:) [ A pebble made no sound in falling upon the ground by reason of blood ]; i. e. the blood was so copious that if one threw a pebble into it no sound would be heard in consequence thereof, (As, S, M, Meyd, K, TA,) because it would not fall upon the ground: (As, S, Meyd:) the saying is a prov. (Meyd.) And hence the saying of Imra-el-Keys, Sm~iY A@bonapa Aljabali , (S, K,) in the following verse: bud~ilotu mino waAy^ilK wakinodapa Eado waAna wafahomFA Sam~iY A@bonapa Aljabali (assumed tropical:) [ I have been given in exchange, for Wáïl and Kindeh,' Adwán and Fahm: make no sound, O pebble: app. meaning that he would shed much blood]: (S, TA: but this verse is omitted in one of my two copies of the S:) or the meaning is, O echo; (S, M, Meyd, K;) so they assert: (AHeyth, TA:) or O calamity; the saying being a prov.; (Meyd, TA;) applied to the case of a severe calamity; as though meaning be dumb, O calamity; said by As to be applied in relation to an event deemed excessively foul or evil: (TA:) or O serpent; (Meyd, TA;) which is said to be the primary meaning: (Meyd:) or O rock. (A Heyth, K, TA. [See also the second of the sentences here following.]) One says also, Sam~a SadaAhu (tropical:) [ His echo became dumb, or may his echo become dumb; ] meaning he perished, or may he perish. (S, K, TA.) And ↓ Sam~iY SamaAmi [in the CK erroneously written Sum~iY ] meaning (tropical:) Increase, O calamity: (S, K, TA:) or it is applied to a man who brings to pass a calamity, and means be dumb, O calamity: (TA:) or SamaAmi means calamity, and war; but primarily, the serpent; and this saying, like Sam~iY A@bonapa Aljabali , is a prov. said when two parties refuse to make peace, and persist in opposition; meaning answer not the charmer, O serpent, but continue as thou art wont to be. (Meyd.) ― -b4- SamamN in relation to stones, (Lth, TA,) or stone, (M,) [app. as an inf. n.,] signifies The being hard [ and solid (see A^aSam~u )]; or [as a simple subst.] hardness [ and solidity ]: (Lth, M, TA:) and in relation to a spear-shaft, the being compact; or compactness. (M.) One says, Sam~a AlHajaru , inf. n. SamamN , The stone was hard [ and solid ]. (MA.) And Sam~ati Alfitonapu , meaning [ The trial, or civil war, &c.,] was, or became, hard, vehement, or severe. (Msb.) -A2- Sam~a AlqaAruwrapa , (S, K,) or Sam~N raA^osa AlqaAruwrapi , (M,) aor. , (PS, [in a copy of the M , contr. to a general rule in the case of a trans. verb of this class, and app. a mistranscription,]) inf. n. Sam~N , (M,) He stopped the flask or bottle [app. with a SamaAm ]: (S, K:) or he stopped the head of the flask or bottle, and bound it; as also ↓ ASm~hu : (K:) or ASm~ AlqaAruwrapa signifies he put a SimaAm to the flask or bottle. (S, K.) ― -b2- And Sam~a AljuroHa , aor. , inf. n. Sam~N , He bound the wound, and put upon it a bandage with medicament. (M.) ― -b3- And Sam~ahu , (S, M, K) inf. n. Sam~N , (M,) He struck him, (S, K,) or it, i. e. his head, (M,) with a staff, or stick, (S, M,) and with a stone, (S, M, K,) and with the like thereof. (M.) And Sum~a , with damm, He was struck vehemently. (IAar, TA.)

definition: , said of a sword, (S, M, K, TA,) accord.
sourceDefinition: , said of a sword, (S, M, K, TA,) accord. to the K, signifies It struck the joint, and cut, or severed, it: or i. q. Tab~aqa : but this is at variance with what is said by J and other leading authorities; which is as follows: (TA:) it penetrated into the bone, and cut, or severed, it; but when it strikes the joint, and cuts, or severs, it, one says Tab~aqa ; a poet says, describing a sword, yuSam~imu A^aHoyaAnFA waHiynFA yuTab~iqu [ It penetrates into the bone, &c., sometimes, and at one time it strikes the joint, &c.]: (S, TA:) or it passed into the bones: (M:) and ↓ SamoSama , said of a sword, signifies the same: (M, TA:) or taSomiymN signifies a sword's penetrating into that which is struck with it without its causing any sound to be heard; from AlS~amamu in the ear. (Ham p. 326.) ― -b2- And hence taSomiymN signifies also (tropical:) A man's keeping constantly, or perseveringly, to the thing that he purposes, until he attains [ it ]. (Ham ubi suprà.) One says, Sam~ama EalaY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) He kept constantly, or perseveringly, to his opinion in respect of such a thing, after his desiring to do it. (IDrd, TA.) ― -b3- And Sm~m , (S, Msb, K, TA,) inf. n. taSomiymN , (M, K,) (tropical:) He acted, or went on, with penetrative energy, or with sharpness, vigorousness, and effectiveness, (S, M, Msb, K, TA,) in an affair, (M, Msb, K, TA,) and in journeying, (S, K, TA,) in this case said of a horse, (Z, TA,) and in other things; (S;) as also ↓ SamoSama . (K.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) He bit, and infixed his canine teeth, (S, K, TA,) and did not let go what he bit: (S, TA:) or Sm~m fiY EaD~atihi he infixed his teeth [or canine teeth ] in his bite. (A, TA.) ― -b5- And Sm~m Alfarasa AlEalafa (tropical:) He (a man) enabled the horse to take of the fodder to such a degree that fat and repletion stuffed him. (K, * TA.) ― -b6- And Sm~m SaAHibahu AlHadiyva (tropical:) He made his companion to retain the narrative, or story, in his memory. (K, * TA.) ― -b7- See also the next paragraph.

definition: applied to any animal, (Mgh,) Deaf;
sourceDefinition: applied to any animal, (Mgh,) Deaf; (S, * M, * Mgh, Msb, K; *) [or] having a stoppage of the ear, and a heaviness of hearing; (M, K:) fem. Sam~aA='u : (Mgh, Msb:) pl. Sum~N (M, Msb, K) and Sum~aAnN . (M, K.) A poet says, A^aSam~u Eam~aA saA='ahu samiyEu (TA,) a prov., (Meyd,) meaning Feigning himself deaf to that which displeases him, (Meyd, TA,) i. e. to what is foul, (Meyd,) as though he heard it not, (TA,) but hearing (Meyd, TA) that which pleases him, i. e. what is good; as does the generous man. (Meyd.) And similar is the saying, waliY A^u*onN Eani AlfaHo$aA='i Sam~aA [ And I have an ear deaf to that which is foul ]. (TA.) [See also Ham p. 636, for another similar ex.] One says likewise, daEaAhu daEowapa AlA^aSam~i (assumed tropical:) He called him [ with the call of the deaf, meaning,] with extraordinary force. (TA.) And Darabahu Daroba AlA^aSam~i (tropical:) He beat him [ with the beating of the deaf, meaning,] uninterruptedly and excessively; because the deaf, when he does thus, [not hearing any cry,] imagines that he is falling short of what he should do, and therefore will not leave off. (TA.) And lamaEa bivawobihi lamoEa AlA^aSam~i (assumed tropical:) He (one warning a people from afar) made a sign by waving his garment continually, as does the deaf; as though he heard not the reply. (TA.) And Hay~apN A^aSam~u (M, K, TA) and Sam~aA='u (TA) (tropical:) A serpent that will not accept charming; (M, K, TA;) as though it heard it not; (M;) that will not obey the charmer: (TA:) and [in like manner] the epithet Sum~N is applied to scorpions. (M.) And rajulN A^aSam~u (tropical:) A man whom one does not hope to win over, and who will not be turned back from the object of his desire; (M, K, TA;) as though he were called and would not hear. (M, TA.) And dahorN A^aSam~u (assumed tropical:) [ Inexorable fortune; ] as though one complained to it and it would not hear. (M.) And AlS~am~aA='u and daAhiyapN Sam~aA='u as expl. voce SamaAmi , q. v. And fitonapN Sam~aA='u (assumed tropical:) A sedition, or the like, that is severe, or hard to be borne; (S, Msb;) to the allaying of which there is no way; because of its having gone to the utmost extent. (TA. [See also A^abokamu .]) And A^amorN A^aSam~u (assumed tropical:) An affair, or event, that is severe, or hard to be borne. (TA.) And SamamN is tropically attributed to AlHilom : (M:) a poet, cited by Th, says, qulo maA badaA laka mino zuwrK wamino ka*ibK HilomiY A^aSam~u waA^u*oniY gayoru Sam~aA='i (tropical:) [the last word I find written thus, app. for the sake of the rhyme: i. e. Say what occurs to thee, of falsehood and of lying: my forbearance is deaf, i. e. insensible, to it, though my ear is not deaf ]. (M, TA.) Sam~aA='u is applied to a qaTaAp [or bird of the species termed qaTFA , and may in this case be rendered (assumed tropical:) Small-eared, or dull-eared, being applied thereto] because of the sakak [i. e. smallness &c.] of its ear or because it is deaf when thirsting. (M.) And AlA^aSam~u [as though meaning (tropical:) The deafmute ] is an epithet applied to rajab , (S, M, Msb, K,) the month thus named, (Msb,) which the people of the Time of Ignorance called $ahoru A@ll~`hi AlA^aSam~u , (Kh, S,) because the cry of the caller for aid was not heard in it, (Kh, S, M, Msb, K, *) shouting yaA lafulaAnK and yaA SabaAHaAho , (M, K,) nor the commotion of fight, (Kh, S, Msb,) nor the clash of arms, it being one of the sacred months: (Kh, S:) thus applied it is tropical, like naAy^imN in the phrase layolN naAy^imN ; as though, in it, the man were deaf to the sound of arms: (TA:) and in like manner it is also called munoSilu AlA^al~i . (M. [See also AlA^aSab~u , and muHar~amN , and $ahorN .]) ― -b2- And [as that which is without a cavity is generally nonsonorous,] one says HajarN A^aSam~u meaning (tropical:) Hard (S, M, Msb, K) and solid (S, Msb, K) stone: (S, &c.:) and SaxorapN Sam~aA='u (tropical:) a hard and solid rock: (K, TA:) or this latter signifies (assumed tropical:) a rock in which is no crack nor hole: pl. Sum~N . (TA.) And qanaApN Sam~aA='u (assumed tropical:) A compact spear-shaft. (M.) ― -b3- AlS~am~aA='u also signifies (assumed tropical:) The earth, or ground. (M:) And A^aroDN Sam~aA='u (assumed tropical:) Rugged ground: pl. Sum~N . (K.) ― -b4- Also [app. (assumed tropical:) The vermiform appendage of the cœcum; ] the thin, or slender, extremity of the Efjp : (K: [the last word in this explanation is thus, without any syll. signs, in my MS. copy of the K and in the TA: in the CK, Eafijap : but the right reading is evidently Eifajap , which is said in the TA, in art. Efj , to be, like A^aEofaAjN , a pl. of EafajN and its dial. vars.: see this last word:] thus called [in my opinion because resembling a meatus auditorius that is closed, and therefore deaf; though said to be so called] because of its hardness. (TA.) ― -b5- And naAqapN Sam~aA='u (tropical:) A fat she-camel: (K, TA:) and, (K,) or as some say, (TA,) one that has just conceived, or become pregnant. (K, TA.) ― -b6- Ai$otimaAlu AlS~am~aA='i , (S, Msb, K, TA,) which is forbidden in a trad., (TA,) is (assumed tropical:) The covering oneself with his garment, like [ as is done in the case of ] the $imolap of the Arabs of the desert with their [ garments called ] A^akosiyap [pl. of kisaA=' ]; (A'Obeyd, S;) i. e. the turning the kisaA=' , from the direction of one's right, upon his left arm and the part between his left shoulderjoint and neck, and then turning it a second time, from behind him, upon his right arm and the part between his right shoulder-joint and neck, so as to cover them both: (A'Obeyd, S, K:) or the wrapping oneself with the garment without making to it a place from which to put forth the hand: (Msb:) or, (K,) as the lawyers explain it, (A'Obeyd, S,) it is the wrapping one's body and arms with one garment, not having upon him another, and then raising it [in the K, as is said in the TA, yaDaEuhu is erroneously put for yarofaEuhu ] on one of its sides, and putting it upon his shoulder, so that his pudendum appears from it: (A'Obeyd, S, K:) [but] with the Arabs, libosapu AlS~am~aA='i means the covering one's whole body with his garment, and not raising a side from which to put forth his hand: (Mgh:) when you say, of a man, Ai$otamala AlS~am~aA='a , it is as though you said, Ai$otamala Al$~imolapa AlS~am~aA='a ; for AlS~am~aA=' is a sort of Ai$otimaAl . (S. [See also Ai$otamala , and Al$~imolapu AlS~am~aA='u , in art. $ml .]) ― -b7- ja*orN A^aSam~u (assumed tropical:) A surd, or an irrational, root, in arithmetic; which is known only to God, accord. to a saying of 'Áïsheh: opposed to ja*orN naATiqN . (Mgh in art. j*r .) ― -b8- [ fiEolN A^aSam~u A surd verb is a term sometimes used in grammar, as meaning a triliteral-radical verb of the class commonly called muDaAEafN of which the second and third radicals are the same letter. ]

definition: The fifteenth letter of the alphabet: called DaAdN : it is one of the letters termed majohuwrap [or vocal, i.
sourceDefinition: The fifteenth letter of the alphabet: called DaAdN : it is one of the letters termed majohuwrap [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, and not with the breath only]; (TA;) and of the letters termed $ajoriy~ap , ('Eyn, Mgh, TA,) from Al$~ajoru , which is the place of the opening of the mouth: ('Eyn, Mgh, TA on the letter j :) its place of utterance is from the extremity of the tongue [extended so as to reach] to the part next to the [lateral teeth called] A^aDoraAs ; and it is more usually pronounced from the left side than from the right: the vulgar [sometimes] pronounce it as ZaA=' , making its place of utterance to be between the extremity of the tongue and the central incisors, which pronunciation is peculiar to a dialect, as mentioned by Fr on the authority of El-Fadl: he says [also] that some of the Arabs substitute it for ZaA=' , saying Dahor for Zahor ; but that the doing thus, though allowable in speech, is not allowable in the reciting of the Book of God, which follows the rule, or usage, of the Prophet: (Msb in art. Dwd :) or its place of utterance is from the foremost part of the edge of the tongue and the part next to the ADrAs ; and it has no sister [or analogue] accord. to Sb; but accord. to the 'Eyn, it is a sister of * and v , and these three letters are termed livawiy~ap [or gingival], because proceeding from the gum; the substitution of any of these, however, for another of them, vitiates prayers: (Mgh:) it is of the class termed AlHuruwfu AlmusotaEoliyapu : (L in art. Dwd :) and is a letter peculiar to the Arabs, (L and K in that art.,) accord. to the general and correct opinion; (TA in that art.;) [whence the saying of Mohammad, A^anaA A^afoSaHu mano naTaqa biAlD~aAdi I am the most chaste in speech of those who have pronounced the letter dád; i. e., of the Arabs, agreeably with another saying, ascribed to him, mentioned voce bayoda ;] or it is a letter rarely occurring in the language of any other people. (L in that art.) ― -b2- It is always a radical letter; and is [said to be] not substituted for another letter; (L in art. Dwd ;) [but it is so substituted in some cases of A_idogaAm , as, for instance, for the l of the article Al , and in yaD~ar~aEu for yataDar~aEu , and the like; and] it is sometimes substituted for S , as in maD~a Alr~um~aAnapa for maS~ahaA , as Ibn-Osfoor says, and Ks mentions manaADN for manaASN ; (TA;) and also for l , as Ibn-Málik says in the Tes-heel, an instance of which is rajulN jaDodN for jalodN , mentioned by J; (MF, TA;) and sometimes it is changed into l , as in the instance of AiloTajaEa for AiDoTajaEa . (S and L &c. in art. DjE .) -A2- [As a numeral, it denotes Eight hundred. ]

sourceDefinition: (As, S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ DaforN , (S, M, A, Mgh, K,) the latter an inf. n. used as a subst. [properly so termed], (Mgh,) A single lock of hair: (M, Msb, K:) and (Msb) a [ lock of hair such as is termed ] *uw^aAbap , (Mgh, Msb,) or jamiyrap and gadiyrap , of a woman: (As, TA:) or a plaited, braided, or interwoven, *w^Abp : (A, TA;) or [ a plait of hair ] consisting of three, or more, distinct portions: (Msb:) or i. q. EaqiySapN [q. v.]: one says lahaA DafiyrataAni , and ↓ DaforaAni , meaning EaqiySataAni : (Yaakoob, S:) or the DafiyrataAni pertain to a man, not to a woman; [though such is not the case accord. to modern usage;] and gadaAy^ir , [pl. of gadiyrapN ,] to women; and these are maDofuwrap [i. e. plaited]: (AZ, TA:) the pl. of DafiyrapN is DafaAy^iru (A, Msb) and DufurN ; (Msb;) and the pl. of ↓ DaforN is DufuwrN . (A.) ― -b2- See also DaforN , in two places. ― -b3- DafiyrapN also signifies (tropical:) A dam, (IAar, S, A, Mgh, Msb,) extending in an oblong form upon the ground, having in it wood and stones. (IAar, TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) A plain, or soft, tract of land, oblong, producing herbage or the like, extending [ to the distance of the journey of ] a day, or two days. (TA.) ― -b5- See also DafiyrN .

definition: , (S, Msb, K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. muDaAhaApN , (S, Msb,) He resembled, or conformed with, him, or it; syn. $aAkalahu ; (S, Msb, K;) like DaAhaA^ahu [q. v.]: (S, Msb:) and, like the latter, he imitated him. (Msb, TA. *) It is said in a trad., A^a$ad~u Aln~aAsi Ea*aAbFA yawoma AlqiyaAmapi Al~a*iyn yuDaAhuwna xaloqa A@ll~`hi i. e. [ The most severely punished of mankind on the day of resurrection will be ] those who imitate by what they make [ the creation of God ]; meaning the sculptors or limners or the like. (Msb.) ― -b2- Also, [or DaAhaY bihi , like DaAhaA^a bh , q. v.,] He was, or became, gentle, tender, or courteous, or he acted, or behaved, gently, &c., with him, or to him; namely, a man, and other than a man. (TA.)

definition: A woman that does not menstruate: pl.
sourceDefinition: A woman that does not menstruate: pl. DuhoYN ; which necessarily implies that the former is [as above, i. e.] with the long A : but AA mentions ↓ DahoyaApN and ↓ DahoyaAhN , with p and with h , as having this meaning; which necessarily implies that DhyA is with the short A [i. e., accord. to a general rule, ↓ DahoyFA , with tenween, like DahoyaA^N , q. v. in art. DhyA^ , though (accord. to a general rule) this should be regarded as a masc. epithet]: (S) or DahoyaA='u , and also with the short A [app. ↓ DahoyFA , as above, not DahoyaA , or, as I rather incline to think, DahoyaA^N (which is mentioned in art. DhyA^ ) may be here meant], signify a woman that does not menstruate nor become pregnant; (K, TA;) so that she is as though she resembled a man: (TA: [see 3:]) or that menstruates but does not become pregnant: (K, TA:) or that does not bring forth, though she menstruate: (TA:) or whose breasts do not grow forth; (K, TA;) and when this is the case, she does not menstruate: or the former signifies that does not menstruate, being pregnant. (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) Land that does not give growth to anything; as also with the short A [i. e. ↓ DahoyFA or DahoyaA^N ]. (K. [In the TA this meaning is restricted, app. without reason, to the form with the short A .]) -A2- Also, (S, K,) and with the short A [i. e. ↓ DahoyFA or DahoyaA^N ], (K,) A species of tree (S, K) of the kind called EiDaAh , (K,) having a baramap [q. v.] and a pod ( Eul~afap ) [ which succeeds the baramap ], and many thorns. (TA. [For further descriptions thereof, see DahoyaA^N , in art. DhyA^ .])

definition: is said by some to be originally [ AiTomaAn~a ] like AiHomaAr~a , (Msb,) as Esh-Shiháb states in the Expos.
sourceDefinition: is said by some to be originally [ AiTomaAn~a ] like AiHomaAr~a , (Msb,) as Esh-Shiháb states in the Expos. of the Shifè, (TA,) and to be pronounced with ' for the purpose of avoiding [the combination of] the two quiescent letters, (Msb, TA,) anomalously: (Msb:) and some say that it is originally AiToA^aman~a , (Msb, TA,) because you say TaA^omana Alr~ajulu Zahorahu , with ' , (Msb,) or, as Suh says, in the R, because it is from taTA^omana , the m being put before the ' in order to render the word more easy of pronunciation, (TA,) therefore it is anomalous; (Msb;) Sb [likewise] held it to be formed by transposition, and derived from TaA^omana ; but AA held the contrary to be the case. (TA.) ― -b2- You say, AiTomaA^an~ati AlA^aroDu , and ↓ taTaAmanat [or ↓ taTaA^omanat ], meaning The land, or ground, was, or became, low, or depressed. (TA.) ― -b3- See also Q. Q. 2. ― -b4- ATmA^n~ , (S, Mgh, K,) inf. n. AiTomiy^onaAnN and TumaA^oniynapN , (S, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Mgh, Msb,) signifies [also] He (a man, S) was, or became, still, in a state of rest or ease, quiet, or calm; syn. sakana ; (S, Mgh;) as also AiTobaA^an~a , which is formed by permutation. (S.) And thus it signifies as said of the heart, i. e. It was, or became, still, in a state of rest or ease, quiet, calm, tranquil, unruffled, or free from disquietude. (Msb.) Thus too in the saying, ATmA^n A_ilaY ka*aA , i. e. (tropical:) He trusted to such a thing, or relied upon it, so as to become at rest or ease, or quiet, in mind. (K, * TA.) And one says also, ATmA^n~ jaAlisFA [ He became still, or at rest, or at ease, sitting ]: (TA:) and ATmA^n~ binaA Aljuluwsu [lit. The sitting became still, or free from disquiet, with us ]; meaning AisotaqoraronaA wasakan~aA fiY Aljuluwsi [i. e. we became settled, or at rest or ease, and still, in the sitting; or became seated at ease ]. (Har p. 280.) And ATmA^n~ biAlmawoDiEi [ He settled in the place; i. e.] he remained, stayed, abode, or dwelt, in the place, and took it as his home. (Msb.) And ATmA^n~ Eam~aA kaAna yafoEaluhu (assumed tropical:) [ He became at rest from that which he was doing; ] i. e. he desisted from that which he was doing. (TA.) And ↓ fiyhi taTaAmunN [or ↓ taTaA^omunN ] In him is quietness, calmness, or sedateness. (TA.)

definition: He caused him, or it, to perish, or come to nought;
sourceDefinition: He caused him, or it, to perish, or come to nought; as also Tw~H bihi , (A,) and Ty~Hhu ; (A, and K in art. TyH ;) and ↓ ATAHhu signifies the same, (IAar, K,) said of a thing, (K,) or of property, (IAar, and K in art. TyH ,) as is also Tw~Hhu , (IAar,) and he made it pass away. (K.) And He sent him to a land from which he should not return. (K.) And Tw~H bivawobihi He cast his garment [app. meaning himself (see a verse of Esh-Shemmákh, or of Leylà, cited voce vwb )] into a place of destruction; as also Ty~H bh . (L, and K in art. TyH .) And ↓ Taw~aHatohu AlT~waAy^iHu i. q. qa*afatohu AlqawaA*ifu (S, K) i. e. Accidents, or events, that cast into places of perdition [ cast him thereinto ]: (MF, * TK:) one should not say AlmuTaw~iHaAtu : it is an extr. phrase, (S, K,) like the phrase in the Kur [xv. 22], waA^arosalonaA Alr~iyaAHa lawaAqiHa accord. to one of the two interpretations thereof: (S:) and AlmaTaAwiHu ↓ A^aTaAHatohu and AlT~awaAy^iHu signify the same, i. e. qa*afatohu AlqawaA*ifu ; (A;) or [rather] the former of these two phrases has a similar meaning [i. e. the places of perdition caused him to fall thereinto; unless maTaAwiHu have a signification which I do not find explained]. (TA.) And Tw~H bihi He incited him, induced him, or made him, to venture upon a desert in which perdition was to be feared. (K, * TA.) ― -b2- Also He, or it, caused him to lose his way, syn. taw~ahahu , (S, K,) and so bihi ↓ TAH , (Har p. 126,) and Ty~Hhu , (K in art. TyH ,) and carried him away hither and thither, (S,) or so that he cast himself hither and thither, (K, TA,) and so Tw~H bihi . (TA.) And Tw~H nafosahu He made himself to be, or become, confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course; like tuw~ahahaA and tay~ahahaA . (S in art. tyh .) ― -b3- Tw~H bihi also signifies He threw it, or cast it, in the air. (K, TA. [For AlhawaA=' , Golius and Freytag have read AlhawaY . See 5.]) ― -b4- And Tw~Hhu He beat him, or struck him, with a staff, or stick. (K.) -A2- Tw~H fiY AljibaAli He went round about much, or often, in the mountains; i. q. Taw~afa and Taw~ada . (S in art. Twd .)

definition: , of ground, or land, Such as is rugged, that will not show any foot-mark;
sourceDefinition: , of ground, or land, Such as is rugged, that will not show any foot-mark; (M;) as also ↓ ZalafN : (S, * M:) or so ↓ ZalifapN (S, K) and ↓ ZalufapN and ↓ ZalafapN : (K:) and ↓ ZalafN signifies ground such as horses like to run upon: (T:) or (i. e. the last) a place elevated above the water and the mud; and so ↓ ZalifN ; (K;) this last thus expl. by Ibn-'Abbád: (O:) or this last and ↓ ZalifapN , accord. to ISh, (TA,) or ↓ ZalafN and ↓ ZalafapN , (so accord. to a copy of the T, in which the authority is not mentioned,) signify ground, or land, in which the foot-mark will not appear, and which is high and rugged: and accord. to Fr, ↓ ZalifN and ↓ ZalifapN signify ground, or land, that will not show a foot-mark; as though it were prevented from doing so: (T, TA:) and ↓ ZilofN , (so in a copy of the T,) or ↓ ZalifN , (so in the TA,) accord. to Fr, signifies such as is soft, of ground, or land: but accord. to IAar, such as is hard, and does not show a foot-mark; in which is no softness, so as to be difficult to him who walks upon it; nor sand, so that the camels would have their feet burnt upon it; nor stones, so that they would be chafed, or abraded, in the soles of their feet, upon it: and it is also expl. (by IAar, TA) as meaning such as is rugged and hard, of ground, or land: (T, TA:) and ↓ ZalifapN signifies high ground, or land, that will not show a foot-mark. (M.) [See also ZaliyfN .] ― -b2- [In the CK, AlZ~alofu is erroneously put for AlZ~alafu as relating to the means of subsistence.] -A2- ZalofN also signifies Ineffectual, null, or void: and allowable. (AA, T, S, M, O, K.)

definition: The Zufor [meaning cloven hoof ] of any ruminant (T, M) of the bovine kind and the like;
sourceDefinition: The Zufor [meaning cloven hoof ] of any ruminant (T, M) of the bovine kind and the like; (T;) [i. e.] it is an appertenance of the bovine kind and of the sheep and goat (S, O, Msb, K) and of the gazelle or antelope (S, O, K) and the like, (O, Msb, K,) which is to them like the Zufor to man, (Msb,) or like the qadam to us: (K:) one says the rijol and qadam of a man, and the HaAfir of a horse, and the xuf~ of a camel and of an ostrich, and the Zilof of a bovine animal and of a sheep or goat [and the like]: (ISk, T, TA:) pl. A^aZolaAfN (S, M, O, Msb, K) and ZuluwfN : (S, O, K:) and A^aZolaAf is applied, by 'Amr Ibn-Maadee-kerib, to the hoofs of horses, (S, M, O,) as is said by Lth and Az and IF, by poetic license, (O,) metaphorically: (S, O:) and by El-Akhtal, metaphorically, to the feet of men. (M, IB, TA.) [Its dual is used in the K, in explanations of the words $aEirapN and A^a$oEaru , in the latter instance on the authority of Lh, as meaning The two halves of a cloven hoof. ] And one says, maA ja$imotu A_ilayoka ZilofFA [app. meaning I have not had the trouble of bringing to thee so much as the hoof of a gazelle or the like ]. (AZ, TA in art. j$m , q. v.) And huwa yaA^okuluhu biDirosK wayaTaw^uhu biZilofK [ He eats it with a lateral tooth, and treads it with a cloven hoof; app. meaning, vehemently ]. (TA.) ― -b2- It is sometimes used as meaning (tropical:) Cloven-hoofed animals. (TA.) One says, maA lahu xuf~N walaA HaAfirN walaA ZilofN (tropical:) [ He possesses not camels, nor horses or asses or mules, nor sheep or goats or other cloven-hoofed beasts ]. (TA in art. xf .) ― -b3- It also signifies [or implies] The making consecutive progressions in walking and in other actions, (T, K,) or, accord. to the L, in a thing. (TA.) One says, jaA='ati AlA_ibilu EalaY ZilofK waAHidK (T, A, O, TA) i. e. The camels came following one another. (A, TA. [See also a similar phrase voce xuf~N .]) And ganamu fulaAnK ZilofK waAHidK and waAHidK ↓ ZalafK The sheep, or goats, of such a one, have all of them brought forth [app. one after another ]. (M.) ― -b4- Also A thing that is suitable to the requirements of a man, and of a beast: (M:) and an object of desire: (M, O, K:) and an object of want. (T, K.) One says, A^aSaAba fulaAnN Zilofahu Such a one attained what was suitable to his requirements, and what he desired: and sometimes one says the like of any beast that finds, or lights on, or meets with, that which he likes. (M.) wajadati Ald~aAb~apu ZilofahaA is a prov., (M, O,) applied to him who finds the means of attaining that which he seeks; (Meyd;) meaning [ The beast found what was suitable to its requirements; or,] what withheld it [ from other things ] and prevented its desire [ thereof ]. (A, TA. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii. 807.]) And one says, wajadati Al$~aApu ZilofahaA The sheep, or goat, found suitable pasturage, and therefore did not quit it: (K, TA:) a prov. mentioned by Fr; applied to him, of men and of beasts, that finds what is suitable to him. (TA.) And baladN mino Zilofi Alganami A country of such as are suitable to sheep or goats. (M.) And wajada Zilofahu He found what he loved, (O,) or what he desired, (K,) and what was suitable to him; (TA;) said of a man. (O.) And maA wajadotu Einodahu ZilofiY I did not find with him the object of my want. (TA.) -A2- See also ZalofN , near the middle of the paragraph. ― -b2- [In some copies of the K, AlZ~ilofu is erroneously put for AlZ~alafu as relating to the means of subsistence. And in the CK ZilofuhaA is erroneously put for ZalifuhaA as meaning Zalifu Aln~afosi .]

sourceDefinition: Clouds ( saHaAbN ) having thunder and lightning: (S, O, K:) or having thunder and lightning, without which they are not thus called, in which the lightning is in commotion, or flickering, and which overshadow and approach so as to become like a roof: (O, TA:) or of which the lightning does not cease: (Lh, TA:) and (K) that gleam, or glisten, much, (A, K,) with lightning: (A:) or that lighten at one time, and become concealed at another: (TA:) or which the wind carries to and fro. (O, TA.) ― -b2- Lightning in a state of commotion, or agitation; quivering; flickering; as also ↓ EariSN and ↓ EaroSN : (K:) or vehemently so, (IDrd, O, TA,) and vehement in its thunder: (TA:) or that gleams, or glistens, much: or that lightens at one time, and becomes unapparent at another; as also ↓ EariSN and ↓ EaroSN . (Ibn-'Abbád, O.) ― -b3- A pliant spear, (AA, S, O, K, TA,) that vibrates, or quivers, when shaken: (S, * O, * TA:) and so applied to a sword: (AA, S, O, K:) or, applied to a spear, it signifies of which, when it is shaken, the head glistens; from EariSa Albaroqu . (Ibn-'Abbád, O, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. Eiz~N (AZ, S, A, O, Msb, K) and Eiz~apN , (AZ, S, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) and EazaAzapN , (S, K,) He was, or became, mighty, potent, powerful, or strong; (TA, in explanation of Eiz~N ;) and so ↓ tEz~z ; or the latter signifies he made himself so; he strengthened himself; syn. taqaw~aY : (Msb:) and the former, he became so after being low, or mean, in condition; (AZ, S, A, K;) as also Eaz~a , sec. pers. Eazirota , aor. : (Msb:) he was, or became, high, or elevated, in rank, or condition, or state; noble, honourable, glorious, or illustrious; (S, * A, * K, * TK; and TA in explanation of Eiz~N ;) as also ↓ tEz~z . (S, * K, * TK.) [ Eaz~a wajal~a , referring to the name of God expressed or understood, is a phrase of frequent occurrence, meaning, To Him, or to Whom, belong might and majesty, or glory and greatness. ] ― -b2- You also say, Eazazotu Ealayohi , (S, O, K,) aor. ; (O, K,) meaning, karumotu Ealayohi , (S, O, K, *) i. e., I exceeded him in nobleness, or generosity. (TK.) ― -b3- And Eaz~a , [aor. , inf. n. Eiz~N and Eiz~apN and app. EazaAzapN also,] He magnified, or exalted, himself: (TA:) (assumed tropical:) he was disdainful, scornful, or indignant, in a blamable manner. (TA, in explanation of Eiz~apN ; q. v. infrà.) [See also 5.] ― -b4- He resisted, or withstood: (TA, in explanation of Eiz~N :) he was indomitable, invincible; not to be overcome. (B and TA, in explanation of Eiz~apN , q. v. infrà.) And Eaz~a Al$~aYo'u , aor. , The thing was, or became, [ difficult, or hard; as also ↓ AiEotaz~a , (occurring in the TA, coupled with taEas~ara , in an explanation of manuEa , in art. mnE ,) and ↓ tEz~z : and] impossible, insuperable, or unattainable: or so, as Es-Sarakustee says, ↓ tEz~z . (Msb.) ― -b5- And Eaz~a , (S, O, K,) aor. , inf. n. Eiz~N and Eiz~apN and EazaAzapN , (S, O,) It (a thing, S, O, K, meaning anything, TA) was, or became, rare, scarce, hardly to be found. (S, O, K.) ― -b6- [And hence, He, or it, was, or became, dear, highly esteemed, or greatly valued. .] ― -b7- Eaz~a EalaY~a A^ano tafoEala ka*aA , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. (Mgh, O, Msb, K) and (Fr, Mgh, O, K,) [the second pers. of the pret. being Eazazota and Eazizota ,] the latter aor. the more chaste, (O,) means Thy doing so distressed, or hath distressed, or afflicted, me; or, emphatically, distresses, or afflicts, me; syn. Ai$otad~a , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA,) and Haq~a , (S, O, K, TA,) and $aq~a : (TA:) a phrase [often, but not always,] alluding to a loathing of the action, or indignation thereat. (Msb.) In like manner also you say, Eaz~a EalaY~a ka*aA Such a thing distressed, or afflicted, me. (S.) And Eaz~a EalaY~a A^ano A^asuwo'aka It distressed, or afflicted, me to displease thee. (A.) And Eaz~a maA A^an~aka *aAhibN , like Haq~a A^an~aka *aAhibN [or Haq~a maA An~k *Ahb , meaning It is distressing that thou art going away ]. (TA.) And one says to a man, Dost thou love me? and he replies, laEaz~a maA , i. e., la$ad~a maA , (A, O, K,) and laHaq~a maA , (A, TA,) meaning It distresses me, what thou sayest; or it has distressed me. (TK.) You say also, bimaA A^aSaAbaka ↓ A^uEozizotu I was, or am, distressed by what befell, or hath befallen, thee. (S, O, K.) And EalaY~a bimaA A^uSibota bihi ↓ A^aEozizo That by which thou hast been afflicted distresses me: (S, O:) [or how doth it distress me! ] so in a trad. of 'Alee; when he beheld Talhah slain, he said, EalaY~a ↓ A^aEozizo A^abaA muHam~adK A^ano A^araAka mujad~alFA taHota nujuwmi Als~amaA='i [ It distresses me, or how doth it distress me! O Aboo-Mohammad, that I see thee prostrated upon the ground beneath the stars of heaven ]. (TA.) [A similar ex. is given in the A; without bi prefixed to A^ano .] -A2- Eaz~a also signifies He was, or became, weak: thus having two contr. meanings. (Msb.) -A3- Eaz~ahu , aor. , (S, A, O, K,) inf. n. Eaz~N , (S, O, TA,) He overcame him, or conquered him: (S, A, O:) he overcame him in argumentative contest; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ EazoEazahu , (K,) inf. n. EazoEazapN ; (TA;) and so Eaz~ahu fiY AlxiTaAbi : (Jel in xxxviii. 22, and TA:) or this last signifies he became stronger than he therein; (TA;) or he strove with him to overcome therein; as also fiyhi ↓ EAz~hu , (S, K,) inf. n. muEaAz~apN : (O, TA:) in the Kur xxxviii. 22, some read Eaz~aniY ; and others, ↓ EaAz~aniY : and you say, faEazazotuhu ↓ EaAz~aniY , meaning, he strove with me to overcome, and I overcame him: and muEaAz~apN signifies the contending together in argument: (TA:) you say also of a horse, faArisahu ↓ AEtz~ [ he overcame his rider, or gained the mastery over him ]. (S and K in art. jmE .) It is said in a prov., (S,) mano Eaz~a baz~a He who overcomes takes the spoil. (S, A, O, K.) And in another prov., (S,) A_i*aA Eaz~a A^axuwka fahuno (Th, S, O, K) When thy brother overcomes thee, and thou art not equal to him ( lamo tuqaAwmohu ) be thou gentle to him: (Az, O, K, TA:) or when thy brother magnifies and exalts himself against thee, abase thyself: (Th, TA:) or, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, what Th says is a mistake; the right reading being fahino , with kesr, and the meaning, when thy brother is hard, or severe, to thee, treat thou him with gentleness, or blandishment; not fahuno , with damm, which is from AlhawaAnu : but ISd approves and justifies the reading given by Th. (TA.) [See also 10.] -A4- Eaz~ahu . aor. , inf. n. Eaz~N , also signifies the same as Eaz~azahu (Msb, TA *) and A^aEaz~ahu , (TA,) in a sense pointed out below: see 2, in two places. (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] with the same aor. and inf. n., He aided, or helped, him. (IKtt, TA.) -A5- Eaz~a AlmaA='u , (O, K,) aor. , (O,) The water flowed. (O, K.) ― -b2- And Eaz~ati AlqaroHapu , (O, K,) aor. , (O,) The qrHp , [i. e. wound, or pustule, ] discharged what was in it. (O, K.) -A6- Eaz~ato , aor. , inf. n. EuzuwzN and EizaAzN ; (S, O, K;) and , (K,) accord. to IAar, (O,) Eazuzato , (O, K,) inf. n. EuzuwzN ; (O, TA;) She (a camel, IAar, S, O, K, and a ewe or goat, IAar, O) was narrow in the orifices of the teats; (S, O, * K;) as also ↓ AEz~t , (S, O, K,) and ↓ tEz~zt : (S, K:) or Eazuzato , [which is of a very uncommon form, (see dam~a , last sentence,)] she (a ewe, or goat,) became scant in her milk. (IKh, TA in art. lb .)

Eazirota , aor. : (Msb:) he was, or became, high, or elevated, in rank, or condition, or state; noble, honourable, glorious, or illustrious; (S, * A, * K, * TK; and TA in explanation of Eiz~N ;) as also ↓ tEz~z . (S, * K, * TK.) [ Eaz~a wajal~a , referring to the name of God expressed or understood, is a phrase of frequent occurrence, meaning, To Him, or to Whom, belong might and majesty, or glory and greatness. ] ― -b2- You also say, Eazazotu Ealayohi , (S, O, K,) aor. ; (O, K,) meaning, karumotu Ealayohi , (S, O, K, *) i. e., I exceeded him in nobleness, or generosity. (TK.) ― -b3- And Eaz~a , [aor. , inf. n. Eiz~N and Eiz~apN and app. EazaAzapN also,] He magnified, or exalted, himself: (TA:) (assumed tropical:) he was disdainful, scornful, or indignant, in a blamable manner. (TA, in explanation of Eiz~apN ; q. v. infrà.) [See also 5.] ― -b4- He resisted, or withstood: (TA, in explanation of Eiz~N :) he was indomitable, invincible; not to be overcome. (B and TA, in explanation of Eiz~apN , q. v. infrà.) And Eaz~a Al$~aYo'u , aor. , The thing was, or became, [ difficult, or hard; as also ↓ AiEotaz~a , (occurring in the TA, coupled with taEas~ara , in an explanation of manuEa , in art. mnE ,) and ↓ tEz~z : and] impossible, insuperable, or unattainable: or so, as Es-Sarakustee says, ↓ tEz~z . (Msb.) ― -b5- And Eaz~a , (S, O, K,) aor. , inf. n. Eiz~N and Eiz~apN and EazaAzapN , (S, O,) It (a thing, S, O, K, meaning anything, TA) was, or became, rare, scarce, hardly to be found. (S, O, K.) ― -b6- [And hence, He, or it, was, or became, dear, highly esteemed, or greatly valued. .] ― -b7- Eaz~a EalaY~a A^ano tafoEala ka*aA , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. (Mgh, O, Msb, K) and (Fr, Mgh, O, K,) [the second pers. of the pret. being Eazazota and Eazizota ,] the latter aor. the more chaste, (O,) means Thy doing so distressed, or hath distressed, or afflicted, me; or, emphatically, distresses, or afflicts, me; syn. Ai$otad~a , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA,) and Haq~a , (S, O, K, TA,) and $aq~a : (TA:) a phrase [often, but not always,] alluding to a loathing of the action, or indignation thereat. (Msb.) In like manner also you say, Eaz~a EalaY~a ka*aA Such a thing distressed, or afflicted, me. (S.) And Eaz~a EalaY~a A^ano A^asuwo'aka It distressed, or afflicted, me to displease thee. (A.) And Eaz~a maA A^an~aka *aAhibN , like Haq~a A^an~aka *aAhibN [or Haq~a maA An~k *Ahb , meaning It is distressing that thou art going away ]. (TA.) And one says to a man, Dost thou love me? and he replies, laEaz~a maA , i. e., la$ad~a maA , (A, O, K,) and laHaq~a maA , (A, TA,) meaning It distresses me, what thou sayest; or it has distressed me. (TK.) You say also, bimaA A^aSaAbaka ↓ A^uEozizotu I was, or am, distressed by what befell, or hath befallen, thee. (S, O, K.) And EalaY~a bimaA A^uSibota bihi ↓ A^aEozizo That by which thou hast been afflicted distresses me: (S, O:) [or how doth it distress me! ] so in a trad. of 'Alee; when he beheld Talhah slain, he said, EalaY~a ↓ A^aEozizo A^abaA muHam~adK A^ano A^araAka mujad~alFA taHota nujuwmi Als~amaA='i [ It distresses me, or how doth it distress me! O Aboo-Mohammad, that I see thee prostrated upon the ground beneath the stars of heaven ]. (TA.) [A similar ex. is given in the A; without bi prefixed to A^ano .] -A2- Eaz~a also signifies He was, or became, weak: thus having two contr. meanings. (Msb.) -A3- Eaz~ahu , aor. , (S, A, O, K,) inf. n. Eaz~N , (S, O, TA,) He overcame him, or conquered him: (S, A, O:) he overcame him in argumentative contest; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ EazoEazahu , (K,) inf. n. EazoEazapN ; (TA;) and so Eaz~ahu fiY AlxiTaAbi : (Jel in xxxviii. 22, and TA:) or this last signifies he became stronger than he therein; (TA;) or he strove with him to overcome therein; as also fiyhi ↓ EAz~hu , (S, K,) inf. n. muEaAz~apN : (O, TA:) in the Kur xxxviii. 22, some read Eaz~aniY ; and others, ↓ EaAz~aniY : and you say, faEazazotuhu ↓ EaAz~aniY , meaning, he strove with me to overcome, and I overcame him: and muEaAz~apN signifies the contending together in argument: (TA:) you say also of a horse, faArisahu ↓ AEtz~ [ he overcame his rider, or gained the mastery over him ]. (S and K in art. jmE .) It is said in a prov., (S,) mano Eaz~a baz~a He who overcomes takes the spoil. (S, A, O, K.) And in another prov., (S,) A_i*aA Eaz~a A^axuwka fahuno (Th, S, O, K) When thy brother overcomes thee, and thou art not equal to him ( lamo tuqaAwmohu ) be thou gentle to him: (Az, O, K, TA:) or when thy brother magnifies and exalts himself against thee, abase thyself: (Th, TA:) or, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, what Th says is a mistake; the right reading being fahino , with kesr, and the meaning, when thy brother is hard, or severe, to thee, treat thou him with gentleness, or blandishment; not fahuno , with damm, which is from AlhawaAnu : but ISd approves and justifies the reading given by Th. (TA.) [See also 10.] -A4- Eaz~ahu . aor. , inf. n. Eaz~N , also signifies the same as Eaz~azahu (Msb, TA *) and A^aEaz~ahu , (TA,) in a sense pointed out below: see 2, in two places. (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] with the same aor. and inf. n., He aided, or helped, him. (IKtt, TA.) -A5- Eaz~a AlmaA='u , (O, K,) aor. , (O,) The water flowed. (O, K.) ― -b2- And Eaz~ati AlqaroHapu , (O, K,) aor. , (O,) The qrHp , [i. e. wound, or pustule, ] discharged what was in it. (O, K.) -A6- Eaz~ato , aor. , inf. n. EuzuwzN and EizaAzN ; (S, O, K;) and , (K,) accord. to IAar, (O,) Eazuzato , (O, K,) inf. n. EuzuwzN ; (O, TA;) She (a camel, IAar, S, O, K, and a ewe or goat, IAar, O) was narrow in the orifices of the teats; (S, O, * K;) as also ↓ AEz~t , (S, O, K,) and ↓ tEz~zt : (S, K:) or Eazuzato , [which is of a very uncommon form, (see dam~a , last sentence,)] she (a ewe, or goat,) became scant in her milk. (IKh, TA in art. lb .)

definition: Might, potency, power, or strength;
sourceDefinition: Might, potency, power, or strength; (TA;) as also ↓ Eiz~apN : (S, O, TA:) and especially after lowness, or meanness, of condition; as also ↓ the latter word: (AZ, S, A, * Msb, and K, in explanation of Eaz~a :) high, or elevated, rank or condition or state; nobility, honourableness, gloriousness, or illustriousness; syn. rifoEapN ; (TA;) contr. of *ul~N ; (S, A, O;) [as also ↓ the latter word: see Eaz~a .] biEiz~iY laqado kaAna ka*aA waka*aA , and biEiz~ika , [ By my might, &c., and by thy might, &c., such and such things have happened, ] like laEamoriY and laEamoruka , are bad phrases of the people of Esh-Shihr. (TA.) ― -b2- [ Self-magnification; self-exaltation: see Eaz~a :] and ↓ Eiz~apN [or Eiz~apN Aln~afosi signifies the same: and also,] (tropical:) disdainfulness; scornfulness; indignation; (O, TA;) of a blameable kind; as in the Kur ii. 202. (TA.) ― -b3- The quality, or power, of resisting, or withstanding; resistibility: (TA:) and ↓ Eiz~apN [signifies the same: and] the quality, in a man, of being invincible, or not to be overcome: (B, TA:) and both signify [ difficulty, or hardness: and] impossibility, insuperableness, or unattainableness, of a thing. (Msb.) ― -b4- [ Rareness; scarceness; as also ↓ Eiz~apN : see Eaz~a .] ― -b5- The act of overcoming; conquest; superior power or farce; (TA;) as also ↓ Eiz~apN : (S, O, TA:) and the latter has this signification especially in relation to an argumentative contest. (K.) -A2- maTarN Eiz~N Vehement rain: (S, K:) or copious rain: (IAar, AHn, O, TA:) or mighty, great, rain, that causes the plain and the mountain to flow. (TA.) And siyolN Eiz~N An overpowering torrent. (A, TA.)

sourceDefinition: Mighty, potent, powerful, or strong, [in an absolute sense; as also ↓ Eaz~N , accord. to the Msb; and especially,] after lowness, or meanness, of condition: (S, A, Msb:) [ high, or elevated, in rank or condition or state; noble, honourable, glorious, or illustrious: see Eaz~a :] rough in manners or behaviour: (TA: [see *aliylN , which signifies, sometimes, the contr. of this:]) [ proud: disdainful; scornful; indignant: see Eiz~N :] resisting; withstanding; indomitable; invincible; not to be overcome; applied to a man: (TA:) [ difficult, or hard: and impossible, insuperable, or unattainable: see Eaz~a :] rare; scarce; hardly to be found: (S, K:) [and hence, dear, highly esteemed, or greatly valued: hence, also, applied to a word or phrase, rare, or extraordinary, in respect of usage or analogy or both: ] and ↓ A^aEaz~u also signifies the same as EaziyzN [mostly in the first of the senses expl. above, or in a similar sense]: (S, O, K:) and ↓ Euz~aY the same as EaziyzapN [app. as meaning noble, or the like ], (O, K, TA,) applied to a woman: (TA:) the pl. of EaziyzN is EizaAzN (S, O, K) and A^aEiz~apN (S, Msb, K) and A^aEiz~aA='u ; (S, K;) but one does not say EuzazaA='u , on account of the reduplication, which is disliked. (TA.) ― -b3- AlEaziyzu , as a name of God, signifies The Mighty, (TA,) who overcomes (O, TA) everything: (TA:) or He who resists, or withstands, so that nothing overcomes Him: (Zj, TA:) or The Incomparable, or Unparalleled. definition: [ More, and most, mighty, potent, powerful, or strong: &c.
sourceDefinition: [ More, and most, mighty, potent, powerful, or strong: &c.: see EaziyzN , of which it is the comparative and superlative form: and see an ex. voce Aalo (p. 75): and another in a verse cited in art. Sb , conj. 6]. It is related in a trad. of Aboo-Bekr, that he said to 'Áïsheh, A_in~a A^aHab~a Aln~aAsi A_ilaY~a ganFY A^anoti waA^aEaz~uhumo faqorFA A^anoti , meaning. Verily the one of mankind whose richness is most pleasing to me art thou; and the one of them whose poverty is most distressing to me art thou. (Mgh.) The fem. of A^aEaz~u [as a noun of excess] is ↓ Euz~aY : (S, ISd, O, K;) like as fuDolaY is of A^afoDalu . (ISd.) [But see what follows.] ― -b2- ↓ AlEuz~aY was the name of A certain idol, (S, O, K,) belonging to Kureysh and Benoo-Kináneh: (S, O, TA:) or a certain gum-acacia-tree, ( samurapN ,) which the tribe of Ghatafán (S, O, K) the son of Saad the son of Keys-'Eilán (TA) used to worship; (S, O, K;) the first who took it as an object of worship was Dhálim the son of As' ad; above Dhát- 'Irk, nine miles towards El-Bustán, (O, K, TA,) at [ the valley called ] En-Nakhleh Esh-Shámeeyeh, (O, TA,) near Mekkeh; or, as some say, at Et- Táïf: (TA:) he, (K,) Dhálim, (O,) or they, (S,) built over it a house, (S, O, K) and named it bus~ , (O, K,) accord. to Ibn-El-Kelbee; or, accord. to others, bus~aA=' ; (TA;) and they appointed to it ministers, (S, TA,) like those of the Kaabeh; (TA;) and they used to hear in it a voice: (O, K, TA:) but Mohammad sent to it Khálid Ibn-El-Weleed, (S, O, K,) in the year of the conquest [of Mekkeh], (O, TA,) and he demolished the house, (S, K,) and slew the [chief] minister, (TA,) and burned the gum-acacia-tree: (S, O, K:) or, as is related on the authority of I'Ab, a certain she-devil, who used to come to three gumacacia-trees ( samuraAt ) in Batn-Nakhleh, against whom Mohammad, when he conquered Mekkeh, sent Khálid Ibn-El-Weleed; and he cut down the trees, and slew her and her minister. (TA.) A poet says, A^amaA wadimaA='K maAy^iraAtK taxaAluhaA EalaY qun~api AlEuz~aY wabiAln~asori EanodamaA [ Verily, or now surely, by bloods flowing, and running hither and thither, which thou wouldst think to be dragon's-blood, upon the mountain-top of El-' Ozzà, and by En-Nesr ]. (S.) sourceDefinition: [The inf. n.] EaqolN signifies The act of withholding, or restraining; syn. manoEN . (TA.) [This is app. the primary signification, or it may be from what next follows.] ― -b2- Eaqala AlbaEiyra , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. EaqolN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) He bound the camel with the [ rope called ] EiqaAl ; (Mgh;) meaning he bound the camel's fore shank to his arm; (K;) i. e. he folded together the camel's fore shank and his arm and bound them both in the middle of the arm with the rope called EiqaAl ; (S, O, Msb;) and ↓ AEtqlhu signifies the same; as also ↓ Eq~lhu ; (K;) or you say, Eaq~alotu AlA_ibila , from AlEiqaAlu , (S, O,) inf. n. taEoqiylN , (O,) [i. e. I bound the camels in the manner expl. above, ] this verb being with tesh-deed because of its application to a number of objects: (S, O:) and sometimes the hocks were bound with the EiqaAl . (TA.) The she-camel, also, was bound with the EiqaAl on the occasion of her being covered: ― -b3- and hence AlEaqolu is metonymically used as meaning AljimaAEu [i. e. (assumed tropical:) The act of compressing a woman]. (TA.) ― -b4- Eaqalotu Alqatiyla , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, *) or Almaqotuwla , (S, O,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (Msb, TA,) means I gave, or paid, the bloodwit to the heir, or next of kin, of the slain person: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K: *) for the camels [that constituted the bloodwit] used to be bound with the EiqaAl in the yard of the abode of the heir, or next of kin, of the slain person; and in consequence of frequency of usage, the phrase became employed to mean thus when the bloodwit was given in dirhems or deenárs. (As, S, O, Msb. * [See a verse cited in the first paragraph of art. Eyf .]) And [hence] one says also, Eaqalotu Eanohu , (inf. n. as above, TA,) meaning I paid for him, (the slayer, Mgh,) i. e., in his stead, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, *) the bloodwit that was obligatory upon him, (S, Mgh, O, K, *) or what was obligatory upon him of the bloodwit. (Msb.) And Eaqalotu lahu dama fulaAnK I relinquished in his favour retaliation of the blood of such a one for the bloodwit. (S, O, Msb, K. *) laA taEoqilu AlEaAqilapu EamodFA walaA EabodFA , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) in a trad. (S, O, Msb) of Esh-Shaabee, (O,) or a saying of Esh-Shaabee, (Mgh, * K,) not a trad., (K,) but the like occurs in a trad. related on the authority of I'Ab, (TA,) [meaning, accord. to an expl. of the verb when trans. without a particle, mentioned above, Those who are responsible for the payment of a bloodwit in certain cases shall not pay it for an intentional act of slaying or the like, nor for the slaying or the like of a slave, ] applies, accord. to Aboo-Haneefeh, to the case of a slave's committing a crime against a free person: (S, O, Msb, K: [and thus as expl. in the Mgh:]) but, (S, O, Msb, K,) accord. to Ibn-Abee-Leylà, (S, O, Msb,) it applies to the case of a free person's committing a crime against a slave; for if the meaning were as Aboo-Haneefeh says, the phrase would be laA taEoqilu AlEaAqilapu Eano EabodK ; (S, O, Msb, K;) and As pronounced this to be correct: (S, O, Msb: *) Akmal-ed-Deen, however, in the Exposition of the Hidáyeh, says that Eaqalotuhu is used in the sense of Eaqalotu Eanohu , and that the context of the trad. indicates this meaning, which MF also defends. (TA.) [See also the saying laA A^aEoqilu Alkaloba Alhar~aAra in art. hr .] ― -b5- Eaqalahu , inf. n. as above, also means He set him up [app. a man] on one of his legs; [app. from Eaqala AlbaEiyra ;] as also Eakalahu : and every Eaqol is a raising. (TA.) ― -b6- Also, [agreeably with the explanation of the inf. n. in the first sentence of this art.,] and ↓ Eq~lhu , and ↓ tEq~lhu , (TA, [see also the first paragraph of art. Ejs ,]) and ↓ AEtqlhu , (Msb, TA,) He withheld him, or restrained him, (Msb, TA,) Eano HaAjatihi from the object of his want. (TA.) ― -b7- And [hence,] Eaqala Ald~awaA='u baTonahu , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. (S, K) and , (K,) inf. n. EaqolN , (TA,) The medicine bound, or confined, his belly [or bowels ]; syn. A^amosakahu : (S, O, Msb, K:) accord. to some, particularly after looseness: and baTonahu ↓ AEtql signifies the same. (TA.) And yaEoqilu AlT~aboEa is said of a medicine [as meaning, in like manner, It binds the bowels; is astringent ]. (TA in art. HmD ; &c.) And Eql AlbaTonu [app. Euqila ] The belly [or bowels ] became bound, or confined; syn. Aisotamosaka . (TA.) ― -b8- Eaqala EalaY Alqawomi , [aor. ,] inf. n. EiqaAlN , means He collected, or exacted, the poor-rates of the people, or party; [app. from Eaqala AlbaEiyra ; as though he bound with the rope called EiqaAl the camels that he collected;] on the authority of IKtt. (TA.) 'Omar, when he had deferred [collecting] the poor-rate in the year [of drought called] EaAmu Alr~amaAdapi , sent Ibn-AbeeDhubáb, and said, AiEoqilo Ealayohimo EiqaAlayoni faA@qosimo fiyhimo EiqaAlFA waA@'otiniY biA@lA=xari [ Collect thou from them two years' poor-rate; then divide among them one year's poor-rate, and bring to me the other ]. (O.) One says of the collector of the poor-rate, yaEoqilu AlS~adaqapa [ He collects, or exacts, the poor-rate ]. (S, O.) ― -b9- Eaqala fulaAnFA and ↓ AEtqlhu signify He threw down such a one [ in wrestling ] by twisting his leg upon the latter's leg: (K, * TA:) [or] you say, Al$~agozabiy~apa ↓ SaAraEahu faA@Eotaqalahu He wrestled with him and twisted his leg upon the leg of the latter: (S, O:) and one says of a wrestler, ↓ lifulaAnK EuqolapN bihaA Aln~aAsa ↓ yaEotaqilu , (S, O,) or yaEoqilu bihaA Aln~aAsa , i. e. [ Such a one has ] a [ mode of ] twisting his leg with another's [ whereby he wrestles with men ]. (TA.) ― -b10- Eaqalato $aEarahaA , (inf. n. EaqolN , TA,) said of a woman, She combed her hair: (S, O:) or combed it in a certain manner; as also ↓ Eaq~alatohu . (TA.) -A2- Eaqala , aor. , inf. n. EaqolN and ↓ maEoquwlN , (S, O, K,) or the latter, accord. to Sb, is an epithet, [or a pass. part. n.,] for he used to say that no inf. n. has the measure mafoEuwlN , (S, O,) He was, or became, EaAqil [i. e. intelligent, &c.; and so ↓ tEq~l ; as though he were withheld, or restrained, from doing that which is not suitable, or befitting: see EaqolN below]: and ↓ Eq~l , (K, TA,) inf. n. taEoqiylN , (TA,) signifies the same, (K,) or [ he possessed much intelligence, for] it is with teshdeed to denote muchness: (TA:) and Eaqila , aor. , is a dial. var. of Eaqala , aor. , signifying he became EaAqil . (IKtt, TA.) ― -b2- And Eaqala Al$~aYo'a , (Msb, K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. EaqolN , (Msb, TA,) He understood, or knew, the thing; syn. fahimahu : (K, TA:) or i. q. tadab~arahu [app. as meaning he looked into, considered, examined, or studied, the thing repeatedly, until he knew it ]; and Eaqila , aor. , is a dial. var. thereof. (Msb.)
