The she-camel, also, was bound with the EiqaAl on the occasion of her being covered: ― -b3- and hence AlEaqolu is metonymically used as meaning AljimaAEu [i. e. (assumed tropical:) The act of compressing a woman]. (TA.) ― -b4- Eaqalotu Alqatiyla , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, *) or Almaqotuwla , (S, O,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (Msb, TA,) means I gave, or paid, the bloodwit to the heir, or next of kin, of the slain person: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K: *) for the camels [that constituted the bloodwit] used to be bound with the EiqaAl in the yard of the abode of the heir, or next of kin, of the slain person; and in consequence of frequency of usage, the phrase became employed to mean thus when the bloodwit was given in dirhems or deenárs. (As, S, O, Msb. * [See a verse cited in the first paragraph of art. Eyf .]) And [hence] one says also, Eaqalotu Eanohu , (inf. n. as above, TA,) meaning I paid for him, (the slayer, Mgh,) i. e., in his stead, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, *) the bloodwit that was obligatory upon him, (S, Mgh, O, K, *) or what was obligatory upon him of the bloodwit. (Msb.) And Eaqalotu lahu dama fulaAnK I relinquished in his favour retaliation of the blood of such a one for the bloodwit. (S, O, Msb, K. *) laA taEoqilu AlEaAqilapu EamodFA walaA EabodFA , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) in a trad. (S, O, Msb) of Esh-Shaabee, (O,) or a saying of Esh-Shaabee, (Mgh, * K,) not a trad., (K,) but the like occurs in a trad. related on the authority of I'Ab, (TA,) [meaning, accord. to an expl. of the verb when trans. without a particle, mentioned above, Those who are responsible for the payment of a bloodwit in certain cases shall not pay it for an intentional act of slaying or the like, nor for the slaying or the like of a slave, ] applies, accord. to Aboo-Haneefeh, to the case of a slave's committing a crime against a free person: (S, O, Msb, K: [and thus as expl. in the Mgh:]) but, (S, O, Msb, K,) accord. to Ibn-Abee-Leylà, (S, O, Msb,) it applies to the case of a free person's committing a crime against a slave; for if the meaning were as Aboo-Haneefeh says, the phrase would be laA taEoqilu AlEaAqilapu Eano EabodK ; (S, O, Msb, K;) and As pronounced this to be correct: (S, O, Msb: *) Akmal-ed-Deen, however, in the Exposition of the Hidáyeh, says that Eaqalotuhu is used in the sense of Eaqalotu Eanohu , and that the context of the trad. indicates this meaning, which MF also defends. (TA.) [See also the saying laA A^aEoqilu Alkaloba Alhar~aAra in art. hr .] ― -b5- Eaqalahu , inf. n. as above, also means He set him up [app. a man] on one of his legs; [app. from Eaqala AlbaEiyra ;] as also Eakalahu : and every Eaqol is a raising. (TA.) ― -b6- Also, [agreeably with the explanation of the inf. n. in the first sentence of this art.,] and ↓ Eq~lhu , and ↓ tEq~lhu , (TA, [see also the first paragraph of art. Ejs ,]) and ↓ AEtqlhu , (Msb, TA,) He withheld him, or restrained him, (Msb, TA,) Eano HaAjatihi from the object of his want. (TA.) ― -b7- And [hence,] Eaqala Ald~awaA='u baTonahu , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. (S, K) and , (K,) inf. n. EaqolN , (TA,) The medicine bound, or confined, his belly [or bowels ]; syn. A^amosakahu : (S, O, Msb, K:) accord. to some, particularly after looseness: and baTonahu ↓ AEtql signifies the same. (TA.) And yaEoqilu AlT~aboEa is said of a medicine [as meaning, in like manner, It binds the bowels; is astringent ]. (TA in art. HmD ; &c.) And Eql AlbaTonu [app. Euqila ] The belly [or bowels ] became bound, or confined; syn. Aisotamosaka . (TA.) ― -b8- Eaqala EalaY Alqawomi , [aor. ,] inf. n. EiqaAlN , means He collected, or exacted, the poor-rates of the people, or party; [app. from Eaqala AlbaEiyra ; as though he bound with the rope called EiqaAl the camels that he collected;] on the authority of IKtt. (TA.) 'Omar, when he had deferred [collecting] the poor-rate in the year [of drought called] EaAmu Alr~amaAdapi , sent Ibn-AbeeDhubáb, and said, AiEoqilo Ealayohimo EiqaAlayoni faA@qosimo fiyhimo EiqaAlFA waA@'otiniY biA@lA=xari [ Collect thou from them two years' poor-rate; then divide among them one year's poor-rate, and bring to me the other ]. (O.) One says of the collector of the poor-rate, yaEoqilu AlS~adaqapa [ He collects, or exacts, the poor-rate ]. (S, O.) ― -b9- Eaqala fulaAnFA and ↓ AEtqlhu signify He threw down such a one [ in wrestling ] by twisting his leg upon the latter's leg: (K, * TA:) [or] you say, Al$~agozabiy~apa ↓ SaAraEahu faA@Eotaqalahu He wrestled with him and twisted his leg upon the leg of the latter: (S, O:) and one says of a wrestler, ↓ lifulaAnK EuqolapN bihaA Aln~aAsa ↓ yaEotaqilu , (S, O,) or yaEoqilu bihaA Aln~aAsa , i. e. [ Such a one has ] a [ mode of ] twisting his leg with another's [ whereby he wrestles with men ]. (TA.) ― -b10- Eaqalato $aEarahaA , (inf. n. EaqolN , TA,) said of a woman, She combed her hair: (S, O:) or combed it in a certain manner; as also ↓ Eaq~alatohu . (TA.) -A2- Eaqala , aor. , inf. n. EaqolN and ↓ maEoquwlN , (S, O, K,) or the latter, accord. to Sb, is an epithet, [or a pass. part. n.,] for he used to say that no inf. n. has the measure mafoEuwlN , (S, O,) He was, or became, EaAqil [i. e. intelligent, &c.; and so ↓ tEq~l ; as though he were withheld, or restrained, from doing that which is not suitable, or befitting: see EaqolN below]: and ↓ Eq~l , (K, TA,) inf. n. taEoqiylN , (TA,) signifies the same, (K,) or [ he possessed much intelligence, for] it is with teshdeed to denote muchness: (TA:) and Eaqila , aor. , is a dial. var. of Eaqala , aor. , signifying he became EaAqil . (IKtt, TA.) ― -b2- And Eaqala Al$~aYo'a , (Msb, K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. EaqolN , (Msb, TA,) He understood, or knew, the thing; syn. fahimahu : (K, TA:) or i. q. tadab~arahu [app. as meaning he looked into, considered, examined, or studied, the thing repeatedly, until he knew it ]; and Eaqila , aor. , is a dial. var. thereof. (Msb.) See also 5. ― -b3- maA A^aEoqiluhu Eanoka $ayoy^FA , (S, and so in the K accord. to my copy of the TA, but in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K ↓ AaEoqalahu ,) meaning daEo Eanoka Al$~ak~a [ Dismiss from thee doubt ], is [said to be] mentioned by Sb; as though the speaker said, maA A^aEolimu $ayoy^FA mim~aA taquwlu fadaEo Eanoka Al$~ak~a [ I know not aught of what thou sayest, so dismiss from thee doubt ]; and [to be] like the phrases xu*o Eanoka and siro Eanoka : Bekr El-Mázinee says, “ I asked AZ and As and Aboo-Málik and Akh respecting this phrase, and they all said, 'We know not what it is: ' ” (so in the S:) [but] it is a mistake, for maA A^agofalahu ; (K, TA;) and thus it is mentioned by Sb and others, with g and f . (TA.) naxolapN laA taEoqilu AlA_ibaAra (tropical:) A palm-tree that will not receive fecundation is a tropical phrase [perhaps from Eaqala meaning “ he understood ” a thing]. (A, TA.) ― -b4- EaAqalotuhu faEaqolotuhu : see 3. ― -b5- Eaqala , aor. , inf. n. EuquwlN (S, O, K) and EaqolN , (K,) He (a mountain-goat, S, O) became, or made himself, inaccessible in a high mountain: (S: in the O unexplained:) or he [a gazelle) ascended [ a mountain ]. (K.) Accord. to Az, AlEuquwlu signifies The protecting oneself in a mountain. (TA.) And one says, Eaqala A_ilayohi , aor. , inf. n. EaqolN and EuquwlN , He betook himself to him, or it, for refuge, protection, covert, or lodging. (K.) ― -b6- Eaqala AlZ~il~u , (S, O, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. EaqolN (K) [and probably EuquwlN also], The shade declined, and contracted, or shrank, at midday; (S, O;) the sun became high, and the shade almost disappeared. (S, O, K.) -A3- Eaqala , (O, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. EaqolN , (TA,) said of a camel, He pastured upon the plant called EaAquwl . (O, K.) -A4- Eaqila , aor. , (K,) inf. n. EaqalN , (S, O, K,) He (a camel) had a twisting in the hind leg, (S, O, K,) and much width [ between the hind legs ]: (S, O:) or had an excessive wideness, or spreading, of the hind legs, so that the hocks knocked together: (ISk, S, O:) or had a knocking together of the knees. (K.) [See also rawaHa .]

definition: (S, Mgh, O, K) means The woman is on a par with the man to the third part of her bloodwit;
sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, O, K) means The woman is on a par with the man to the third part of her bloodwit; (S, Mgh, O;) she receives like as the man receives [up to that point]: (Mgh:) i. e., [for instance,] his muwDiHap [or wound of the head for which the mulct is five camels] and her muwDiHap are equal; (K;) but when the portion reaches to the third of the bloodwit, her [portion of the] bloodwit is the half of that of the man: (S, O, K:) thus, for one of her fingers, ten camels are due to her, as in the case of the finger of the man; for two of her fingers, twenty camels; and for three of her fingers, thirty; but for four of her fingers, only twenty, because they exceed the third, therefore the portion is reduced to the half of what is due to the man: so accord. to Ibn-El-Museiyab: but Esh-Sháfi'ee and the people of El-Koofeh assign for the finger of the woman five camels, and for two of her fingers ten; and regard not the third part. (TA.) -A2- ↓ EaAqalotuhu faEaqalotuhu , (S, O, K, *) inf. n. of the former muEaAqalapN , (TA,) and aor. of the latter , (S, O, K,) and inf. n. EaqolN , (TA,) means I vied, or contended, with him for superiority in Eaqol [or intelligence ], (O, TA,) and I surpassed him therein. (S, O, K, * TA.)

definition: They paid among themselves, or conjointly, the mulct for the blood of such a one.
sourceDefinition: They paid among themselves, or conjointly, the mulct for the blood of such a one. (K.) It is said in a trad., A_in~aA laA nataEaAqalu AlmaSoEa Verily we will not pay among ourselves, or conjointly, the mulcts for slight wounds of the head, [lit. the stroke with a sword, ] but will oblige him who commits the offence to pay the mulct for it: i. e. the people of the towns or villages shall not pay the mulcts for the people of the desert; nor the people of the desert, for the people of the towns or villages; in the like of the case of the [wound termed] muwDiHap . (TA.) And in another it is said, yataEaAqaluwna bayonahumo maEaAqilahumu AlA^uwlaY [ They shall take and give among themselves, or conjointly, their former bloodwits ]: i. e. they shall be as they were in respect of the taking and giving of bloodwits. (TA.) And one says, Alqawomu EalaY maA kaAnuwA yataEaAqaluwna Ealayohi [ The people, or party, are acting in conformity with that usage in accordance with which they used to pay and receive among themselves bloodwits ]. (S, O.) -A2- tEAql also signifies He affected, or made a show of possessing, Eaqol [i. e. intelligence, &c.], without having it. (S, O.) [See also 5.]

sourceDefinition: an inf. n. used as a subst. [properly so termed], (Msb,) A bloodwit, or mulct for bloodshed; syn. diyapN ; (As, S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) so called for a reason mentioned in the first paragraph in the explanation of the phrase Eaqalotu Alqatiyla ; (As, S, Mgh, * O, Msb;) as also ↓ maEoqulapN , (S, Mgh, O, K,) of which ↓ miEoqalapN , with fet-h to the q , is a dial. var., mentioned in the R; (TA;) and of which the pl. is maEaAqilu : (S, O, K:) one says, ↓ lanaAEinoda fulaAnK DamadN mino maEoqulapK i. e. We have a remainder of a bloodwit owed to us by such a one. (S, O.) And AlA^uwlaY ↓ humo EalaY maEaAqilihimi They are [acting] in conformity with [the usages relating to] the bloodwits that were in the Time of Ignorance; (K, TA;) or meaning EalaY maA kaAnuwA yataEaAqaluwna Ealayohi [expl. above (see 6)]: (S, O:) or they are [acting] in conformity with the conditions of their fathers; (K, TA;) but the former is the primary meaning: (TA:) and [hence] EalaY qawomihi ↓ SaAra damu fulaAnK maEoqulapF The blood of such a one became [ the occasion of ] a debt incumbent on his people, or party, (S, O, K, *) to be paid by them from their possessions. (S, O.) -A2- And as being originally the inf. n. of Eaqala in the phrase Eaqala Al$~aYo'a meaning [ fahimahu or] tadab~arahu ; (Msb;) or as originally meaning AlmanoEu , because it withholds, or restrains, its possessor from doing that which is not suitable; or from AlmaEoqilu as meaning “ the place to which one has recourse for protection &c., ” because its possessor has recourse to it; (TA;) AlEaqolu signifies also Intelligence, understanding, intellect, mind, reason, or knowledge; syn. AlHajoru , (S, O,) and Aln~uhaY , (S,) or Aln~uhoyapu , (O,) or AlHijaA , and All~ub~u , (Msb,) or AlEilomu , (K,) or the contr. of AlHumoqu ; (M, TA;) or the knowledge of the qualities of things, of their goodness and their badness, and their perfectness and their defectiveness; or the knowledge of the better of two good things, and of the worse of two bad things, or of affairs absolutely; or a faculty whereby is the discrimination between the bad and the good; (K, TA;) but these and other explanations of AlEaqol in the K are all in treatises of intellectual things, and not mentioned by the leading lexicologists; (TA; [in which are added several more explanations of a similar kind that have no proper place in this work;]) some say that it is an innate property by which man is prepared to understand speech; (Msb;) the truth is, that it is a spiritual light, (K, TA,) shed into the heart and the brain, (TA,) whereby the soul acquires the instinctive and speculative kinds of knowledge, and the commencement of its existence is on the occasion of the young's becoming in the fætal state, [or rather of its quickening, ] after which it continues to increase until it becomes complete on the attainment of puberty, (K, TA,) or until the attainment of forty years: (TA:) the pl. is EuquwlN : (K:) Sb mentions EaqolN as an instance of an inf. n. having a pl., namely, EuquwlN ; like $ugolN and maraDN : (TA in art. mrD :) IAar says, (O,) AlEaqolu is [ syn. with ] Alqalobu , and Alqalobu is [ syn. with ] AlEaqolu : (O, K:) and ↓ AlmaEoquwlu is [said to be] a subst., or name, for AlEaqolu , like Almajoluwdu and Almayosuwru for AljalaAdapu and Alyusoru : (Har p. 12:) it is said in a prov., ↓ maA lahu juwlN walaA maEoquwlN , (Meyd, and Har ubi suprà,) meaning He has not strong purpose of mind, [to withhold, or protect, him,] like the jwl [or casing] of the well of the collapsing whereof one is free from fear because of its firmness, nor intellect, or intelligence, ( Eaqol ,) to withhold him from doing that which is not suitable to the likes of him. (Meyd. [But see maEoquwlN below.]) [Hence, A^asonaAnu AlEaqoli (see 1 in art. Hnk ) and A^aDoraAsu AlEaqoli (see DirosN ), both meaning The wisdom-teeth. ] -A3- [It is said that] EaqolN also signifies A fortress; syn. HiSonN . (K.) [But this seems to be doubtful.] See maEoqilN . -A4- And A sort of red cloth (S, O, K) with which the [ women's camel-vehicle called ] hawodaj is covered: (K:) or a sort of what are called buruwd [pl. of burodN , q. v.] or a sort of figured cloth, (K,) or, as in the M, of red figured cloth: (TA:) or such as is figured with long forms. (Har p. 416.)

definition: [act. part. n. of Eaqala : and as such,] The payer of a bloodwit: pl. [or rather coll. gen. n.] ↓ EaAqilapN : (Msb:) the latter is an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates; (TA;) and...
sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of Eaqala : and as such,] The payer of a bloodwit: pl. [or rather coll. gen. n.] ↓ EaAqilapN : (Msb:) the latter is an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates; (TA;) and signifies a man's party (S, Mgh, O, K, TA) who league together to defend one another, (S, O, K, TA,) consisting of the relations on the father's side, (S, Mgh, * O, TA,) who pay the bloodwit (S, Mgh, O, TA) [app. in conjunction with the slayer ] for him who has been slain unintentionally: (S, O, TA:) it was decided by the Prophet that it was to be paid in three years, to the heirs of the person slain: (TA:) they look to the offender's brothers on the father's side, who, if they take it upon them, pay it in three years: if they do not take it upon them, the debt is transferred to the sons [meaning all the male descendants] of his grandfather; and in default of their doing so, to those of his father's grandfather; and in default of their doing so, to those of his grandfather's grandfather; and so on: it is not transferred from any one of these classes unless they are unable [to pay it]: and such as are enrolled in a register [of soldiers or pensioners or any corporation] are alike in respect of the bloodwit: (IAth, TA:) or, accord. to the people of El-'Irák, it means the persons enrolled in the registers [ of soldiers or of others ]: (S, O:) or it is applied to the persons of the register which was that of the slayer; who derive their subsistence-money, or allowances, from the revenues of a particular register: (Mgh:) Ahmad Ibn-Hambal is related to have said to Is-hák Ibn-Mansoor, it is applied to the tribe ( qabiylap ) [of the slayer]; but that they bear responsibility [only] in proportion to their ability; and that if there is no EaAqilap , it [i. e. the bloodwit] is not to be from the property of the offender; but Is-hák says that in this case it is to be from the treasury of the state, the bloodwit not being [in any case] made a thing of no account: (TA:) the pl. of EaAqilapN thus applied is EawaAqilu . (Msb.) -A2- EaAqilN also signifies Having, or possessing, Eaqol [i. e. intelligence, understanding, &c.; or intelligent, &c.; a rational being]; (S, O, Msb, K;) and so ↓ EaquwlN , (S, O, K,) or this latter has an intensive signification [i. e. having much intelligence &c.]: (TA: [see an ex. in a saying cited voce A^abolahu , in art. blh :]) the former is expl. by some as applied to a man who withholds, or restrains, and turns back, his soul from its inclinations, or blamable inclinations: (TA:) and it is likewise applied to a woman, as also EaAqilapN : (Msb:) the pl. masc. is Euq~aAlN and EuqalaA='u , (Msb, K,) this latter pl. sometimes used; and the pl. fem. is EawaAqilu and EaAqilaAtN . (Msb.) ― -b2- EaAqilN is also applied to a mountaingoat, as an epithet, signifying That protects himself in his mountain from the hunter: (TA:) [and in like manner ↓ EaquwlN is said by Freytag to be used in the Deewán of Jereer.] And it is [also] a name for A mountain-goat, (S, O,) or a gazelle; (K;) because it renders itself inaccessible in a high mountain. (S, O, K. *) ― -b3- And EaAqilapN signifies A female comber of the hair. (S, O.)

definition: A place to which one betakes himself for refuge, protection, preservation, covert, or lodging;
sourceDefinition: A place to which one betakes himself for refuge, protection, preservation, covert, or lodging; syn. malojaA^N ; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ EaqolN , (S, O, K,) of which the pl. is EuquwlN : (S, O:) but Az says that he had not heard Eaqol in this sense on any authority except that of Lth; and held AlEuquwlu , which is cited as an ex. of its pl., to signify “ the protecting oneself in a mountain: ” (TA:) and maEoqilN signifies also a fortress; [like as EaqolN is said to do;] syn. HiSonN : (Mgh:) the pl. is maEaAqilu . (TA.) Hence one says, using it metaphorically, huwa maEoqilu qawomihi (tropical:) He is the refuge of his people: and the kings of Himyer are termed in a trad. maEaAqilu AlA^aroDi , meaning The fortresses [or refuges ] of the land. (TA.) ― -b2- [It is perhaps primarily used in relation to camels; for] maEaAqilu AlA_ibili means The places in which the camels are bound with the rope called EiqaAl . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, TA,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. Eama$N , (S, A, O, K,) He (a man, S, TA) was weak in sight, (S, A, O, K,) and generally, or at most times, shedding tears. (S, O, K.) And fulaAnN laA taEoma$u fiyhi AlmawoEiZapu (assumed tropical:) Such a one, exhortation produces no good effect upon him. (A, O.) (TA.) ― -b3- And Eananotuhu , (Msb,) and Eun~a , (Mgh,) I confined him, (Msb,) and he was confined, (Mgh,) in the Eun~ap i. e. the enclosure (Mgh, Msb) of the camels. definition: is used in three manners: -A2- First, it is a prep.
sourceDefinition: is used in three manners: -A2- First, it is a prep.: and as such it has ten meanings. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b2- (1) It denotes transition; (Msb, Mughnee, K;) either sensibly or virtually; (Msb;) and the Basrees have mentioned no other meaning than this: (Mughnee:) or, as Sb expresses it, (Msb,) it denotes what has passed [or rather it denotes passage] from the thing [that is mentioned immediately after it]: (S, Msb:) Er-Rághib says that it necessarily denotes transition from that to the mention of which it is prefixed: and the grammarians say that it is applied to denote what has passed and become remote from thee. (TA.) Thus in the saying, saAfarotu Eani Albaladi [ I journeyed from the country, or town ]. (Mughnee, K. *) And in ragibotu Eano ka*aA [ I abstained from such a thing; and hence, I did not desire, or wish for, such a thing ]. (Mughnee.) And ramayotu Eani Alqawosi [ I shot an arrow, or arrows, from the bow ]; (S, Mughnee;) because by means of the bow one projects his arrow from the bow, and makes it to pass therefrom: (S:) but another meaning of this will be mentioned in what follows. (Mughnee.) And A^aToEamotuhu Eano juwEK [ I fed him so as to free him from hunger ]; (S, Msb;) making hunger to be quitted, and passed from: (S, * Msb:) and in this case, mino is used in its place, (S, TA,) as in the Kur cvi. 3; (TA;) or the meaning in this instance is, because of hunger. (Jel.) And jalasotu Eano yamiynihi , [as though] meaning I sat passing away from the place of his right side, in sitting, to another place [ adjacent thereto: but see another explanation near the end of the paragraph]. (Msb.) And AinoSarifo Ean~iY and tanaH~a Ean~iY [ Turn thou, or go thou, away, or aside, from me ]. (TA.) And A^axa*otu AlEiloma Eanohu I understood, or became acquainted with, [or acquired, ] knowledge, or science, from him; as though the understanding passed from him. (Msb.) [And similar to this is the phrase rawaY Eano fulaAnK , for which Eano fulaAnK alone (the verb being understood) is often used, He related a tradition or traditions &c. as learned, or heard, or received, from such a one, or on the authority of such a one. In many other phrases also, some of which will be mentioned in treating of Eano as syn. with mino , the former of these two prepositions is to be, or may be, expl. as denoting transition. For ex., one says, dafaEa Eanohu and daAfaEa He repelled from him; and hence, he defended him: (see art. dfE :) and ramaY Eanohumo He shot in defence of them: (see an ex. in a verse cited voce maEobuwlN :) and Eanohu is sometimes used for difaAEFA Eanohu ; as in the phrase qaAtalotu Eanohu I fought in defence of him; i. e., repelling from him. But the instances of this and other usages of Eano , exclusive of those mentioned in this paragraph, depending upon verbs or part. ns. expressed or obviously understood, are far too numerous to be here collected: many of these will be found among the explanations of words with which they occur.] ― -b3- (2) It denotes a compensation; or something given, or received, or put, or done, instead, or in lieu, of another thing. (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying [in the Kur ii. 45], wa A@t~aquwA yawomFA laA tajoziY nafosN Eano nafosK $ayoy^FA [ And fear ye a day wherein a soul shall not give anything as a satisfaction for a soul, i. e. for another soul: or shall not make satisfaction for a soul at all; accord. to the latter rendering, $yy^A being put in the accus. case after the manner of an inf. n.]. (Mughnee, K. *) And in the saying in a trad., SuwmiY Eano A^um~iki [ Fast thou for, or in lieu of, thy mother ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b4- (3) It denotes superiority ( AlAisotiEolaA=' [as used tropically]); (Mughnee, K;) i. e. as syn. with EalaY . (Mughnee.) Thus in the saying of Dhu-l-Isba' El-'Adwánee, laAhi A@bonu Eam~ika laA A^afoDalota fiY HasabK Ean~iY walaA A^anota day~aAniY fataxozuwaniY (S, Mughnee,) i. e. To God be attributed the excellence of the son of thy paternal uncle (the meaning being lil~`hi dar~u A@boni Eam~ika ), thou hast not become possessed of superiority, in grounds of pretension to respect or honour, above me, or over me, ( EalaY~a ,) nor art thou my governor that thou shouldst rule me; for the well-known mode is to say A^afoDalotu Ealayohi . (Mughnee.) [Thus too in the phrases taEaZ~ama Eanohu and taEaAZama Eanohu (expl. in art. EZm ), and in the phrase tajaAl~a Eanohu (expl. in art. jl ), and the like.] And thus it has been said to be used in the phrase [in the Kur xxxviii. 31], A_in~iY A^aHobabotu Hub~a A@loxayori Eano *ikori rab~iY , meaning qad~amotuhu Ealayohi [i. e. Verily I have preferred the love of good things above, or to, the remembrance, or praise, of my Lord ]: but it is also said that it is here used in its proper manner, as dependent upon a denotative of state suppressed; the meaning being, munoSarifFA Eano *ikori rab~iY [i. e. turning away from the remembrance, &c.]: and AO is related to have said that A^aHobabotu is from A^aHab~a , AlbaEiyru , signifying “ the camel lay down and did not become roused; ” and that the meaning is, I have become withheld by the love of good things from the remembrance, &c. (Mughnee.) And it is [said to be] used as denoting superiority or the like in the saying [in the Kur xlvii. last verse], faA_in~amaA yaboxalu Eano nfosihi [as though the meaning were He is niggardly only to himself ( EalaY nafosihi , for EalaY is considered in this case as importing an ideal superiority); but the phrase may be better rendered, agreeably with the proper, or primary, signification of Eano , he withholds, with niggardliness, only from himself; as is indicated by Bd]. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b5- (4) It denotes a cause. (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying [in the Kur ix. 115], wamaA kaAna A@sotigofaAru A_ibor`hiyma liA^abiyhi A_il~aA Eano mawoEidapK [ And Abraham's begging forgiveness for his father was not otherwise than because of a promise ]. (Mughnee, K.) And thus in the saying [in the Kur xi. 56], wamaA naHonu bitaArikiY A=lihatinaA Eano qawolika [ And we are not, or will not be, relinquishers of our gods because of thy saying ]: or the meaning may be, we do not, or will not, relinquish our gods, turning away ( SaAdiriyna , as a denotative of state relating to the pronoun [implied] in tArkY ,) from thy saying; and this is the opinion of Z. (Mughnee.) [See also an ex. voce danodana , last sentence.] ― -b6- (5) It is syn. with baEoda . (S, Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying [in the Kur xxiii. 42], Eam~aA qaliylK layuSobiHun~a naAdimiyna , (Mughnee, K,) meaning baEoda qaliylK [i. e. After a little while, they will assuredly become repentant ]. (TA.) And in the phrase [in the Kur lxxxiv. 19], latarokabun~a TabaqFA Eano TabaqK [expl. in art. Tbq ], meaning HaAlapF baEoda HaAlapK . (Mughnee.) And in the saying, wamanohalK waradotuhu Eano manohalK [ And to many a watering-place have I come after a watering-place ]. (Mughnee.) And in the saying of El-Hárith Ibn-'Obád, qar~ibaA marobaTa Aln~aEaAmapi min~iY laqiHato Harobu wAy^ilK Eano HiyaAli (S, * TA,) meaning baEoda HiyaAlK [i. e. Make ye two to be near to me the place of the tying of En-Na'ámeh (the name of a horse of the poet): the war of Wáïl has become pregnant after failing to be pregnant during a year, or years ]. (TA.) And in the saying of Et-Tirimmáh, sayaEolamu kul~uhumo A^an~iY musin~N ↓ A_i*aA dafaEuwA EinaAnFA Eano EinaAni i. e. [ All of them shall know that I am of full age, when they press forward ] heat after heat. (TA.) ― -b7- (6) It denotes the meaning of the preposition fiY . (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying, walaA taku Eano Hamoli Alr~ibaAEapi waAniyaA [ And be not thou remiss in bearing the responsibility of the obligation that thou takest upon thyself ]; as is shown by the phrase, [in the Kur xx. 44], walaA taniyaA fiY *ikoriY : (Mughnee, K:) so it is said; but it seems that the meaning of wanaY Eano ka*aA is, “ he passed from such a thing, not entering upon it; ” and wanaY fiyhi , “ he entered upon it but was remiss, or languid: ” by Alr~ibaAEap is meant the payment of a bloodwit or the like. (Mughnee.) ― -b8- (7) It is syn. with mino . (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying [in the Kur xlii. 24], wahuwa A@l~a*iY yaqobalu A@lt~awobapa Eano EibaAdihi [ And He is he who accepts repentance from his servants ]. (AO, Mughnee, K.) Az mentions among the cases in which there is a difference between mino and Eano , that the former has adjoined to it a noun signifying what is near; and the latter, [one signifying] what is remote; as in one's saying samiEotu mino fulaAnK HadiyvFA [ I heard from such a one a narrative ], and Had~avaniY Eano fulaAnK HadiyvFA [ He related to me a narrative from such a one, a phrase similar to rawaY Eano fulaAnK , mentioned among exs. of the first meaning of En ]: accord. to As, one says, Had~avaniY fulaAnN mino fulaAnK , meaning Eanohu [i. e. Such a one related to me from such a one ]; and lahiytu mino fulaAnK and Eanohu [ I became diverted from such a one so as to forget him ]: accord. to Ks, one says lahiytu Eanohu only: and Eanoka jaA='a h`*aA as meaning minoka [i. e. From thee came this ]. (TA.) ― -b9- (8) It is syn. with bi . (Mughnee, K.) Thus [it is said to be used] in the phrase [in the Kur liii. 3], wamaA yanoTiqu Eani A@lohawaY [ Nor does he speak with the desire of self-gratification ]: (Mughnee, K:) but it seems that it is here used in its proper [or primary] sense; and that the meaning is, wamaA yaSoduru qawoluhu Eano hawFY [ nor does his speech proceed from desire of self-gratification; so the phrase may be well rendered, nor does he speak from the desire &c.]. (Mughnee.) One says also, A^ajaAbuwA Eano bawaA='K waAHidK , meaning bijawaAbK waAHidK [i. e. They replied with one reply ]. (T, S, O, K, all in art, bwA^ .) And jaAw^uwA Eano A=xirihimo [ They came with the last of them; Eano being here syn. with bi ; meaning they came all, without exception ]. (A in art. Axr .) [And in like manner, qataluwhumo Eano A=xirihimo They slew them with the last of them; meaning they slew them all, without exception. ] ― -b10- (9) It denotes the using a thing as an aid or instrument. (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying, ramayotu Eani Alqawosi [ I shot with, or by means of, the bow ], accord. to Ibn-Málik; (Mughnee, K;) because one says also, ramayotu biAlqawosi ; both mentioned by Fr. (Mughnee.) [Another explanation of this phrase has been mentioned before.] ― -b11- (10) It is redundant, to compensate for another [ En ] suppressed (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying, A^atajozaEu A_ino nafosN A^ataAhaA HimaAmuhaA fahal~aA A@l~atiY Eano bayoni janobayoka tadofaEu [ Art thou impatient if the decreed event of death befall a soul? but why wilt not thou repel from, i. e. defend, that which is between thy two sides? ]; (Mughnee, K;) the meaning being, tadofaEu Eani A@l~atiY bayona janobayoka ; (IJ, Mughnee;) En being suppressed before the conjunct noun [ AltY ], and added after it. (Mughnee, K.) And sometimes it is redundant without compensation, when conjoined with a pronoun: AZ says that the Arabs make Eanoka redundant in the phrase xu*o *aA Eanoka [meaning Take thou, or receive thou, this ]: (TA:) [but xu*o Eanoka is expl. in the S and L, in art. Ax* , as meaning xu*o maA A^aquwlu wadaEo Eanoka Al$~ak~a waAlmiraA='a : see 1 in art. Ax* :] and Aunofu*o Eanoka , occurring in a trad., is expl. as meaning daEohu [i. e. Leave thou it ]: (TA:) or this means go thou from thy place; pass thou from it. (L in art. nf* .) [See also the last ex. in this paragraph.] -A3- The second manner of using it is, as a particle of the kind called maSodariY~N , [combining with an aor. following it to form an equivalent to an inf. n.,] as is done by the tribe of Temeem, (Mughnee, K, *) in what is termed their EanoEanap : (K: [see R. Q. 1:]) they use it in the place of A^ano ; (S, Mughnee;) saying, A^aEojabaniY Eano tafoEala , (Mughnee, K,) for A^ano tafoEala [meaning Thy doing such a thing pleased me ]. (Mughnee.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, A^aEano taras~amota mino xaroqaA='a manozilapF maA='u AlS~abaAbapi mino Eayonayoka masojuwmu [ Is thy having looked upon the traces of a place of abiding of thy beloved Kharkà the cause that the water of excessive love is shed from thine eyes? ]. (S, Mughnee.) And thus they do in the case of A^an~a ; saying, muHam~adFA rasuwlu A@ll~`hi ↓ A^a$ohadu Ean~a [ I acknowledge, or declare, or testify, that Mohammad is the apostle of God ]. (Mughnee.) -A4- The third manner of using it is, as a noun, in the sense of jaAnib , (Mughnee, K, *) or naAHiyap : (S:) and this is said to be in three cases. (Mughnee.) ― -b2- (1) It is when mino is prefixed to it; and this is of frequent occurrence: (Mughnee:) as in the saying, walaqado A^araAniY lilr~imaAHa dariyoy^apF mino Eano yamiyniY mar~apF waA^amaAmiY [ And verily I see me to be like a ring for the spears to be aimed at, from the side of my right hand at one time, and from before me at another time]: (Mughnee, K: *) and in the saying, jiy^otu mino Eano yamiynihi I came from the side of his right hand. (S.) In the opinion of Ibn-Málik, mino prefixed to Eano is redundant; but accord. to others, it is used [as expl. above,] to denote the beginning of a space between two limits: these say that qaEadotu Eano yamiynihi means fiY jaAnibi yamiynihi [i. e. I sat in the side of his right hand ], either closely or otherwise; but if you say mino [before Eano ], the sitting is particularized as being close to the first part of the lateral space. (Mughnee.) ― -b3- (2) It is also when EalaY is prefixed to it: (Mughnee:) thus in the saying, EalaY Eano yamiyniY mar~ati AlT~ayoru sun~aHaA [ On, or over, the side of my right hand, the birds passed along turning the right side towards me, or turning the left side towards me; the last word being a pl., accord. to analogy, of saAniHN , which is used in two opposite senses]: (Mughnee, K:) but this usage is extraordinary; no other instance of it than that here cited having been preserved. (Mughnee.) ― -b4- (3) It is also when what is governed by it in the gen. case and the agent of the verb in connection with it are two pronouns having one application: so says Akh: as in the saying of Imra-el-Keys, daEo Eanoka nahobFA SiyHa fiY HajaraAtihi [or fadaEo Eanoka : see the entire verse cited and expl. in art. Hjr ]: but it is shown to be not a noun in such a case by this, that jaAnib may not take its place [unless used in a tropical sense]. (Mughnee. [See what has been said above, that Eanoka in a phrase of this kind is held to be redundant.])

And A^aToEamotuhu Eano juwEK [ I fed him so as to free him from hunger ]; (S, Msb;) making hunger to be quitted, and passed from: (S, * Msb:) and in this case, mino is used in its place, (S, TA,) as in the Kur cvi. 3; (TA;) or the meaning in this instance is, because of hunger. (Jel.) And jalasotu Eano yamiynihi , [as though] meaning I sat passing away from the place of his right side, in sitting, to another place [ adjacent thereto: but see another explanation near the end of the paragraph]. (Msb.) And AinoSarifo Ean~iY and tanaH~a Ean~iY [ Turn thou, or go thou, away, or aside, from me ]. (TA.) And A^axa*otu AlEiloma Eanohu I understood, or became acquainted with, [or acquired, ] knowledge, or science, from him; as though the understanding passed from him. (Msb.) [And similar to this is the phrase rawaY Eano fulaAnK , for which Eano fulaAnK alone (the verb being understood) is often used, He related a tradition or traditions &c. as learned, or heard, or received, from such a one, or on the authority of such a one. In many other phrases also, some of which will be mentioned in treating of Eano as syn. with mino , the former of these two prepositions is to be, or may be, expl. as denoting transition. For ex., one says, dafaEa Eanohu and daAfaEa He repelled from him; and hence, he defended him: (see art. dfE :) and ramaY Eanohumo He shot in defence of them: (see an ex. in a verse cited voce maEobuwlN :) and Eanohu is sometimes used for difaAEFA Eanohu ; as in the phrase qaAtalotu Eanohu I fought in defence of him; i. e., repelling from him. But the instances of this and other usages of Eano , exclusive of those mentioned in this paragraph, depending upon verbs or part. ns. expressed or obviously understood, are far too numerous to be here collected: many of these will be found among the explanations of words with which they occur.] ― -b3- (2) It denotes a compensation; or something given, or received, or put, or done, instead, or in lieu, of another thing. (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying [in the Kur ii. 45], wa A@t~aquwA yawomFA laA tajoziY nafosN Eano nafosK $ayoy^FA [ And fear ye a day wherein a soul shall not give anything as a satisfaction for a soul, i. e. for another soul: or shall not make satisfaction for a soul at all; accord. to the latter rendering, $yy^A being put in the accus. case after the manner of an inf. n.]. (Mughnee, K. *) And in the saying in a trad., SuwmiY Eano A^um~iki [ Fast thou for, or in lieu of, thy mother ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b4- (3) It denotes superiority ( AlAisotiEolaA=' [as used tropically]); (Mughnee, K;) i. e. as syn. with EalaY . (Mughnee.) Thus in the saying of Dhu-l-Isba' El-'Adwánee, laAhi A@bonu Eam~ika laA A^afoDalota fiY HasabK Ean~iY walaA A^anota day~aAniY fataxozuwaniY (S, Mughnee,) i. e. To God be attributed the excellence of the son of thy paternal uncle (the meaning being lil~`hi dar~u A@boni Eam~ika ), thou hast not become possessed of superiority, in grounds of pretension to respect or honour, above me, or over me, ( EalaY~a ,) nor art thou my governor that thou shouldst rule me; for the well-known mode is to say A^afoDalotu Ealayohi . (Mughnee.) [Thus too in the phrases taEaZ~ama Eanohu and taEaAZama Eanohu (expl. in art. EZm ), and in the phrase tajaAl~a Eanohu (expl. in art. jl ), and the like.] And thus it has been said to be used in the phrase [in the Kur xxxviii. 31], A_in~iY A^aHobabotu Hub~a A@loxayori Eano *ikori rab~iY , meaning qad~amotuhu Ealayohi [i. e. Verily I have preferred the love of good things above, or to, the remembrance, or praise, of my Lord ]: but it is also said that it is here used in its proper manner, as dependent upon a denotative of state suppressed; the meaning being, munoSarifFA Eano *ikori rab~iY [i. e. turning away from the remembrance, &c.]: and AO is related to have said that A^aHobabotu is from A^aHab~a , AlbaEiyru , signifying “ the camel lay down and did not become roused; ” and that the meaning is, I have become withheld by the love of good things from the remembrance, &c. (Mughnee.) And it is [said to be] used as denoting superiority or the like in the saying [in the Kur xlvii. last verse], faA_in~amaA yaboxalu Eano nfosihi [as though the meaning were He is niggardly only to himself ( EalaY nafosihi , for EalaY is considered in this case as importing an ideal superiority); but the phrase may be better rendered, agreeably with the proper, or primary, signification of Eano , he withholds, with niggardliness, only from himself; as is indicated by Bd]. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b5- (4) It denotes a cause. (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying [in the Kur ix. 115], wamaA kaAna A@sotigofaAru A_ibor`hiyma liA^abiyhi A_il~aA Eano mawoEidapK [ And Abraham's begging forgiveness for his father was not otherwise than because of a promise ]. (Mughnee, K.) And thus in the saying [in the Kur xi. 56], wamaA naHonu bitaArikiY A=lihatinaA Eano qawolika [ And we are not, or will not be, relinquishers of our gods because of thy saying ]: or the meaning may be, we do not, or will not, relinquish our gods, turning away ( SaAdiriyna , as a denotative of state relating to the pronoun [implied] in tArkY ,) from thy saying; and this is the opinion of Z. (Mughnee.) [See also an ex. voce danodana , last sentence.] ― -b6- (5) It is syn. with baEoda . (S, Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying [in the Kur xxiii. 42], Eam~aA qaliylK layuSobiHun~a naAdimiyna , (Mughnee, K,) meaning baEoda qaliylK [i. e. After a little while, they will assuredly become repentant ]. (TA.) And in the phrase [in the Kur lxxxiv. 19], latarokabun~a TabaqFA Eano TabaqK [expl. in art. Tbq ], meaning HaAlapF baEoda HaAlapK . (Mughnee.) And in the saying, wamanohalK waradotuhu Eano manohalK [ And to many a watering-place have I come after a watering-place ]. (Mughnee.) And in the saying of El-Hárith Ibn-'Obád, qar~ibaA marobaTa Aln~aEaAmapi min~iY laqiHato Harobu wAy^ilK Eano HiyaAli (S, * TA,) meaning baEoda HiyaAlK [i. e. Make ye two to be near to me the place of the tying of En-Na'ámeh (the name of a horse of the poet): the war of Wáïl has become pregnant after failing to be pregnant during a year, or years ]. (TA.) And in the saying of Et-Tirimmáh, sayaEolamu kul~uhumo A^an~iY musin~N ↓ A_i*aA dafaEuwA EinaAnFA Eano EinaAni i. e. [ All of them shall know that I am of full age, when they press forward ] heat after heat. (TA.) ― -b7- (6) It denotes the meaning of the preposition fiY . (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying, walaA taku Eano Hamoli Alr~ibaAEapi waAniyaA [ And be not thou remiss in bearing the responsibility of the obligation that thou takest upon thyself ]; as is shown by the phrase, [in the Kur xx. 44], walaA taniyaA fiY *ikoriY : (Mughnee, K:) so it is said; but it seems that the meaning of wanaY Eano ka*aA is, “ he passed from such a thing, not entering upon it; ” and wanaY fiyhi , “ he entered upon it but was remiss, or languid: ” by Alr~ibaAEap is meant the payment of a bloodwit or the like. (Mughnee.) ― -b8- (7) It is syn. with mino . (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying [in the Kur xlii. 24], wahuwa A@l~a*iY yaqobalu A@lt~awobapa Eano EibaAdihi [ And He is he who accepts repentance from his servants ]. (AO, Mughnee, K.) Az mentions among the cases in which there is a difference between mino and Eano , that the former has adjoined to it a noun signifying what is near; and the latter, [one signifying] what is remote; as in one's saying samiEotu mino fulaAnK HadiyvFA [ I heard from such a one a narrative ], and Had~avaniY Eano fulaAnK HadiyvFA [ He related to me a narrative from such a one, a phrase similar to rawaY Eano fulaAnK , mentioned among exs. of the first meaning of En ]: accord. to As, one says, Had~avaniY fulaAnN mino fulaAnK , meaning Eanohu [i. e. Such a one related to me from such a one ]; and lahiytu mino fulaAnK and Eanohu [ I became diverted from such a one so as to forget him ]: accord. to Ks, one says lahiytu Eanohu only: and Eanoka jaA='a h`*aA as meaning minoka [i. e. From thee came this ]. (TA.) ― -b9- (8) It is syn. with bi . (Mughnee, K.) Thus [it is said to be used] in the phrase [in the Kur liii. 3], wamaA yanoTiqu Eani A@lohawaY [ Nor does he speak with the desire of self-gratification ]: (Mughnee, K:) but it seems that it is here used in its proper [or primary] sense; and that the meaning is, wamaA yaSoduru qawoluhu Eano hawFY [ nor does his speech proceed from desire of self-gratification; so the phrase may be well rendered, nor does he speak from the desire &c.]. (Mughnee.) One says also, A^ajaAbuwA Eano bawaA='K waAHidK , meaning bijawaAbK waAHidK [i. e. They replied with one reply ]. (T, S, O, K, all in art, bwA^ .) And jaAw^uwA Eano A=xirihimo [ They came with the last of them; Eano being here syn. with bi ; meaning they came all, without exception ]. (A in art. Axr .) [And in like manner, qataluwhumo Eano A=xirihimo They slew them with the last of them; meaning they slew them all, without exception. ] ― -b10- (9) It denotes the using a thing as an aid or instrument. (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying, ramayotu Eani Alqawosi [ I shot with, or by means of, the bow ], accord. to Ibn-Málik; (Mughnee, K;) because one says also, ramayotu biAlqawosi ; both mentioned by Fr. (Mughnee.) [Another explanation of this phrase has been mentioned before.] ― -b11- (10) It is redundant, to compensate for another [ En ] suppressed (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the saying, A^atajozaEu A_ino nafosN A^ataAhaA HimaAmuhaA fahal~aA A@l~atiY Eano bayoni janobayoka tadofaEu [ Art thou impatient if the decreed event of death befall a soul? but why wilt not thou repel from, i. e. defend, that which is between thy two sides? ]; (Mughnee, K;) the meaning being, tadofaEu Eani A@l~atiY bayona janobayoka ; (IJ, Mughnee;) En being suppressed before the conjunct noun [ AltY ], and added after it. (Mughnee, K.) And sometimes it is redundant without compensation, when conjoined with a pronoun: AZ says that the Arabs make Eanoka redundant in the phrase xu*o *aA Eanoka [meaning Take thou, or receive thou, this ]: (TA:) [but xu*o Eanoka is expl. in the S and L, in art. Ax* , as meaning xu*o maA A^aquwlu wadaEo Eanoka Al$~ak~a waAlmiraA='a : see 1 in art. Ax* :] and Aunofu*o Eanoka , occurring in a trad., is expl. as meaning daEohu [i. e. Leave thou it ]: (TA:) or this means go thou from thy place; pass thou from it. (L in art. nf* .) [See also the last ex. in this paragraph.] -A3- The second manner of using it is, as a particle of the kind called maSodariY~N , [combining with an aor. following it to form an equivalent to an inf. n.,] as is done by the tribe of Temeem, (Mughnee, K, *) in what is termed their EanoEanap : (K: [see R. Q. 1:]) they use it in the place of A^ano ; (S, Mughnee;) saying, A^aEojabaniY Eano tafoEala , (Mughnee, K,) for A^ano tafoEala [meaning Thy doing such a thing pleased me ]. (Mughnee.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, A^aEano taras~amota mino xaroqaA='a manozilapF maA='u AlS~abaAbapi mino Eayonayoka masojuwmu [ Is thy having looked upon the traces of a place of abiding of thy beloved Kharkà the cause that the water of excessive love is shed from thine eyes? ]. (S, Mughnee.) And thus they do in the case of A^an~a ; saying, muHam~adFA rasuwlu A@ll~`hi ↓ A^a$ohadu Ean~a [ I acknowledge, or declare, or testify, that Mohammad is the apostle of God ]. (Mughnee.) -A4- The third manner of using it is, as a noun, in the sense of jaAnib , (Mughnee, K, *) or naAHiyap : (S:) and this is said to be in three cases. (Mughnee.) ― -b2- (1) It is when mino is prefixed to it; and this is of frequent occurrence: (Mughnee:) as in the saying, walaqado A^araAniY lilr~imaAHa dariyoy^apF mino Eano yamiyniY mar~apF waA^amaAmiY [ And verily I see me to be like a ring for the spears to be aimed at, from the side of my right hand at one time, and from before me at another time]: (Mughnee, K: *) and in the saying, jiy^otu mino Eano yamiynihi I came from the side of his right hand. (S.) In the opinion of Ibn-Málik, mino prefixed to Eano is redundant; but accord. to others, it is used [as expl. above,] to denote the beginning of a space between two limits: these say that qaEadotu Eano yamiynihi means fiY jaAnibi yamiynihi [i. e. I sat in the side of his right hand ], either closely or otherwise; but if you say mino [before Eano ], the sitting is particularized as being close to the first part of the lateral space. (Mughnee.) ― -b3- (2) It is also when EalaY is prefixed to it: (Mughnee:) thus in the saying, EalaY Eano yamiyniY mar~ati AlT~ayoru sun~aHaA [ On, or over, the side of my right hand, the birds passed along turning the right side towards me, or turning the left side towards me; the last word being a pl., accord. to analogy, of saAniHN , which is used in two opposite senses]: (Mughnee, K:) but this usage is extraordinary; no other instance of it than that here cited having been preserved. (Mughnee.) ― -b4- (3) It is also when what is governed by it in the gen. case and the agent of the verb in connection with it are two pronouns having one application: so says Akh: as in the saying of Imra-el-Keys, daEo Eanoka nahobFA SiyHa fiY HajaraAtihi [or fadaEo Eanoka : see the entire verse cited and expl. in art. Hjr ]: but it is shown to be not a noun in such a case by this, that jaAnib may not take its place [unless used in a tropical sense]. (Mughnee. [See what has been said above, that Eanoka in a phrase of this kind is held to be redundant.])

definition: The presenting, or opposing, oneself, with meddling, or impertinent, speech;
sourceDefinition: The presenting, or opposing, oneself, with meddling, or impertinent, speech; with speech respecting that which does not concern him; (Msb, TA;) as also ↓ Ean~apN , with fet-h, (Msb,) or ↓ Ein~apN , with kesr. (TA.) ― -b2- A^aEoTayotuhu Eayona Eun~apK , (S,) or Eayona Eun~apa , imperfectly decl., and sometimes Eayona Eun~apK , (K,) means I gave to him distinguishing him particularly from among his companions: (S, K:) from AlEan~u signifying “ the presenting, or opposing, oneself. ” (TA.) And one says, raA^ayotuhu Eayona Eun~apK (S) or Eun~apa (K) I saw him just now, (S, K, TA,) presenting, or opposing, himself, (TA,) without my seeking him. (S, TA.) And A^aEonanotu biEun~apK maA A^adoriY maA hiYa : see 4. (S, K.) -A2- It is also the subst. from Eun~ina Eani A@moraA^atihi [i. e. a subst. signifying The state of being pronounced by the judge to be incapacitated from going in to his wife, or to have no desire for his wife: or of being withheld from her by enchantment, or fascination ]: (S, Msb, * K:) or incapacity to go in to women: (Mgh, Msb:) or undesirousness of women: (Msb:) a word used in this sense by the lawyers; (Mgh, Msb;) who say, bihi Eun~apN : (Msb:) but it is declared to be a low word, not allowable; (Mgh, Msb;) instead of which one should say ↓ taEoniynN , (Mgh,) or, accord. to Th and others, ↓ EananN , and ↓ Ein~iynapN , and accord. to the Bári', ↓ EanaAnapN : (Msb:) [i. e.] ↓ Ein~iynapN signifies undesirousness of women: (S:) or, as also ↓ EiniynapN , and ↓ EanaAnapN , and ↓ taEoniynN , and ↓ taEoniynapN , (K,) and ↓ Ein~iyniy~apN , (TA,) it signifies thus, or non-performance of the act of going in to women, by reason of impotence. (K, TA.) -A3- Also An enclosure (S, Mgh, Msb, K) made of wood, (S, Msb, K, TA,) or of trees, (TA,) for camels, (S, Mgh, K, *) or for camels and horses, (Msb,) or for camels and sheep or goats, to be confined therein: (TA:) or an enclosure at the door of a man, in which are his camels and his sheep or goats: (Th, TA:) pl. EunanN (S, K) and EinaAnN . (K.) laA yajotamiEu A@vonaAni fiY Eun~apK [ Two (app. meaning stallion-camels) will not be together in an enclosure for camels ] is one of their sayings. (TA.) And one says, kA@lomuhad~iri fiY AlEun~api Like the brayer (meaning the braying stallion-camel) in the enclosure of trees, in which the stallion-camel is sometimes confined to prevent him from covering; such a stallion being hence termed ↓ mEan~FY , originally ↓ muEan~anN : (Meyd:) it is a prov., applied to a man (Meyd, TA, and S and A and K in art. hdr ) raising a cry and clamour, (S, K,) or threatening, (TA,) who does not make his saying, or action, to have effect; (S, * Meyd, K;) like the camel that is so confined, prevented from covering, and brays. (S, K.) ― -b2- It is also said, by El-Bushtee and in the K, to signify A rope; and in a verse of El-Aashà, in which he mentions flesh-meat as put upon the Eunan , this last word has been expl. as meaning ropes which are stretched, and upon which is thrown the flesh-meat that is cut into strips, or oblong pieces, and dried in the sun: but Az says that the right meaning is, the enclosures for camels; that he had seen such enclosures in the desert, thus called because facing the direction whence blows the north wind, to protect the camels from the cold of that wind; and that he had seen the people spread the flesh-meat cut into strips, or oblong pieces, and dried in the sun, upon them: he thinks that the word was expl. as meaning ropes by one who had seen the poor of the sacred territory extending ropes in Minè, and putting upon them the flesh of the victims of sacrifice that had been given to them. (TA.) ― -b3- Also A booth by means of which one shades himself, made of panic grass ( vumaAm ) or [probably a mistake for and ] branches of trees. (IB, TA.) ― -b4- And Reeds, or plants or herbage, which a man collects, to give, as fodder, to his sheep or goats: one says, jaA='a biEun~apK EaZiymapK [ He came with, or brought, a great collection of reeds, &c.]. (TA.) And one says, kun~aA fiY Eun~apK mina AlkalaA^i , and gun~apK , and vun~api , i. e. We were in abundant herbage. (TA.) -A4- Also The diqodaAn (thus [correctly, as will be shown by an explanation in what follows, confirmed by an ex. from a poet,] in more than one of the copies of the K, in the CK daqodAn , in the copy of the K followed in the TA wqdAn , and in the L rqdAn ,) of the cooking-pot: (K, TA:) MF read wqdAn , and conjecturally, and from analogy, supposed it [to be waqadaAn and] to mean galayaAn ; but the word is arabicized from the Pers. dykdAn , [correctly dyGdAn , pronounced dēgdān, ] a name for the thing upon which the cooking-pot is set up; and thus it [i. e. Eun~apN ] is expl. in the M and other lexicons [among which may be mentioned the L]: hence the saying of a poet, Eafato gayora A^anoA='K wamanoSabi Eun~apK waA^woraqa mino taHoti AlxaSaASapi haAmidi [ It (the dAr , or place of abode,) was effaced, save trenches dug around the tents to keep off the torrent, and the place of the setting-up of the support of the cooking-pot, and ashes beneath the space between the three stones that formed that support, in a state of extinction ]. (TA.)

EunanN (S, K) and EinaAnN . (K.) laA yajotamiEu A@vonaAni fiY Eun~apK [ Two (app. meaning stallion-camels) will not be together in an enclosure for camels ] is one of their sayings. (TA.) And one says, kA@lomuhad~iri fiY AlEun~api Like the brayer (meaning the braying stallion-camel) in the enclosure of trees, in which the stallion-camel is sometimes confined to prevent him from covering; such a stallion being hence termed ↓ mEan~FY , originally ↓ muEan~anN : (Meyd:) it is a prov., applied to a man (Meyd, TA, and S and A and K in art. hdr ) raising a cry and clamour, (S, K,) or threatening, (TA,) who does not make his saying, or action, to have effect; (S, * Meyd, K;) like the camel that is so confined, prevented from covering, and brays. (S, K.) ― -b2- It is also said, by El-Bushtee and in the K, to signify A rope; and in a verse of El-Aashà, in which he mentions flesh-meat as put upon the Eunan , this last word has been expl. as meaning ropes which are stretched, and upon which is thrown the flesh-meat that is cut into strips, or oblong pieces, and dried in the sun: but Az says that the right meaning is, the enclosures for camels; that he had seen such enclosures in the desert, thus called because facing the direction whence blows the north wind, to protect the camels from the cold of that wind; and that he had seen the people spread the flesh-meat cut into strips, or oblong pieces, and dried in the sun, upon them: he thinks that the word was expl. as meaning ropes by one who had seen the poor of the sacred territory extending ropes in Minè, and putting upon them the flesh of the victims of sacrifice that had been given to them. (TA.) ― -b3- Also A booth by means of which one shades himself, made of panic grass ( vumaAm ) or [probably a mistake for and ] branches of trees. (IB, TA.) ― -b4- And Reeds, or plants or herbage, which a man collects, to give, as fodder, to his sheep or goats: one says, jaA='a biEun~apK EaZiymapK [ He came with, or brought, a great collection of reeds, &c.]. (TA.) And one says, kun~aA fiY Eun~apK mina AlkalaA^i , and gun~apK , and vun~api , i. e. We were in abundant herbage. (TA.) -A4- Also The diqodaAn (thus [correctly, as will be shown by an explanation in what follows, confirmed by an ex. from a poet,] in more than one of the copies of the K, in the CK daqodAn , in the copy of the K followed in the TA wqdAn , and in the L rqdAn ,) of the cooking-pot: (K, TA:) MF read wqdAn , and conjecturally, and from analogy, supposed it [to be waqadaAn and] to mean galayaAn ; but the word is arabicized from the Pers. dykdAn , [correctly dyGdAn , pronounced dēgdān, ] a name for the thing upon which the cooking-pot is set up; and thus it [i. e. Eun~apN ] is expl. in the M and other lexicons [among which may be mentioned the L]: hence the saying of a poet, Eafato gayora A^anoA='K wamanoSabi Eun~apK waA^woraqa mino taHoti AlxaSaASapi haAmidi [ It (the dAr , or place of abode,) was effaced, save trenches dug around the tents to keep off the torrent, and the place of the setting-up of the support of the cooking-pot, and ashes beneath the space between the three stones that formed that support, in a state of extinction ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: is a subst. [as well as an inf. n.] of Ean~a ; (Msb, K, TA;) [as such,] i. q. AiEotiraADN [used as a simple subst., meaning Opposition ]; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ EinaAnN : (K, TA:) or opposition of oneself to another, from either side of him, with an abominable, or evil, action. (Msb.) El-Hárith Ibn-Hillizeh says, EananFA baATilFA waZulomFA kamaA yuEo taru Eano Hujorapi Alr~abiyDi AlZ~ibaA='u (TA,) meaning In wrong opposition, ( AiEotiraADFA baATilFA ), [ and injurious conduct ], like as when gazelles are sacrificed [in fulfilment of a vow] for what is due on the part of the flock of sheep, or herd of goats. (EM p. 281.) And it is said in a trad., bariy^onaA A_ilayoka mina Alwavani wAlEanani i. e. [ We are clear, to thee, ] of the idol ( AlS~anam ) and opposition ( AlAiEotiraAD ); as though saying, of associating another with God and of wrongdoing: or, as some say, the meaning [of the last word] in this case is disagreement, or opposition, or contravention, ( AlxilaAf ), and that which is wrong ( AlbaATil ). (TA.) And in another trad., dahimatohu Almaniy~apu fiY Eanani jimaAHihi [ Death came upon him suddenly in the opposition of his heedless, or inconsiderate, course ]. (TA. [There expl. only by the words huwa maA layosa biqaSodK .]) And one says, huwa laka bayona AlA^awobi waAlEanani , meaning [ He is to thee in a state] between obedience and disobedience. (TA.) ↓ warohaA='u AlEinaAni , a phrase used by a poet, means [A woman foolish in ] opposing herself, or intervening, in every discourse. (TA.) And AlEananu signifies also [particularly] Death's opposing itself, and preceding: (TA, JM:) occurring in a trad. of Sateeh [the Diviner]. (TA.) ― -b2- See also EinaAnN , near the middle of the paragraph. ― -b3- Also The place in which a person, or thing, presents, or opposes, himself, or itself. (TA.) ― -b4- See also A^aEonaAnN . -A2- And see Eun~apN , former half.

(TA.)

sourceDefinition: : see EananN , in two places. ― -b2- Also an inf. n. of 3 [q. v.]. (TA.) -A2- And A certain appertenance of a horse or the like; (S, Msb;) [i. e. the rein; ] the strap of the bridle, by means of which the horse, or similar beast, is withheld: (K:) [said to be] so called because it lies over against the mouth, not entering into it, (Msb,) or because its two straps lie over against the two sides of the neck of the beast, on the right and left: (TA:) pl. A^aEin~apN (S, Msb, K) and EununN , (K,) or, accord. to Sb, the former only. (TA.) [Sometimes it may be rendered The bridle; as in the first of the following phrases.] vanayotu EalaY Alfarasi EinaAnahu I put upon the horse his bridle. (TA.) farasN qaSiyru AlEinaAni [ A horse short in the rein ] implies discommendation, as denoting shortness of the neck: [but] huwa qaSiyru AlEinaAni [said of a man] means qliylu Alxayori [i. e. (assumed tropical:) He is one possessing little, or no, good; or few, or no, good things; or little, or no, goodness ]: and A_in~ahu laTawiylu AlEinaAni [lit. Verily he is one whose rein is long ] means, (assumed tropical:) an exalted person; of great chiefdom, or eminence. (TA.) rajulN Tarifu AlEinaAni (S, * K, TA, TK, in one of my copies of the S Tarfu , and in the other Trafu , and in copies of the K Taroqu , [but correctly Tarif , q. v., like katif , as is said in the TK,]) means (tropical:) A man light, or active. (S, K, TA.) fulaAnN A^abiY~u AlEinaAni (assumed tropical:) Such a one is one who refuses the rein. (TA.) *uw AlEinaAni applied to the horse means (assumed tropical:) The tractable, or submissive. (TA.) And *al~a EinaAnu fulaAnK (assumed tropical:) Such a one became submissive. (TA.) Abog mino EinaAnihi [in which the first word is written in my original thus, but it has been altered by the copyist, and I doubt not that it is correctly A^aroxi , the phrase, reading thus, being well known, i. e. Slacken thou his rein, ] means (assumed tropical:) ease thou him, or relieve him. (TA.) Aivoni EalaY~a EinaAnahu means Turn thou back [or bend thou ] towards me his rein. (TA.) jaA=' vaAniyFA fiY EinaAnihi [thus in my original, but correctly mino EnAnh , as in the S in art. vnY , i. e. He came bending a part of his rein, turning from his course,] means (assumed tropical:) he [ came having ] accomplished the object of his want. (TA.) malaA^a EinaAna daAb~atihi (assumed tropical:) He made, or urged, his beast to run vehemently. (TA.) And [hence, app.,] AimotalaA^a EinaAnuhu (assumed tropical:) The utmost of his power, or ability, was accomplished. (TA.) humaA yajoriyaAni fiY EinaAnK (assumed tropical:) They two are equal in excellence or otherwise. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) A heat; or single run to a goal, or limit: one says, jaraY Alfarasu EinaAnFA (assumed tropical:) The horse ran a heat: and kabaA fiY EinaAnihi (assumed tropical:) He stumbled in his heat. (TA.) See also an ex., in a verse of Et- Tirimmáh, voce Eano , in the middle of the paragraph. And ↓ EananN signifies the same, i. e. A heat of a beast: and also the beginning of speech: whence the prov., muEotariDN liEananK lamo yaEonihi meaning (assumed tropical:) Addressing himself to that which is not of his business ( maA layosa mino $aA^onihi ). (Meyd.) ― -b3- And A long rope or cord. (TA.) ― -b4- And AlEinaAnu signifies Habolu Almatoni [ The cord of the portion of the back along which extends the spine; app. meaning the spinal cord, also called medulla spinalis, considered as a single cord]: (K:) [but this consists of two lateral cords, connected together: and therefore, app., it is said that] EinaAnaA Almatoni signifies HabolaAhu [ the two cords of the maton ]. (S.) -A3- $irokapu AlEinaAni is The copartnership of two persons in one particular thing, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) exclusive of the rest of the articles of property of either: (S, Msb, * K:) as though a thing presented itself to them ( Ean~a lahumaA , S, Mgh, Msb) and they bought it (S) and they then became copartners in it: (S, Mgh, Msb:) so says ISk: (Mgh:) or it is from the EinaAn of the horse, because each assigns to his companion the EnAn of the free management of part of the property: (Mgh, Msb:) or because it is allowable for them to differ, like as does the EnAn in the hand of the rider when pulled and when slackened: (Mgh:) or, accord. to Az, it is the case in which each of the two copartners produces deenárs or dirhems, which they mix together, and each gives permission to the other to traffic therewith: and the lawyers differ not in respect of its being lawful; if they gain upon the two sums, the gain being between them; and if they lose, the loss being on the head of each of them [equally]: the partnership of two persons in everything that is in their possession is called $irokapu AlmufaAwaDapi [q. v.]: (TA:) or it is the case of one's competing with a man in the making of a purchase, and saying to him, “ Make me to be a partner with thee; ” this being before he [the purchaser] becomes entitled to Algalaq , or Algiloq , or AlElq , or AlEalaq : (K: [the last word in this explanation, thus written in four different ways in different copies of the K, following the words qabola A^ano yasotawojiba , I think to be most probably Algalaqa , and to mean irredeemability by the seller, from galiqa Alr~ahonu :]) or it is the case of two persons' being equal in partnership, (Z, Msb, K, TA,) in respect of what they contribute of gold or silver; and is from the EinaAn of the beast; (TA;) because the EnAn of the beast consists of two equal single pieces: (Z, Msb, K, TA:) or it is from AlEinaAn as syn. with ↓ AlmuEaAn~ap , meaning AlmuEaAraDap ; (Msb, TA;) because each of them does like as does the other in respect of his property [that he supplies] and in selling and buying. (TA.) See an ex. in a verse cited in art. $rk , conj. 3. ― -b2- See also EanaAnN , in two places.

definition: and ↓ EaAn~N One who presents, or opposes, himself, with meddling, or impertinent, speech;

sourceDefinition: The sides, quarters, tracts, or regions, of anything: (Yoo, TA:) this is the proper signification: (TA:) [hence,] A^aEonaAnu Als~amaA='i [in one of my copies of the S Als~aHaAbi , but altered from Als~amaA='i ,] means The sides, quarters, tracts, or regions, of the sky: (K:) or the surfaces thereof, and what present themselves to view of the sides, quarters, tracts, or regions, thereof; as though pl. of ↓ Eanano , (S, TA,) or of ↓ Ean~N : (TA:) the vulgar say EinaAnu Als~amaA='i . (S, TA.) ― -b2- And [it is said that] A^aEonaAnu Al$~ayaATiyni means The natural dispositions of the devils. (K.) It is said of camels, in a trad., xuliqato mino A^aEonaAni Al$~ayaATiyni [as though meaning They are created of the natural dispositions of the devils ]: and in another trad., A^aEonaAnu Al$~ayaATiyni occurs as said [app. by Mohammad] in answer to a question respecting camels: [but] accord. to IAth, the meaning seems to be, that, by reason of their many evil affections, they are as though they were from the tracts of the devil in respect of their natural dispositions. (TA.)

definition: An evening-draught;
sourceDefinition: An evening-draught; i. e. a draught, drink, or potation, [and particularly of milk, but also applied to one of water, and of wine, &c., ] that is drunk in the evening, or the last, or latter, part of the day. (S, O, K. [See also SabuwHN .]) See an ex. in a verse of Khuzaz Ibn-Lowdhán cited voce ka*aba . One of the Arabs said to a companion of his, A_ino kunota kaA*ibFA fa$aribota gabuwqFA baAridFA [ If thou be tying, then mayest thou drink a cold evening-draught ]; meaning, may there not be milk for thee, so that thou shalt drink water not mixed with anything; this being called by him gbwq by way of comparison: or meaning, may that be to thee in the place of gbwq . (TA.) And one says, laqaytuhu *aA gabuwqK [lit. I met him at a time of drinking the evening-draught ], meaning, in the evening; a phrase used only adverbially; like *aA SabuwHK : (TA:) and *aAta Algabuwqi [which has a similar meaning]. (T in art. *uw .) ― -b2- Also, and with p , A she-camel whose milk one drinks in the evening: or, accord. to Lh, that is milked after sunset: epithets like SabuwHN and SabuwHapN . (TA.)

definition: signifies The night;
sourceDefinition: signifies The night; (Zj, TA;) and [hence] wamino $ar~i gaAsiqK A_i*aA waqaba (in the Kur [cxiii. 3], S, O) means [ And from the mischief ] of the night when it cometh in; (S, O, K;) accord. to El-Hasan (S, O) El-Basree: (O:) or the beginning of the night; as El-Hasan is related to have said: (TA:) or the night when the $afaq [or redness in the horizon after sunset ] disappears: (S, O, K:) and the night is said to be so called because it is colder than the day: (O, TA:) [for] AlgaAsiqu signifies [also] the cold ( AlbaAridu ) [like AlgasaAqu ] (TA:) or what is meant in the verse of the Kur-án cited above is the accident in the night: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or AlgaAsiqu signifies the moon; (K;) and this is said to be meant in the verse of the Kur-án; (S, TA;) so the Prophet is related to have said to Áïsheh; i. e. the verse means, [ the mischief of ] the moon when it is eclipsed: (Th, O, * TA:) or what is meant in that verse is, Alv~uray~aA [i. e. the asterism called the Pleiades ] when it sets [ aurorally (see vuray~aA )], because diseases and pestilences are frequent at that period. (O, K, TA,) and become removed at that period of its [auroral] rising [in the opposite season of the year], (O, TA,) as is related in a trad. (TA:) or the sun when it sets: or the day when it enters upon the night. or the serpent called AlA^asowad when it smites, or turns over: or, accord. to Sub. Iblees when he suggests evil: (TA:) or, accord. to I'Ab and several others, from the mischief of the *akar when it becomes erect; (K, TA:) a strange explanation: and ↓ Algas~aAqu is like AlgaAsiqu ; [but in what sense or senses is not said;] each is an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant. (TA.) ― -b2- gaAsiqN also signifies Flowing; applied by a poet in this sense to a source, or spring; and having to relation to darkness. (Sh. TA.)

And gal~a signifies also Inivit ( Ha$aA^a , in some copies of the K without the hemzeh,) feminam: (K, TA; in which latter is added wlA ykwn Al~A mn DaxomK [app. meaning that this is not said of any but such as is big, or bulky]:) mentioned by IAar. (TA.) ― -b4- gal~a Ald~uhona fiY raA^osihi He made the oil to enter amid the roots of the hair of his head. (K.) And gal~a $aEarahu biAlT~iybi He made the perfume to enter amid his hair. sourceDefinition: , (K,) inf. n. A_igolaAlN , (TA,) He watered his camels ill, so that they did not satisfy their thirst: (K, TA:) or he brought, or sent, them back from the water without satisfying their thirst: (O, TA:) thus expl. by Az, who says that it is incorrectly mentioned by A'Obeyd, on the authority of AZ, [in this sense,] with the unpointed E . (TA. [But see 4 in art. El .]) ― -b2- And Agl~ signifies also Agtl~t ganamuhu (O, K) [accord. to the TA as meaning His sheep, or goats, thirsted: but this I think doubtful: see 8]. -A2- Agl~ and its aor. and inf. n. as relating to unfaithfulness, see in the latter half of the first paragraph, in five places. -A3- Agl~t AlD~ayoEahu , (Mgh, Msb, K, [in the CK gal~at ,]) and AlD~iyaAEu , (S, O, K,) from Algal~apu , (S, O,) [ The estate, and estates, consisting of land, &c.,] became in the condition of having gal~ap [or proceeds, revenue, or income, accruing from the produce, &c.]: (Mgh, Msb:) or yielded gal~ap : (K, TA:) i. e. yielded somewhat, the source thereof remaining. (TA.) ― -b2- And Agl~ Alqawomu meaning balagato gal~atuhumo [i. e. The gal~ap of the people, or party, arrived; as expl. in the PS and TA; or the people, or party, had their gl~p brought to them ]. (S, O, K.) And The people, or party, became in [or entered upon ] the time of the gal~ap . (TA.) ― -b3- And fulaAnN yugil~u EalaY EiyaAlihi Such a one brings the gal~ap to his family, or household. (S, O.) -A4- Agl~ AlwaAdiY The valley gave growth to what are termed gul~aAn , (S, O, K,) pl. of gaAl~N . (TA.) -A5- Agl~ fiY AlA_ihaAbi , (S, O,) He (a butcher) left some of the flesh sticking in the hide, in stripping it off: (S, O:) or he took some of the flesh and of the fat [ in the hide ] in the skinning: (K:) and AlA_ihaAba ↓ gl~ he left somewhat [ of the flesh, or of the flesh and of the fat, ] remaining in the hide on the occasion of the skinning: a dial. var. of A^agal~a . (TA.) ― -b2- And accord. to AA, AlA_igolaAlu signifies The milking of the she-camel when milk remains [app. afterwards ] in her udder. (O.) [Perhaps the meaning is The leaving some remaining in the udder on the occasion of milking. ] -A6- Agl~ AlxaTiybu The orator, or preacher, said, or spoke, what was not right, or correct. (TA.) -A7- Agl~ baSarahu , (S, O,) or AlbaSara , (K,) He (a man, S, O) looked intensely, or intently. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- See also 1, last sentence. -A8- A_igolaAlN signifies also The making an overt, or open, hostile, or predatory, incursion. (TA.) -A9- And The clothing oneself with, or wearing, a coat of mail. (TA.)

definition: A ring, or collar, of iron, which is put upon the neck: (Msb:) a shackle for the neck or for the hand: [i.
sourceDefinition: A ring, or collar, of iron, which is put upon the neck: (Msb:) a shackle for the neck or for the hand: [i. e. a ring, or collar, for the neck, or a pinion or manacle for the hand: ] (MA:) or a [ shackle of the kind called ] jaAmiEap , (TA, and so in the S and K in art. jmE ,) of iron, (TA,) collecting together the two hands to the neck: (S in art. jmE ; and Jel * in xxxvi. 7:) [sometimes, a shackle for the neck and hands, consisting of two rings, one for the neck and the other for the hands, connected by a bar of iron: (see zam~aArapN :)] and a shackle with which the Arabs used to confine a captive when they took him, made of thongs, upon which was hair, so that sometimes, when it dried, it became infested with lice upon his neck: (TA:) the pl. is A^agolaAlN : (S, O, Msb, K:) which repeatedly occurs in the Kur-án and the Sunneh as meaning (assumed tropical:) difficult tasks and fatiguing works [as being likened to shackles upon the necks]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence] the Arabs apply it metonymically to denote (tropical:) A wife. (TA.) And gul~N qamilN [lit. A lousy shackle for the neck &c.] is an appellation of (assumed tropical:) a woman of evil disposition; originating from the fact that the gul~ used to be of thongs, upon which was hair, so that it became infested with lice. (S.) -A2- Also, and ↓ gul~apN , (S, O, K,) and ↓ galalN , (K,) or this is the inf. n. of gul~a , (S,) [and accord. to analogy of gal~a as originally galila ,] and ↓ galiylN , (S, O, K,) Thirst: or vehement thirst: (K, TA:) or the burning of thirst; (S, O, TA;) little or much: (TA:) or burning of the inside, (K, TA,) from thirst, and from anger and vexation (TA.)

sourceDefinition: Proceeds, revenue, or income, (Mgh, Msb, K, TA, [in the CK, Ald~axalapu is put for Ald~axolu ,]) of any kind, (Mgh, Msb,) accruing from the produce, or yield, of land, (Mgh, Msb, K, TA,) or from the rent thereof, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) [in which sense ↓ magal~N is also used, as a subst., pl. mugal~aAtN ,] or from seed-produce, and from fruits, and from milk, and from hire, and from the increase of cattle, and the like, (TA,) and from the rent of a house, (K, TA,) and from the hire of a slave, (Mgh, K, TA,) and the like; (Mgh, Msb;) [generally meaning corn, or grain; i.e.] wheat and barley and rice and the like; (KL;) the gal~ap of the slave is the payment imposed by the master, and made to him: (TA voce DariybapN :) pl. gal~aAtN (S, O, Msb, TA) and gilaAlN . (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- Also Dirhems [or pieces of money ] that are clipped ( muqaT~aEap ), in a single piece thereof [ the quantity clipped being ] a qiyraAT or a Tas~uwj or a grain; of which it is said in the “ Eedáh, ” that one's lending gal~ap in order to have such as are free from defect returned to him is disapproved: (Mgh:) or dirhems [or pieces of money ] that are rejected by the treasury of the state, but taken by the merchants. (KT. [Freytag has given this latter explanation, but has erroneously assigned it to gul~apN .])

definition: Water amid trees: pl.
sourceDefinition: Water amid trees: pl. A^agolaAlN . (S, O. [See an ex. voce Ea*obN .]) And Water having no current, only appearing a little upon the surface of the earth, disappearing at one time and appearing at another: (AA, S, O:) or, accord. to AHn, a feeble flow of water from the bottom of a valley or water-course, amid trees. (TA.) Aboo-Sa'eed says, laA ya*ohabu kalaAmunaA galalaA [ Our speech shall not pass away as a feeble flow of water ]: meaning that it ought not to be concealed from men, but should be made public. (TA.) -A2- Also A strainer, or clarifier: occur- ring in a verse of Lebeed, cited voce raAziqiY~N : where it means the fidaAm (S, O, TA) on the heads of the A^abaAriyq , (S,) or on the head of the A_iboriyq : (O, TA:) or, as some relate the verse, the word is gulalN , pl. of ↓ gul~apN ; (S, O, TA;) which signifies [the same, i. e.] a piece of rag bound on the head of the Abryq [ to act as a strainer ]. (IAar, TA.) -A3- And The flesh that is left upon the thumb when one skins [ a beast ]. (TA.) -A4- See also gul~N , last sentence. -A5- Also, (O, K,) and ↓ galaAlapN , (O, and so in copies of the K,) or ↓ gulaAlapN , (so in other copies of the K, and accord. to the TA,) A certain disease that attacks sheep, or goats, (O, K, TA,) in the orifice of the teat, occasioned by the milker's not exhausting the udder, but leaving in it some milk, which becomes blood, or coagulates and is mixed with a yellow fluid. (TA.)

(O, TA.)

(TA in art. rtq .) ― -b4- [Hence also A rupture; a hernia; ] a certain malady; a protrusion in the thin, or delicate, and soft part of the belly; (S, O;) a malady in the SifaAq [meaning peritonæum ], consisting in a solution of the integument so that a rent takes place in it, and through this passes a strange body, or substance, that was confined within it before the rent; and there is no cure for it, except for that which happens, rarely, to children: (K:) a disease that befalls a man in his intestines, consisting in a disruption of a place between these and his scrotum, in consequence of which a flatus collects between the two testicles and they become enlarged; in which case one says, A^aSaAbatohu riyHu Alfatoqi : or a severing of the fat [or cellular substance ] that encloses the testicles: in the “ Ghareebáni, ” it is termed ↓ fataq , with fet-h to the t : (Mgh:) and thus it is said to be by Az, and thus it is expl. by him: (O:) or it is a rending of the skin between the scrotum and the lower part of the belly, in consequence of which [ some of ] the intestines fall into the scrotum: (TA:) accord. to Ibráheem El-Harbee, a rupture of the bladder. (O, TA.) ― -b5- [And A rent in the clouds: see 4:] and ↓ fataqN [likewise] signifies a gap of the clouds: pl. futuwqN . (TA.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) An open, and a spacious, place. (O, K.) ― -b7- And A place upon which rain has not fallen when it has fallen upon what is around it; (S, O, K;) and ↓ fataqapN signifies thus, applied to a land: pl. of the former futuwqN . (TA.) [Hence,] EaAmN *uw Alfutuwqi A year of little rain. (TA.) ― -b9- See also 4, last sentence but one, for a meaning of the pl. futuwqN .

(TA.)

definition: Impotent (T, S, M, K) in speech, (T, M, K,) and in adducing an argument;
sourceDefinition: Impotent (T, S, M, K) in speech, (T, M, K,) and in adducing an argument; (T, M;) [as though his mouth were covered with a fidaAm , for it is said in the S to be from fadamotu EalaY fiyhi biAlfidaAmi ;] heavy, sluggish, or dull; (S;) or with heaviness, sluggishness, or dulness, and softness, and paucity of understanding: (M, K:) or unintelligent: (Msb:) and thick; (M, K;) fat; (M;) foolish, or stupid; rough, rude, or uncivil: (M, K:) accord. to IAar, the heavy, sluggish, or dull; as being likened to blood, which is thus called: (T:) and vadomN is a dial. var. thereof, or, accord. to Yaakoob, the v is a substitute for the f : (M:) the fem. is with p : (M, Msb, K:) and the pl. is fidaAmN [agreeably with analogy]. (M, K: in a copy of the T fudum [which I think a mistranscription].) ― -b2- Also Heavy [and app. thick ] blood: and, accord. to IAar, blood [itself]. (T.) ― -b3- And A garment, or piece of cloth, (T, TA,) saturated with dye, (T,) or saturated with red dye by its being put again into the safflower time after time. (TA.) And Red that is saturated (M, K) with redness: (K:) or of which the redness is not intense. (Thus also in some copies of the K.) [See also mufodamN .]

sourceDefinition: and ↓ fadaAmN and ↓ fad~aAmu and ↓ fad~uwmN , (K,) or ↓ fad~aAmN [only], (S, T, M,) A thing which the Persians or other foreigners, (T, K,) and the Magians, (K,) bind upon their mouths on the occasion of their giving to drink; (T, K;) or a piece of cloth with which the Magian binds his mouth; (S;) or a sort of thing with which the Persians or other foreigners wipe [app. the mouth ] when they give to drink; one of which is termed ↓ fad~aAmapN . (TA. [See 2: and see also the first paragraph of art. gm .])
